# x install

Cross-platform installer — query and install software and skills, with interactive selection, CI/CD auto best-match, or structured output for AI agents


::: tip x i is shorthand for x install — identical in every way.
x i bun is the same as x install bun.
:::

::: tip Recommended exploration path:
1. x install --ls — list all recorded software (supports --tsv output)
2. x install — no arguments opens interactive fzf UI to browse all software and skills
3. x install &lt;name&gt; — lists all install methods for the software, pick interactively
4. x install &lt;prefix&gt;/&lt;name&gt; — skip selection with prefix (e.g. brew/jq, best/bun)
:::

::: tip Prefix format: package_manager/software
brew/jq, apt/git, npm/express, pip/httpie, cargo/ripgrep

sys/bun — system package manager

best/jq — auto-select best method

skill/anthropics/pptx — general skill

clawhub/skill-vetter — clawhub.ai platform skill
:::

::: tip Non-interactive install (CI, scripts) with --best, --sys, --withtool:
x install --best bun — auto-select by priority

x install --sys bun — use system package manager

x install --withtool brew bun — use specified package manager

x install --best --priority brew,apt bun — custom priority

All three support batch install and --printcmd (print without executing):

x install --best --printcmd bun vim
:::

::: tip Install skills with skill/ or clawhub/ prefix:
x install skill/anthropics/pptx

x install clawhub/skill-vetter

Skills go to the global environment by default. For version control or project isolation, use x skill: https://x-cmd.com/mod/skill
:::

::: tip AI Agent (Claude Code, OpenClaw, etc.) workflow:
1. x install --search &lt;keyword&gt; — aggregate search across apt, brew, npm, skills.sh, clawhub.ai
2. x install --printinfo &lt;software&gt; — view details and all install methods
3. x install --best --printcmd &lt;software&gt; — preview install command, then execute

Output supports --json, --tsv, --csv.
:::

::: tip AI Agent (Claude Code, OpenClaw, etc.) environment probing:
x install —env — get platform, architecture, distro info

x install --available-tool — list all supported package managers

x install --available-tool --installed — show only installed package managers

Both support --json, --tsv, --csv output.
:::


## Examples

Open interactive UI to search, browse, and install software and skills

```sh
x install
```

Interactively select and install bun and vim

```sh
x install bun vim
```

Install skills from skill/* or clawhub/* format

```sh
x install skill/anthropics/pptx clawhub/skill-vetter
```

Automatically select the best method to install bun

```sh
x install --best bun
```

Install bun with brew as priority, falling back to xpkg

```sh
x install --best --priority brew,xpkg bun
```

Install vim and bun using brew

```sh
x install --withtool brew vim bun
```

Preview the best install command for bun without executing

```sh
x install --best --printcmd bun
```

Preview brew install command for bun without executing

```sh
x install --withtool brew --printcmd bun
```

Print detailed information and all installation methods for bun

```sh
x install --printinfo bun
```

Output bun info in JSON format for AI agents

```sh
x install --printinfo --json bun
```

Search for software and skills across multiple sources

```sh
x install --search ppt
```

Print current system environment info

```sh
x install --env
```

List all software recorded in the install module

```sh
x install --ls
```

List all package managers supported in current environment

```sh
x install --available-tool
```

Update the resource files of x install

```sh
x install --update
```
## introduce



install is a module used to help users quickly install various software. It can help you quickly find the software installation command suitable for the current system and run the installation command to install the software.

This module is designed to simplify the query process of software installation commands, so that you do not have to search for software installation commands in complicated web pages, and reduce the need to switch back and forth between the browser and the development environment, so that you can focus more on development.



## main feature


1. **Simple and clear**: Directly give the installation command and source of the software without adding other redundant information.
2. **Fast**: The installation command is retrieved from the scheduled install resource package rather than through the network. Therefore, you are not limited by network speed.
3. **Comprehensive**: For specified software, as many installation methods as possible will be given to meet different application scenarios as much as possible. At the same time, the install resource package will also be regularly maintained and updated.

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x install --ls](/mod/install/--ls.md) | List all software supported by the install module |
| [x install --fzf](/mod/install/--fzf.md) | Enable the interactive fzf UI for the install module |
| [x install --printinfo](/mod/install/--printinfo.md) | Print detailed information and all installation methods for a software (without executing) |
| [x install --printcmd](/mod/install/--printcmd.md) | Print only the installation commands for a software (without executing) |
| [x install --available-tool](/mod/install/--available-tool.md) | Query available package managers in current environment |
| [x install --run](/mod/install/--run.md) | Run the installation command to install software (interactive selection by default) |
| [x install --best](/mod/install/--best.md) | Automatically select the best installation method based on priority |
| [x install --sys](/mod/install/--sys.md) | Install using the system package manager (brew, apt, dnf, apk, etc.) |
| [x install --withtool](/mod/install/--withtool.md) | Install using a specified package manager |
| [x install --search](/mod/install/--search.md) | [EXPERIMENTAL] Search for software and skills across multiple package sources and skill platforms |
| [x install --env](/mod/install/--env.md) | Print current system environment information |
| [x install --update](/mod/install/--update.md) | Update index information |

# x is

Value checking tool for verifying values meet expected conditions.

Supports batch multi-value checking, returns success only if all pass.


::: tip Best practices:
1. Batch check values: 'x is int 1 2 3 4 5'
2. Check vars unset: 'x is unset VAR1 VAR2'
3. Check file newest: 'x is newest target src/* lib/*'
:::


## Examples

Check integers: batch verify multiple values are integers

```sh
x is int 42 100 -5 0
```

Check floats: batch verify multiple values are floats

```sh
x is float 3.14 -2.5 .5
```

Check positive: batch verify multiple values are ≥0

```sh
x is positive 1 10 100
```

Check negative: batch verify multiple values are &lt;0

```sh
x is negative -1 -10 -100
```

Range check: verify values are within [1,100]

```sh
x is minmax 1 100 50 75
```

Equality: check all values are equal

```sh
x is eq "a" "a" "a"
```

Membership: check value is in candidate list

```sh
x is within "ok" pending success failed
```

Delimited list: check membership in comma-separated list

```sh
x is in "b" "a,b,c,d"
```

IP check: verify values are IPv4 addresses

```sh
x is ip 192.168.1.1 10.0.0.1
```

File age: check if file is newer than wildcard matches

```sh
x is newest build.tar.gz src/*.c lib/*.h
```

File age: check if file is older than wildcard matches

```sh
x is oldest cache.txt /tmp/*.tmp
```

Variable check: verify variables are unset

```sh
x is unset TEMP_VAR1 TEMP_VAR2
```

Interactive: check if running in interactive session

```sh
x is interactive && echo "Interactive" || echo "Script"
```

WSL: check if running in Windows Subsystem for Linux

```sh
x is wsl && echo "In WSL"
```

Termux: check if running in Termux Android terminal

```sh
x is termux && echo "In Termux"
```

Suitability: check if environment supports advise features

```sh
x is suitable_advise_env && x advise enable
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x is int](/mod/is/int.md) | Check if value is integer. Supports batch checking, all must pass |
| [x is float](/mod/is/float.md) | Check if value is float (must contain decimal point). Batch supported |
| [x is positive](/mod/is/positive.md) | Check if value is positive integer (≥0). Supports batch checking |
| [x is negative](/mod/is/negative.md) | Check if value is negative integer (&lt;0). Supports batch checking |
| [x is minmax](/mod/is/minmax.md) | Check if value is in [min,max] range. Format: x is minmax MIN MAX VALUE... |
| [x is eq](/mod/is/eq.md) | Check if multiple values are equal. Reads from stdin if no args |
| [x is within](/mod/is/within.md) | Check if first value is within the following candidate list |
| [x is in](/mod/is/in.md) | Check membership in colon-separated list. Ex: x is in: a a:b:c |
| [x is in-](/mod/is/in-.md) | Check membership in dash-separated list. Ex: x is in- a a-b-c |
| [x is in_](/mod/is/in_.md) | Check membership in underscore-separated list. Ex: x is in_ a a_b_c |
| [x is in](/mod/is/in.md) | Check membership in pipe-separated list. Ex: x is in&#124; a a&#124;b&#124;c |
| [x is ip](/mod/is/ip.md) | Check if value is IPv4 address. Supports batch checking |
| [x is newest](/mod/is/newest.md) | Check if first file is newer than others. Supports wildcards |
| [x is oldest](/mod/is/oldest.md) | Check if first file is older than others. Supports wildcards |
| [x is unset](/mod/is/unset.md) | Check if variable is unset. Supports batch multi-var checking |
| [x is interactive](/mod/is/interactive.md) | Check if current session is interactive (checks PS1 or $- contains i) |
| [x is interactive_tty](/mod/is/interactive_tty.md) | Check if stdin is an interactive TTY ([ -t 0 ]) |
| [x is interactiveshell](/mod/is/interactiveshell.md) | Check if current shell is interactive (checks $- contains i) |
| [x is repl](/mod/is/repl.md) | Check if currently in REPL mode (checks $___X_CMD_REPL) |
| [x is stdout2tty](/mod/is/stdout2tty.md) | Check if stdout is connected to a TTY ([ -t 1 ]) |
| [x is wsl](/mod/is/wsl.md) | Check if running in WSL (checks uname -r and /proc/version) |
| [x is cygwin](/mod/is/cygwin.md) | Check if running in Cygwin (checks OSTYPE and uname -o) |
| [x is msys](/mod/is/msys.md) | Check if running in MSYS/MinGW environment |
| [x is gitbash](/mod/is/gitbash.md) | Check if running in Git Bash (based on MSYS + Git-specific vars) |
| [x is termux](/mod/is/termux.md) | Check if running in Termux (checks PREFIX and /data/data/com.termux) |
| [x is ish](/mod/is/ish.md) | Check if running in iSH (Alpine Linux on iOS) |
| [x is suitable_pkg](/mod/is/suitable_pkg.md) | Check if environment is suitable for package installation |
| [x is suitable_advise_env](/mod/is/suitable_advise_env.md) | Check if environment supports advise (needs interactive+TTY+TERM) |

# x jina

CLI for jina.ai, providing functions to get website content, generate vector data, etc.


::: tip
- Get jina api key: https://jina.ai/embeddings/#apiform
- Interactive env use `x jina init` to initialize configuration. The configure will be saved locally.
- Run command `x jina --cfg apikey=<apikey>` to add access apikey.
:::


## Examples

Retrieve the content of the x-cmd website, returned in Markdown format; this is the short for 'x jina reader https://x-cmd.com'

```sh
x jina https://x-cmd.com
```

Retrieve the content of the x-cmd website, returned in HTML format

```sh
x jina reader --html https://x-cmd.com
```

List all embed model



# x jq

jq is a lightweight JSON processing tool developed by Stephen Dolan in 2012.

`x jq` is an enhancement module based on the jq command, designed to improve the jq user experience. The specific enhancements are as follows:
1. Simplified jq command installation: If jq is not found in the current environment, `x jq` will download and install jq through the x-cmd pkg system in a way that does not affect the user's environment.
2. Provides the `repl` command: This offers an interactive way to read and explore JSON data using fzf.

## Examples

Example: Extract name field from JSON file

```sh
x jq '.name' data.json
```

Example: Iterate over each element in JSON array

```sh
x jq '.items[]' data.json
```

Example: Enable interactive mode to process x ascii output

```sh
x ascii --json | x jq r
```

Example: Enable interactive mode to process test.json

```sh
x jq r test.json
```

Example: Create a new JSON object

```sh
x jq -n '{"key":"value"}'
```

Example: Filter users with age greater than 18

```sh
x jq '.[] | select(.age > 18)' users.json
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x jq open](/mod/jq/open.md) | Open the jqplay.org website in your browser. |
| [x jq repl](/mod/jq/repl.md) | Read and explore JSON data using an interactive JSON viewer |
| [x jq --cmd](/mod/jq/--cmd.md) | Run the jq command directly |

# x keyring

System-level encrypted local note: persist keys / credentials / critical info (API tokens / SSH private keys / DB passwords / TLS certs / service accounts / any sensitive data you don't want plaintext) into the OS-native encrypted credential store (macOS Keychain / Linux SecretService / KWallet / Windows Credential Manager), protected by OS-level security, at-rest encryption on the local machine. Accessible across shells and sessions without .env files or shell history. Namespace defaults to x-cmd-&lt;UID&gt;. For per-access auth / network approval / cross-device sync, use op/bw/vault.


::: tip
Use scope: local + OS-level encryption + at-rest = small encrypted note. Fits: anything you don't want plaintext — API tokens / SSH private keys / DB passwords / recovery codes / TLS client certs / service accounts. Doesn't fit: per-access auth / network approval (`op/bw/vault`) / cross-device sync (iCloud Keychain via `cget/cset/cls`, or a different tool).
:::

::: tip
UID namespace: `--ns` defaults to x-cmd-&lt;UID&gt;. Same-UID scripts overwrite each other (last write wins). For independent slots, give each `--ns` (e.g. `--ns deploy-bot`, `--ns ci-runner`).
:::

::: tip
`set` input: pipe `printf '%s' "$pw" | x keyring set ...` (avoid `echo`, trailing newline); or tty silent prompt. Empty password rejected.
:::

::: tip
Same-UID scripts can dump all your entries: macOS `security find-generic-password -w`, Linux `secret-tool search` + DBus, Windows `CredEnumerate`. x keyring does not block this — OS model is the same on all three. Keep critical entries out of OS keychain; use op/bw/vault for truly sensitive.
:::

::: tip
`lock` / `unlock` is macOS-only; other OS is daemon-managed, no CLI. **Core flow is at-rest encryption; lock/unlock is optional.**
:::


## Examples

Persist: write the token / private key / critical info to keychain entry (github, alice)

```sh
x keyring set github alice
```

Retrieve: $(x keyring get github alice) inside a script reads the secret directly

```sh
x keyring get github alice
```

Scripted: pipe password via stdin to avoid leaving plaintext in shell history

```sh
printf '%s' "$pw" | x keyring set github alice
```

Audit: list what entries I have stored

```sh
x keyring ls
```

Optional: macOS real keychain lock; Linux / Windows are daemon-managed, no-op + note

```sh
x keyring lock
```

iCloud Keychain (macOS): same as `set` but synced to Apple devices

```sh
x keyring cset github alice
```

Backend switch: Linux SecretService / KWallet, macOS Keychain

```sh
x keyring backend set secret_service
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x keyring get](/mod/keyring/get.md) | Retrieve an already-stored password from the keychain |
| [x keyring get_](/mod/keyring/get_.md) | script-friendly get — writes to a variable; for byte-exact round-trip inside scripts |
| [x keyring set](/mod/keyring/set.md) | Write a password to the keychain; namespace defaults to x-cmd-&lt;UID&gt;. Pipe the password via stdin (or tty silent prompt) |
| [x keyring ls](/mod/keyring/ls.md) | List entries (current UID by default); output is service&lt;TAB&gt;namespace |
| [x keyring rm](/mod/keyring/rm.md) | Delete an entry |
| [x keyring lock](/mod/keyring/lock.md) | Optional, macOS real lock; other OS no-op + note |
| [x keyring unlock](/mod/keyring/unlock.md) | Optional, macOS real unlock; other OS no-op + note (daemon-managed) |
| [x keyring cget](/mod/keyring/cget.md) | iCloud Keychain get (macOS-only; `c` = cloud) — bypasses login keychain, syncs across Apple devices |
| [x keyring cget_](/mod/keyring/cget_.md) | script-friendly cget — iCloud Keychain get into a variable; for byte-exact round-trip inside scripts |
| [x keyring cset](/mod/keyring/cset.md) | iCloud Keychain set (macOS-only) — syncs to Apple devices |
| [x keyring cls](/mod/keyring/cls.md) | iCloud Keychain list (macOS-only) |
| [x keyring crm](/mod/keyring/crm.md) | iCloud Keychain delete (macOS-only) |
| [x keyring backend](/mod/keyring/backend.md) | Switch or query the OS backend (keychain / secret_service / kwallet / windows / null) |

# x last

Enhanced `last` command with multiple output formats and filtering.

Shows user login/logout records, system reboots, and session duration.

Supports CSV, JSON, interactive UI, and tree view formats.



In TTY mode, --all and --login use interactive picker for easy selection.

## Examples

Interactive view (TTY default) / CSV format (piped)

```sh
x last
```

Output login records in JSON format

```sh
x last --json
```

Output login records in CSV format

```sh
x last --csv
```

Show only system reboot records

```sh
x last --reboot
```

Tree view of login records (grouped by reboot)

```sh
x last --tree
```

Show only user login records (exclude reboots)

```sh
x last --login
```

## Usage

```sh
x last [FLAGS]
```

## Flags

| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--exec` | Execution mode (default), supports format options |
| `-j`, `--json` | Output in JSON format |
| `-c`, `--csv` | Output in CSV format |
| `--app` | Interactive UI view |
| `-a`, `--all` | All records (with interactive picker in TTY) |
| `--login`, `-l` | Login records only, exclude reboots (with picker in TTY) |
| `--tree` | Tree view (grouped by reboot) |
| `-r`, `--reboot` | Show only reboot records |

# x line

functions for line-oriented situation


::: tip
Most subcommands have a `_` suffix variant that stores result in `x_` variable for scripting (e.g. `join_`, `count_`, `indexof_`).
:::

::: tip
Use `x uni`, `x uno`, `x duo` as shortcuts for `x line uni`, `x line uno`, `x line duo`. These are set operations on lines.
:::

::: tip
The `from` and `split` families use pure shell to avoid external commands. For large strings, prefer `tr` instead.
:::


## Examples

Deduplicate lines (like `sort | uniq` but faster).

```sh
{ seq 1 3; seq 3 1; } | x line uni
```

Join lines with separator.

```sh
seq 5 | x line join ", "
```

Wrap each line with prefix and suffix.

```sh
seq 3 | x line wrap "[" "]"
```

Format each line with printf-style pattern.

```sh
seq 3 | x line prf "item_%s\n"
```

Print each argument on a new line.

```sh
x line prln a b c
```

Group lines in pairs (outputs: pair 1 2, pair 3 4, pair 5 6).

```sh
seq 6 | x line args -n 2 'echo pair $1 $2'
```

Filter out lines matching patterns.

```sh
seq 10 | x line minus 3 5 7
```

Parse colon-separated string into lines.

```sh
x line from "$PATH"
```

Split string by custom separator.

```sh
x line split ";" "a;b;c"
```

Find line number of first match.

```sh
x line indexof pattern file.txt
```

Count lines in files.

```sh
x line count LICENSE .gitignore
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x line uni](/mod/line/uni.md) | Deduplicate lines from stdin, output only the first occurrence of each. Using a set for O(1) lookup, faster than `sort | uniq`. |
| [x line duo](/mod/line/duo.md) | Find and print duplicate lines from stdin, preserving the order of their second appearance. Supports `-f field` to check a specific field and `-s separator` for custom field separator. |
| [x line uno](/mod/line/uno.md) | Find and print unique lines from stdin, preserving the order of their first appearance. |
| [x line join](/mod/line/join.md) | Join all lines from stdin with a specified separator. Supports `--noblank` to skip empty lines, and optional `begin`/`end` to wrap each element. |
| [x line wrap](/mod/line/wrap.md) | Wrap each line from stdin with a prefix and suffix. |
| [x line count](/mod/line/count.md) | Count lines from stdin or files, equivalent to `wc -l` but outputs only the number. |
| [x line prf](/mod/line/prf.md) | Format and print each line from stdin using printf-style format string. |
| [x line prln](/mod/line/prln.md) | Print arguments as separate lines. |
| [x line minus](/mod/line/minus.md) | Filter lines from stdin, removing lines that match specified patterns. |
| [x line args](/mod/line/args.md) | Group lines from stdin into batches of n lines, process each batch with a shell function. |
| [x line arg1](/mod/line/arg1.md) | Process each line from stdin as $1 to a shell function, one line at a time. |
| [x line from](/mod/line/from.md) | Parse a delimited string and print each element on a new line. Auto-detects colon, comma, or space as separator. |
| [x line fromcomma](/mod/line/fromcomma.md) | Parse a comma-separated string and print each element on a new line. |
| [x line fromcolon](/mod/line/fromcolon.md) | Parse a colon-separated string and print each element on a new line. |
| [x line fromeq](/mod/line/fromeq.md) | Parse an equals-separated string and print each element on a new line. Useful for parsing key=value pairs like environment variables. |
| [x line split](/mod/line/split.md) | Split a string by a specified separator and print each element on a new line. |
| [x line indexof](/mod/line/indexof.md) | Find the line number of the first line containing the target string in a file or stdin. |
| [x line contain](/mod/line/contain.md) | Check if a file or stdin contains the target string, returns 0 if found. |

# x llmf

Run local large language models based on llamafile, zero dependencies, zero configuration.



Key features:
- Start local API server (serve) with OpenAI-compatible interface
- CLI mode (cli) for quick text generation
- Interactive chat (chat) with multi-turn conversation
- Model management (model) with download/import/export/query
- Text tokenization (tokenize) to analyze token count



Supported formats: GGUF, llamafile


::: tip Usage tips:
1. Run 'x llmf init' for interactive first-time setup
2. Use 'x llmf serve --nobrowser' to start API service
3. Use '@l' shortcut in terminal for chat
4. Models are stored in ~/.x-cmd/data/llmf/model/
:::


## Examples

Example: interactive initialization

```sh
x llmf init
```

Example: start API server

```sh
x llmf serve -m llava/v1.5-7b/q4_k.gguf --nobrowser
```

Example: quick text generation

```sh
x llmf cli -p 'Write a Python function'
```

Example: list local models

```sh
x llmf model ls
```

Example: download specific model

```sh
x llmf model download llava/v1.5-7b/q4_k.gguf
```

# x lua

Module used to improve the Lua development experience, adding common functions needed to develop Lua projects

## Examples

Run the lua code

```sh
x lua ./hi.lua
```

Initialize lua project

```sh
x lua init
```

Install lua-cjson modules (using luarocks)

```sh
x lua i lua-cjson
```

Check lua code

```sh
x lua check ./hi.lua
```
## Introduction



`x lua` is a module aimed at enhancing the Lua development experience. It is compatible with platforms such as Windows, Linux, macOS, etc., and provides commonly needed functionalities for Lua projects, such as initializing Lua projects, downloading and installing Lua extensions, checking Lua code syntax, and formatting Lua code.



## Lua Version Used by x lua



`x lua` defaults to using the Lua version currently being used by the user. If Lua is not available in the user's environment, the `x lua` module will install and invoke [Lua provided by the x-cmd pkg system](https://x-cmd.com/pkg/lua), which is compiled by the x-cmd team, version 5.4.6. The process of compiling Lua by the x-cmd team mainly follows the practices of [LuaBinaries](https://luabinaries.sourceforge.net/) and [Homebrew](https://brew.sh/), aiming to stay consistent with the Lua community.



## Consideration of LUA_PATH and LUA_CPATH by x-cmd


1. For `LUA_PATH`, 6 levels of directories are set, prioritized from high to low as follows:
   - `./`: Current directory where Lua is executed.
   - `./lua_modules/`: Directory for Lua modules in the current Lua project.
   - `$LUA_PATH_WS/`: Lua workspace directory. Default value is empty unless specified by the user.
   - `$HOME/.luarocks/share/lua/`: Directory for global Lua modules in luarocks.
   - `${___X_CMD_ROOT_MOD}/lua/lib/share/`: Directory for Lua modules of the x-cmd Lua module.
   - `;;`: Default paths of the original LUA_PATH.


2. For `LUA_CPATH`, 5 levels of directories are set, prioritized from high to low as follows:
   - `./`: Current directory where Lua is executed.
   - `./lua_modules/`: Directory for Lua lib in the current Lua project.
   - `$LUA_PATH_WS/`: Lua workspace directory. Default value is empty unless specified by the user.
   - `$HOME/.luarocks/lib/lua/$LUA_version/`: Directory for global Lua lib in luarocks.
   - `usr/local/lib/lua/$LUA_version/`: Directory for system Lua lib storage.


3. For `.so`, `.dll`, and `.dylib` files, we have made additional adjustments to `LUA_CPATH`:
   - On Linux platforms, Lua can locate `.so` files in the 5-level directories set by `LUA_CPATH`.
   - On macOS platforms, Lua can locate `.so` and `.dylib` files in the 5-level directories set by `LUA_CPATH`.
   - On Windows platforms, Lua can locate `.dll` files in the 5-level directories set by `LUA_CPATH`.



## Development Progress of x lua



The development of the `x lua` module by the x-cmd team is in the preliminary stage, and we are continuously exploring better solutions. Currently implemented features (such as initializing Lua projects, downloading and installing Lua modules, checking Lua code syntax) mainly rely on the `x luarocks` module and third-party Lua extensions.

# x luarocks

Enhancement module for luarocks


::: tip
Run `x luarocks help` to get help for luarocks native commands
:::


## Examples

Install lua-cjson modules

```sh
x luarocks i lua-cjson
```

Remove lua-cjson modules

```sh
x luarocks remove lua-cjson
```

Use luarocks.cn server to speed up access to https://luarocks.org

```sh
x luarocks install lua-cjson --server https://luarocks.cn
```
## Introduction



`x luarocks` is an enhanced module for the luarocks command. This module is primarily used to simplify the installation configuration of luarocks and enhance the user experience of using luarocks.



## luarocks Version Used by the x luarocks Module



`x luarocks` by default invokes the luarocks currently being used by the user. If luarocks is not available in the user's environment, the `x luarocks` module will install and invoke [luarocks provided by the x-cmd pkg system](https://x-cmd.com/pkg/luarocks), which is luarocks version 3.11.0.



The luarocks provided by the x-cmd pkg system defaults to using lua 5.4.6 provided by the x-cmd pkg system. Users can adjust the corresponding configuration of luarocks to choose other versions of lua.

On **Windows platforms**, luarocks provided by the x-cmd pkg system is LuaRocks official precompiled luarocks;

On **Linux platforms** and **MacOS platforms**, the x-cmd pkg system downloads the LuaRocks official source code and uses [make provided by cosmo](https://x-cmd.com/mod/cosmo) to compile and install luarocks.



## Handling Dependencies of luarocks install Functionality such as gcc, unzip, etc.



`x luarocks install` by default calls the gcc, unzip, and other tools currently being used by the user. If these tools are not available in the user's environment, we provide `x lua ensurecc` + `x cosmo use unzip` as an alternative solution. This solution can quickly set up the environment for users without the need for **root privileges**, and it works on **Windows platforms**, **Linux platforms**, and **MacOS platforms**.

For detailed information about `x lua ensurecc` and `x cosmo use unzip`, please visit [x-cmd mod](https://x-cmd.com/mod/).

## Usage

```sh
x luarocks [OPTIONS] [FLAGS] [SUB_COMMAND] <#n>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#n` | extends `luarocks` subcmd or options |


## Options

| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--server` &lt;server&gt; |  | Fetch rocks/rockspecs from this server (takes priority over config file). |
| `--only-server` &lt;server&gt; |  | Fetch rocks/rockspecs from this server only (overrides any entries in the config file). |
| `--only-sources` &lt;url&gt; |  | Restrict downloads to paths matching the given URL. |
| `--namespace` &lt;namespace&gt; |  | Specify the rocks server namespace to use. |
| `--lua-dir` &lt;prefix&gt; |  | Which Lua installation to use |
| `--lua-version` &lt;ver&gt; |  | Which Lua version to use |
| `--tree` &lt;tree&gt; |  | Which tree to operate on |
| `--timeout` &lt;seconds&gt; |  | Timeout on network operations, in seconds. 0 means no timeout (wait forever). Default is 30. |


## Flags

| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `-h`, `--help` | Show this help message and exit. |
| `--version` | Show version info and exit. |
| `--dev` | Enable the sub-repositories in rocks servers for rockspecs of in-development versions. |
| `--local` | Use the tree in the user's home directory |
| `--global` | Use the system tree when `local_by_default` is `true` |
| `--no-project` | Do not use project tree even if running from a project folder |
| `--force-lock` | Attempt to overwrite the lock for commands that require exclusive access, such as 'install'. |
| `--verbose` | Display verbose output of commands executed. |

# x mac

The Mac module is a collection of handy tools designed specifically for macOS users. Its goal is to make it easier for users to automate tasks with scripts or manage their Macs remotely.

## Examples

Use fingerprint (touchid) for sudo verification, and restart password verification when failed

```sh
x mac tidsudo enable
```

Open claudecode, deny access to: $HOME/.bitcoin, $HOME/.ssh, $HOME/Library

```sh
x mac sb -9 -d "$HOME/.bitcoin" -d "$HOME/.ssh" -d "$HOME/Library" claude
```

Enable the alias feature, if no parameter is provided, it defaults to m, and you can use m instead of x mac in the future

```sh
x mac alias enable
```

Display System Information

```sh
x mac info
```

Get battery information

```sh
x mac b
```

Adjust the output volume to 24%

```sh
x mac vol set 24
```

Test network quality

```sh
x mac net test
```

Desktop Lock Screen

```sh
x mac lock
```

Entering sleep mode

```sh
x mac sleep
```

Ignoring the warnings, the computer was forcefully shut down

```sh
x mac shutdown -y
```

Empty the Trash

```sh
x mac trash empty
```

Show the list of disks

```sh
x mac disk ls
```

# x mankier

A command-line client tool for searching and browsing ManKier man pages via the ManKier API. For information about ManKier, please visit https://www.mankier.com/about

## Examples

Example: Explain tar command and its options

```sh
x mankier explain "tar -czvf"
```

Example: Explain 'jq -cr' command options

```sh
x mankier explain jq -cr
```

Example: Search man pages starting with 'ls'

```sh
x mankier query ls
```

Example: Search regex man pages with interactive UI

```sh
x mankier query --app regex
```

Example: Get detailed man page for jq.1

```sh
x mankier page jq.1
```

Example: Search nvme on ManKier via DDGo

```sh
x mankier : nvme
```

Example: Get NAME section content from tar man page

```sh
x mankier section NAME tar
```

Example: Get all reference links for tar man page

```sh
x mankier ref tar
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x mankier explain](/mod/mankier/explain.md) | Explain a Shell Command |
| [x mankier query](/mod/mankier/query.md) | Search man pages |
| [x mankier page](/mod/mankier/page.md) | Get details for a man page |
| [x mankier section](/mod/mankier/section.md) | Get the contents of a section in a man page |
| [x mankier ref](/mod/mankier/ref.md) | Get all the connections from and to a man page |
| [x mankier ddgo](/mod/mankier/ddgo.md) | Search for relevant information on the ManKier website using DuckDuckGo |

# x mosh

Mosh (https://mosh.org/) is an interactive SSH alternative that supports roaming, intermittent connections, intelligent local echo and line editing.

This module prioritizes using the local mosh command. If it's not available, it will download and run via pixi, requiring no installation and impacting neither your environment nor system dependencies (Windows is not yet supported).

For more information about pixi, please visit https://prefix.dev/ or run `pixi --help`.

## Examples

Connect to a remote server

```sh
x mosh root@192.168.1.134
```

Select Mosh UDP 80 port

```sh
x mosh -p 80 root@192.168.1.134
```

Connect to a remote server using 2222 port

```sh
x mosh --ssh="ssh -p 2222" root@192.168.1.134
```

Equivalent to the 'mosh -h' command

```sh
x mosh -- -h
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x mosh --](/mod/mosh/--.md) | Run the 'mosh' command directly |

# x nano

Wraps the nano editor with automatic on-demand installation. On macOS, when detecting the system's pico (disguised as nano), it automatically switches to the more feature-complete GNU nano. Supports all native nano command-line arguments.


::: tip To place the cursor on a specific line of a file, put the line number with
a '+' before the filename.  The column number can be added after a comma.

When a filename is '-', nano reads data from standard input.
:::

::: tip On macOS, the system "nano" is actually pico which cannot load nanorc
configuration files. This command automatically detects pico and downloads

GNU nano for direct use without affecting the system.
:::


## Examples

Edit myfile.txt with nano

```sh
x nano myfile.txt
```

Open file and place cursor at line 10

```sh
x nano +10 myfile.txt
```

Open file and place cursor at line 10, column 5

```sh
x nano +10,5 myfile.txt
```

Open menu with nano documentation and resource links

```sh
x nano --open
```

## Usage

```sh
x nano <#n>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#n` | Extends `nano` command and options |

# x neo

Neofetch is an updated version of screenfetch, where "neo" means "new".

X-CMD interprets it as Neo (from The Matrix). The default subcommand

"fetch" provides functionality similar to neofetch.



In the long term, neo will evolve into an AI agent that assists users

in managing and understanding their OS based on system information.

We will soon provide "x neo chat" for interactive OS assistance.



Currently, it shows OS, kernel, uptime, packages, shell, desktop

environment, window manager, CPU, GPU, memory and other system

information alongside distribution ASCII art logos.

It supports both standard and large ASCII art logos, multiple

display modes (mini/std/all/llm/ui), and customizable info widgets.


::: tip Use 'x neo logo ls' to see all supported distro logos
Use 'x neo logo large &lt;name&gt;' to display large ASCII art

Use 'x neo --cfg' to configure startup behavior
:::


## Examples

Display system info with default settings

```sh
x neo
```

Show all available system information

```sh
x neo fetch --all
```

List all supported distribution logos

```sh
x neo logo ls
```

Print the Arch Linux ASCII art logo

```sh
x neo logo print arch
```

Print the large Arch Linux logo

```sh
x neo logo large arch
```

Show minimal system information

```sh
x neo fetch --mini
```

Display system info without logo

```sh
x neo fetch --no-logo
```

Configure startup behavior

```sh
x neo --cfg
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x neo fetch](/mod/neo/fetch.md) | Display system information (default command) |
| [x neo logo](/mod/neo/logo.md) | Logo operations - print ASCII art logos |
| [x neo update](/mod/neo/update.md) | Update the neo module |
| [x neo boot](/mod/neo/boot.md) | Boot operations for startup display |
| [x neo fastfetch](/mod/neo/fastfetch.md) | Run fastfetch command |
| [x neo --cfg](/mod/neo/--cfg.md) | Configure neo settings (startup, tmux, ssh modes) |

# x nets

nets is an enhanced module designed for the `netstat` command, aiming to provide a more intuitive way to display network statistics.

It supports interactive mode, various output formats, and flexible filtering capabilities, greatly simplifying the viewing and analysis of network status.

## Examples

```sh

```

```sh

```

View information for the 'internet' table (TCP/UDP connections)

```sh
x nets view internet
```

Output 'route' table information in TSV format

```sh
x nets view --tsv route
```

## Usage

```sh

```

## Flags

# x notify

Send cross-platform desktop notifications using the OS-native backend (macOS, Linux, Windows / WSL)


::: tip
Backend dependencies: osascript on macOS, notify-send (libnotify) on Linux, PowerShell on Windows / WSL.
:::

::: tip
Quotes and backslashes in msg and title are auto-escaped per platform.
:::

::: tip
macOS `display notification` does not support custom icons; --icon is ignored on macOS.
:::


## Examples

Example: Send a notification with the default title

```sh
x notify "build finished"
```

Example: Use a custom notification title

```sh
x notify --title "Build" "build finished"
```

Example: Use a custom icon on Linux/Windows

```sh
x notify --icon /usr/share/icons/Adwaita/symbolic/status/dialog-warning.svg "task done"
```

## Usage

```sh
x notify [FLAGS] <#1>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | Notification message |


## Flags

| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--title`, `-t` | Notification title, default X-CMD Notify |
| `--icon`, `-i` | Custom icon path (Linux/Windows only; ignored on macOS) |

# x ohmyposh

Oh-my-posh is a cross platform tool to render your prompt.

It can use the same configuration everywhere to offer a consistent experience, regardless of where you are.

For a detailed guide on getting started, have a look at the docs at https://ohmyposh.dev



The ohmyposh module is a powerful enhancement for oh-my-posh, designed to make theme customization a breeze. It lets you download theme resource packs, simplifying the process of switching between different looks.

This module also includes a handy theme preview feature, allowing you to directly preview various themes right in your command line. This makes choosing and changing themes a much smoother experience.


::: tip
This module's try/untry feature is currently only compatible with bash and zsh environments.
:::

::: tip
Using the ohmyposh module's theme will override the current environment's POSH_THEME variable
:::

::: tip
1_shell theme is incompatible with xonsh. For details, please check github.com/JanDeDobbeleer/oh-my-posh/issues/6282.
:::


## Examples

Invoke the command `x ohmyposh fz` to interactively preview the oh-my-posh theme

```sh
x ohmyposh
```

Use the montys theme globally

```sh
x ohmyposh use montys
```

Use a custom configuration theme globally

```sh
x ohmyposh use <custom file path>
```

Cancel the theme that is currently used globally

```sh
x ohmyposh unuse
```

Try to use the agnoster theme in this current Shell

```sh
x ohmyposh try agnoster
```

View the currently used theme settings

```sh
x ohmyposh current
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x ohmyposh ls](/mod/ohmyposh/ls.md) | List all theme |
| [x ohmyposh fz](/mod/ohmyposh/fz.md) | An interactive list showcasing previews of all the themes |
| [x ohmyposh which](/mod/ohmyposh/which.md) | Retrieve the configuration file path for the specified theme |
| [x ohmyposh update](/mod/ohmyposh/update.md) | Update all theme configuration and preview files |
| [x ohmyposh use](/mod/ohmyposh/use.md) | Apply the specified theme globally |
| [x ohmyposh unuse](/mod/ohmyposh/unuse.md) | Use the specified theme globally |
| [x ohmyposh try](/mod/ohmyposh/try.md) | In this current Shell, attempt to use the specified theme |
| [x ohmyposh untry](/mod/ohmyposh/untry.md) | Cancel the theme that the current Shell is trying to use |
| [x ohmyposh current](/mod/ohmyposh/current.md) | Display the currently used prompt theme |
| [x ohmyposh feature](/mod/ohmyposh/feature.md) | Manage features of the current theme |
| [x ohmyposh --](/mod/ohmyposh/--.md) | Use the native commands of oh-my-posh |

# x onsh

xonsh is a Python-powered shell that supports users to mix Python and shell commands on the command line.

This module mainly provides support for calling the x-cmd toolset on xonsh; and adds functions such as searching the official website ( xon.sh ) , using without installation, and generating xonsh commands with LLM.


::: tip In xonsh, because `@<name>` is interpreted as an annotation, when no parameters are provided (e.g., `@gemini`), xonsh will wait for the function to be decorated.
Users can input `;` to avoid this issue, such as `@gemini ;`.
:::


## Examples

Modify the $HOME/.xonshrc file to introduce the x-cmd toolkit (including the x command, c command, @gpt, comma command, etc.) into the xonsh environment.

```sh
x onsh setup
```

Search the xon.sh website for content related to "alias" and display the search results in an interactive table format.

```sh
x onsh : alias
```

Start xonsh. If xonsh is not already installed locally, it will be automatically installed and used through the x-cmd pkg system (this process will not affect your environment variables or dependencies).

```sh
x onsh
```

## Usage

```sh
x onsh [SUB_COMMAND] <#n>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#n` | extends `xonsh` subcmd or options |


## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x onsh setup](#x-onsh-setup) | Modify the $HOME/.xonshrc file to introduce the x-cmd toolset into the xonsh environment |
| [x onsh ddgo](#x-onsh-ddgo) | Search the xon.sh website for the specified content |


### x onsh setup

Modify the $HOME/.xonshrc file to introduce the x-cmd toolset into the xonsh environment

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | content |

Text to speech


# x osv

The `osv` module is the CLI for the OSV (Open Source Vulnerabilities) project, mainly used for obtaining open source vulnerability information and integrating vulnerability scanning tools to help developers and users better address software security issues.

OSV is an open source project initiated by Google, aiming to provide a unified and easily accessible open source software vulnerability database. Its official website is https://osv.dev.

## Examples

Get vulnerability information for a given vulnerability ID ( osv-*, cve-*, etc. Case insensitive. )

```sh
x osv osv-2020-111
```

Scan system installed packages or local project dependencies and generate a unified SARIF report

```sh
x osv sarif
```

Generate a unified SARIF report in JSON format by scanning the dependencies of pip projects in the specified directory.

```sh
x osv sarif pip --json "<project dir>"
```

Query the vulnerabilities of the specified version of software

```sh
x osv q -p jq -v 1.7.1
```

Query the vulnerabilities of the specified software

```sh
x osv q -p OSS-Fuzz,jq
```

Retrieve vulnerability information for OSV-2020-111 and output it in JSON format.

```sh
x osv vuln --json OSV-2020-111
```

Search for git-related vulnerabilities on the osv.dev website.

```sh
x osv : git
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x osv ls](/mod/osv/ls.md) | List all Cloud Storage |
| [x osv q](/mod/osv/q.md) | Query vulnerabilities for a given package and version |
| [x osv eco](/mod/osv/eco.md) | List OSV-supported ecosystem |
| [x osv scanner](/mod/osv/scanner.md) | Scan for vulnerabilities using osv-scanner |
| [x osv sarif](/mod/osv/sarif.md) | Using osv-scanner to scan system installed packages or local project dependencies and generate a unified SARIF report |
| [x osv vuln](/mod/osv/vuln.md) | Get vulnerability information for a given vulnerability ID |
| [x osv ddgo](/mod/osv/ddgo.md) | Search the osv.dev website for the specified content |
| [x osv ddgoai](/mod/osv/ddgoai.md) | Search for specific content on the osv.dev website and use AI to summarize it |

`x paru` is an enhancement tool for the `paru` AUR helper, designed for Arch Linux users.

# x pick

Create interactive option-based picklists in the terminal


::: tip
Sometimes you need to specify the loading function command through `___X_CMD_PICK_SHBIN_CODE` in zsh environment
:::


## Examples

Stats file information and creates an interactive selection list in the terminal based on the counted content

```sh
stat `ls | x pick`
```

Enumerates the contents of the "$___X_CMD_ROOT_MOD" file directory and creates an interactive selection list in the terminal based on the enumerated contents

```sh
x pick ls "$___X_CMD_ROOT_MOD"
```

Create an interactive selection list in the terminal based on the enumeration, and you can select up to two items.Use the [Tab] key to select or deselect

```sh
ls | x pick --limit 2
```

Create an interactive picklist in the terminal that is presented as two columns based on the columns of the enumerated content

```sh
ls | x pick --col 2
```

Get the data list in the ___X_CMD_PICK_DATA variable

```sh
___X_CMD_PICK_DATA="$(ls)"; x pick
```

## Usage

```sh
x pick [OPTIONS] [FLAGS]
```

## Options

| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--ask` &lt;string&gt; |  | Display what you want to ask |
| `--row` &lt;number&gt; |  | set rows |
| `--col` &lt;number&gt; |  | set columns |
| `--width` &lt;number&gt; |  | set width |
| `--limit` &lt;number&#124;no-limit&gt; |  | set the number of options |
| `--continue` &lt;string&gt; |  | Specify the target pick app name to inherit the previously available QUIT position |
| `--datafile` &lt;filepath&gt; |  | Specify the datafile to pick |


## Flags

| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--ctrl-c-clear` | Clear the screen when Ctrl-C is pressed |
| `--ctrl-c-keep` | Keep the screen when Ctrl-C is pressed |

# x pixi

Pixi is a cross-platform, multilingual package manager and workflow tool built on the conda ecosystem. Its official website is https://prefix.dev/

This module first tries to use any available PixiJS installation in the current environment. If none is found, it automatically runs `x pixi --install` to install and activate it.

This module is primarily designed to optimize the user experience of installing and using Pixi, such as using the Codeberg Pixi mirror to improve the download experience for users in China.

Furthermore, it introduces the `la` command for interactive searching and previewing installable Pixi packages, and offers x-cmd style commands like `use` and `unuse` for managing global packages within the current user environment.

## Examples

Install fish shell and jq in the user environment. Equivalent to `pixi global install fish jq`

```sh
x pixi use fish jq
```

List the packages and dependency in the user environment.

```sh
x pixi use ls
```

Use the interactive app to search for all available packages

```sh
x pixi
```

Install the yq command globally using pixi

```sh
x pixi g install yq
```

Activate pixi in the current user environment.

```sh
x pixi --activate
```

Activate pixi in the current user environment.

```sh
x pixi --deactivate
```

Install pixi (Install the latest version by default)

```sh
x pixi --upgrade
```

Install pixi (Install the latest version by default)

```sh
x pixi --install
```
## Introduction



The `x pixi` module is an enhanced tool for pixi commands implemented by the x-cmd team using the posix shell. It optimizes the installation and usage experience of pixi commands as follows:
1. Provide auto-completion functionality for advise. For users in China, we also offer a localized version of advise.
2. For users in China, considering the network issues accessing Github, we use a mirror on Codeberg to help users quickly download and install pixi.
3. Provide document search functionality. Support searching for document content on the pixi.sh website from the command line, so that users can quickly obtain the desired pixi command documentation.
4. Provide the `la` command. In an interactive environment, it uses `fzf` as the interactive framework, helping users quickly find the required software and view software information.



## prefix-dev/pixi



[`pixi`](https://github.com/prefix-dev/pixi) is a package and workflow management tool developed in Rust by the [prefix-dev team](https://github.com/prefix-dev). It can download and install various software tools (such as Python, Git, Vim, jq, etc.) and manage project environments, dependencies, tasks, and more.



Built on the Conda ecosystem, `pixi` is compatible with both Conda and PyPI ecosystems. Compared to Conda, `pixi` is compiled into a single executable file, offering faster dependency resolution and package installation, lower memory usage, and more comprehensive project management capabilities. It is an excellent choice for Conda users seeking a lightweight and efficient solution.

## Usage

```sh
x pixi [SUB_COMMAND] <#n>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#n` | extends `pixi` subcmd or options |


## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x pixi unuse](/mod/pixi/unuse.md) | Uninstalling the software package in the user environment. Equivalent to `x pixi use rm`, or `pixi global uninstall`. |
| [x pixi use](/mod/pixi/use.md) | Managing software packages within the user environment.  By default, this is equivalent to running  `x pixi use add <pkg> [pkg...]` or `pixi global install <pkg> [pkg...]`. |
| [x pixi --install](/mod/pixi/--install.md) | Install the specified version of pixi |
| [x pixi --uninstall](/mod/pixi/--uninstall.md) | Uninstall pixi and remove related data (the .pixi directory in the HOME directory). |
| [x pixi --activate](/mod/pixi/--activate.md) | Activate pixi, allowing globally installed software to run directly |
| [x pixi --deactivate](/mod/pixi/--deactivate.md) | With pixi deactivated, the newly launched shell won't automatically load pixi's environment variables, like PATH.  This means any software globally installed via pixi will be inaccessible. |
| [x pixi --upgrade](/mod/pixi/--upgrade.md) | Update Pixi to the latest version. |
| [x pixi la](/mod/pixi/la.md) | List the packages supported by pixi |
| [x pixi ddgo](/mod/pixi/ddgo.md) | Search the pixi.sh website for the specified content |
| [x pixi --](/mod/pixi/--.md) | Run the pixi command directly |

# x pkgx

pkgx is an independent, lightweight Universal Tool Runner that helps developers obtain and run any open-source tool directly without the need for prior installation or configuration.

It aims to address the issues of "versioning" and "instant availability" in the development environment, and its official website is https://pkgx.dev/

## Examples

Use the interactive app to search for all available packages, equivalent to `x pkgx ls`

```sh
x pkgx
```

Use the bun software without installing or registering it in the system and without modifying the PATH

```sh
x pkgx bun --eval 'console.log("hello world")'
```

Add fzf to the current execution environment so that the fzf command can be executed directly

```sh
eval "$(x pkgx +fzf)"
```

Equivalent to the 'pkgx --help' command

```sh
x pkgx -- --help
```

## Usage

```sh
x pkgx [SUB_COMMAND] <#n>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#n` | extends `pkgx` subcmd or options |


## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x pkgx --install](/mod/pkgx/--install.md) | Install the specified version of pkgx |
| [x pkgx --uninstall](/mod/pkgx/--uninstall.md) | Uninstall pkgx |
| [x pkgx --activate](/mod/pkgx/--activate.md) | Activate pkgx |
| [x pkgx --deactivate](/mod/pkgx/--deactivate.md) | Deactivate pkgx |
| [x pkgx --upgrade](/mod/pkgx/--upgrade.md) | Update pkgx to the latest version. |
| [x pkgx ddgo](/mod/pkgx/ddgo.md) | Search the docs.pkgx.sh website for the specified content |
| [x pkgx ls](/mod/pkgx/ls.md) | List the packages supported by pkgx |
| [x pkgx --](/mod/pkgx/--.md) | Run the pkgx command directly |

# x python

Enhanced python command


::: info Extends 'python' options.
See https://docs.python.org/ website for more information.

See `x python --help` for more information.
:::

## Introduction



The Python module is dedicated to enhancing the user experience of Python users in the command line.



## Striving for Consistency



We strive to maintain consistency with the Python command. However, there will be enhancements that may cause differences, for example:


1. `x python me:hi.py`: The Python module will attempt to download the file from the hub to the local directory before executing it.
2. Due to the enhancement in point 1, if you want to run the file `me:hi.py` in the current folder, you can only do so by adding `./` in front: `x python ./me:hi.py`.
3. We consider it extremely rare for directory names to contain ":" and thus have designed it this way.



## Adding GPT Functionality



If you want to know how to achieve a certain functionality using the Python command, you can use "co" (copilot, abbreviated as `,`). For example, `x python , How to set up an HTTP server to serve all contents located in $HOME` will return `python -m http.server --directory "$HOME"`.



If you need to query the corresponding code, you can use "coco" (code copilot, abbreviated as `,,`):


1. `x python ,, Put file names in $HOME directory into a dict`.
2. We will use the local Python interpreter for linting to check the syntax correctness. If there are any issues, users can choose to package the problem and code to return to GPT for re-questioning.

## Usage

```sh
x python <#1> <#n>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | python script |
| `#n` | extends `python` subcmd or options |

# x qywx

Send and listen to WXwork messages using x qywx.


::: tip Webhook Bot (x qywx bot)
Use case: One-way notifications to groups, e.g., CI/CD build notifications (GitHub Actions), server monitoring alerts

Setup: https://x-cmd.com/mod/qywx/cookbook-1
:::

::: tip Intelligent Bot (x qywx abot)
Use case: Send and receive messages via WebSocket background listener service

First-time setup requires bot_id and bot_secret (from WXwork Open Platform application creation)

Configuration command: x qywx --cfg bot_id=&lt;id&gt; bot_secret=&lt;secret&gt;
:::

::: tip Integrate with claw as private AI assistant:
1. Configure bot_id and bot_secret
2. Start WXwork background listener service: x qywx abot service start
3. Start x claw to integrate with WXwork: x claw start --qywx
:::


## Examples

Initialize configuration in interactive mode

```sh
x qywx init
```

Send text messages to WXwork group

```sh
x qywx send --text "x-cmd 新版本发布成功"
```

Send text messages using intelligent bot

```sh
x qywx abot send --text --chatid <chat_id> "Hello"
```

Start intelligent bot listener service

```sh
x qywx abot service start
```

Stop listener service

```sh
x qywx abot service stop
```

Start interactive REPL mode, executing messages as commands and returning output

```sh
x qywx react --runner repl
```

## Usage

| [x qywx bot](/mod/qywx/bot.md) | Send messages using WXwork group bot |
| [x qywx abot](/mod/qywx/abot.md) | Send messages and manage listener service using WXwork intelligent bot |

# x repo

Unify code repository clone paths for AI agents (default ~/.x-repo/&lt;provider&gt;/&lt;owner&gt;/&lt;name&gt;, shared across agents)


::: tip
Unless the user specifies otherwise or an existing convention applies, place new clones under the default layout — enabling cross-agent reuse, `x repo` discoverability, and future sync / shared cache acceleration.
:::

::: tip
Without format flag, interactive terminal opens csv app; pipe or redirect outputs TSV.
:::

::: tip
Open in tmux: `x repo t <id>` or `x tmux repo <id>`. The session is named `<provider>/<owner>/<name>` (github.com→gh, codeberg.org→cb, gitlab.com→gl, gitee.com→gt, bitbucket.org→bb).
:::


## Examples

Default: resolve then cd into the local repo; update-clones if missing

```sh
x repo x-bash/repo
```

Example: list all cloned repositories

```sh
x repo ls
```

Raw paths: provider/org/repo format, suitable for scripting

```sh
x repo ls --raw
```

TSV format: with headers, suitable for piping and awk

```sh
x repo ls --tsv
```

CSV format: suitable for spreadsheets and database import

```sh
x repo ls --csv
```

Resolve owner/name to the local path (owner contains sh, name contains re)

```sh
x repo which sh/re
```

which in fuzzy mode: a leading / routes through fuzzywhich

```sh
x repo which /sh/re
```

which in wt mode: @&lt;wtname&gt; resolves directly to the worktree path (wtname can be branch / tag / SHA / agent name / issue id)

```sh
x repo which x-bash/repo@feat~auth
```

Explicit cd: equivalent to the default x repo &lt;name&gt;

```sh
x repo cd x-bash/repo
```

shortcut for fresh: resolve then open in the fresh editor

```sh
x repo fe x-bash/repo
```

shortcut for code: resolve then open in vscode; update-clones if missing

```sh
x repo c x-bash/repo
```

shortcut for tmux: open (or create) session :gh/x-bash/repo

```sh
x repo t x-bash/repo
```

Batch: resolve each id and clone-or-update in turn

```sh
x repo update x-bash/repo x-bash/brew
```

Multi-repo workspace setup: clone-or-update each id and print resolved paths for ../&lt;sibling&gt; references

```sh
x repo prepare x-bash/repo x-bash/wsl
```

Repo scorecard: 1 GraphQL (carrying 12 aliased search counts) + 2 REST commits, outputs star/lastCommit/lastRelease/release/contributor/pullRequest/issue/language/totalLine plus four windowed recent:{last30d,last90d,last180d,last360d} blocks, fully API-driven

```sh
x repo card x-cmd/install
```

Default form: create-or-attach a worktree on branch feat/auth (new branch from HEAD if absent, attaches otherwise)

```sh
x repo wt x-bash/repo feat/auth
```

List all worktrees of the repo (bare + default wt + extras)

```sh
x repo wt ls x-bash/repo
```

Graceful remove (git worktree remove; bare's worktrees/ registry stays in sync)

```sh
x repo wt rm x-bash/repo feat/auth
```

Reuse a wt path: x repo which &lt;id&gt;@&lt;wtname&gt; resolves directly to the worktree

```sh
x repo which x-bash/repo@feat~auth
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x repo ls](/mod/repo/ls.md) | List all cloned code repositories |
| [x repo which](/mod/repo/which.md) | Resolve owner/name to a local clone path (a leading / uses fuzzywhich for fuzzy matching) |
| [x repo cd](/mod/repo/cd.md) | Resolve then cd into the local repo path (update-clones if missing) |
| [x repo fresh](/mod/repo/fresh.md) | Resolve then open the local repo in the fresh editor |
| [x repo code](/mod/repo/code.md) | Resolve then open the local repo in vscode (update-clones if missing) |
| [x repo tmux](/mod/repo/tmux.md) | Resolve then open a tmux session (naming follows x tmux repo; see tip) |
| [x repo update](/mod/repo/update.md) | Resolve each id; update if a local clone exists, otherwise clone; accepts multiple ids |
| [x repo prepare](/mod/repo/prepare.md) | Prepare a multi-repo local workspace; clone-or-update each id and print resolved paths |
| [x repo card](/mod/repo/card.md) | Emit a YAML scorecard for a repo: 1 GraphQL (carrying 8 aliased search counts) + 2 REST commits, API-only, no local clone touched |
| [x repo init](/mod/repo/init.md) | Push an empty bare from uninitialized to initialized: scaffold a minimal README, commit, push to main, then attach the default worktree |
| [x repo wt](/mod/repo/wt.md) | Manage worktrees: create-or-attach (default), explicit create, list (ls), remove (rm); a thin worktree-only wrapper, does not fetch or merge |

# x rg

rg (ripgrep) is a modern search tool similar to grep that supports recursively searching for lines matching a regex pattern within the current directory.

`x rg` is an enhancement module based on the rg command, designed to improve the rg user experience. The specific enhancements are as follows:
1. Simplified rg command installation: If rg is not found in the current environment, `x rg` will download and install rg through the x-cmd pkg system in a way that does not affect the user's environment.
2. Provides the `--fzfapp` command: This offers an interactive way to use the rg command with fzf.


::: tip Shortcut Keys in Interactive Mode:
`alt-a`: Select all matching items

`alt-d`: Deselect all selected items

`ctrl-/`: Hide/Show Preview Window

`ctrl-o`: Edit selected items with editor

`ctrl-t`: Toggle between Ripgrep and Fzf search modes
:::


## Examples

Using fzf to provide interactive app search for rg in the current directory

```sh
x rg
```

Using fzf to provide an interactive app for rg to process the results of the `x ascii` command.

```sh
x ascii | x rg
```

Use fzf to provide interactive app search for a specified directory or file with rg

```sh
x rg --fzfapp ~/.x-cmd.root
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x rg --fzfapp](/mod/rg/--fzfapp.md) | Using fzf to provide an interactive app for rg |
| [x rg --cmd](/mod/rg/--cmd.md) | Run the rg command directly |

# x sb

`x sb` is a cross-platform sandbox runner that executes commands with minimal privileges.

It supports Deno-style permission control, such as `--net` to enable network access, `--tty` to allow TTY access, `--pwd` to allow access to the current directory, etc.



On macOS, it uses `sandbox-exec` with dynamically generated profiles;

on Linux, it leverages pledge-style constraints;

on unsupported systems, execution can be forced using `___X_CMD_SB_RUN_ANYWAY=1`.



Ideal for securing scripts or tools in lightweight, permission-restricted environments without needing full containers.

## Examples

Block curl access

```sh
x sb airrun curl https://x-cmd.com || echo "Successfully stop curl from Internet"
```

Allow write access to the `./tmp` directory. The command `touch /tmp/test.txt` should succeed

```sh
x sb editrun --wd ./tmp touch ./tmp/test.txt
```

Access Home directory. The command `ls ~` should succeed

```sh
x sb --home ls ~
```

## Usage

```sh
x sb [FLAGS] [SUB_COMMAND]
```

## Flags

| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--net` | Allow network access |
| `--all` | Allow all filesystem access |
| `--allrx` | Allow read and execute permissions |
| `--tty` | Allow TTY access |
| `--pwd` | Allow access to the current working directory |
| `--home` | Allow access to the user's home directory |
| `--ws` | Allow access to the workspace directory (the most recent directory with .x-cmd) |


## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x sb airrun](/mod/sb/airrun.md) | Provides broad local resource access (e.g., file system, TTY) while prohibiting network access |
| [x sb editrun](/mod/sb/editrun.md) | Provides operations to modify specified directories or files (e.g., creating, writing to, or deleting files) |
| [x sb stdiorun](/mod/sb/stdiorun.md) | Provides a highly restricted sandbox environment, prohibiting file system modifications and network access |

# x scoop

Enhanced module based on scoop, providing auto-download, efficient search, mirror acceleration and command completion for seamless shell integration

## Examples

List installed applications

```sh
x scoop ls/list
```

Enable aria2 to download packages using multiple threads

```sh
x scoop aria2 enable
```

View detailed information about Telegram

```sh
x scoop info telegram --verbose
```

Do not use local cache, and re-download the latest Telegram from the remote source

```sh
x scoop install telegram --no-cache
```

View the currently available buckets

```sh
x scoop bucket list
```

Add known bucket

```sh
x scoop bucket add <bucket>
```

Add a bucket from other

```sh
x scoop bucket add <name> <repo>
```

Download from third-party bucket

```sh
x scoop install <bucket name>/<app_name>
```

Using native proxy  commands

```sh
x scoop config proxy 127.0.0.0:8888
```

# x scorecard

OpenSSF Scorecard is a project developed by the Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) that automates the assessment of the security and best practices compliance of open source projects.

The `x scorecard` module attempts to encapsulate the scorecard.dev API service into simpler commands to help developers and users better use Scorecard to identify potential security risks.


::: tip
Running `x scorecard help` will provide help for the scorecard command
:::


## Examples

Show the OpenSSF Scorecard for the github.com/ossf/scorecard project

```sh
x scorecard info github.com/ossf/scorecard
```

Find OpenSSF Scorecard Supported Open Source Projects

```sh
x scorecard search
```

Open the OpenSSF Scorecard report for the github.com/ossf/scorecard project

```sh
x scorecard open github.com/ossf/scorecard
```

## Usage

```sh
x scorecard [SUB_COMMAND] <#n>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#n` | extends `scorecard` subcmd or options |


## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x scorecard info](/mod/scorecard/info.md) | Display the OpenSSF Scorecard for Open Source Software |
| [x scorecard search](/mod/scorecard/search.md) | Find OpenSSF Scorecard Supported Open Source Projects |
| [x scorecard open](/mod/scorecard/open.md) | Open the OpenSSF Scorecard report for the specified project |
| [x scorecard update](/mod/scorecard/update.md) | Update local scorecard index data |

# x sd

sd (search & displace) is a text search and replace tool that uses common regular expression syntax, similar to sed, but focuses on replacement operations, making it more intuitive and readable.

This module primarily utilizes fzf to interactively preview changes in text content, enabling users to dynamically view the effects of expression changes. It also adds the functionality of direct use without installation.

Within the fzf preview window, you can use the shortcut key `ctrl-s` to leverage diff and view contextual differences within the text content.

## Examples

Interactively view the effects of expression search and replace text

```sh
x sd <test.txt
```

Preview the changes made to the test.txt file using fzf.

```sh
x sd --fzfapp test.txt
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x sd --fzfapp](/mod/sd/--fzfapp.md) | Using fzf to provide an interactive app for sd |
| [x sd --cmd](/mod/sd/--cmd.md) | Run the sd command directly |

# x sed

sed (Stream Editor) is a powerful text processing tool that supports processing large amounts of text in a streaming manner. It is suitable for operations such as searching, replacing, inserting, and deleting file content.

This module primarily utilizes fzf to interactively preview changes in text content, enabling users to dynamically view the effects of expression changes and display contextual differences in the text content.

Within the fzf preview window, you can use the shortcut key `ctrl-s` to leverage diff and view contextual differences within the text content.

## Examples

Example: Interactively view the effects of expression search and replace text

```sh
x sed <test.txt
```

Example: Preview changes to test.txt file using fzf

```sh
x sed --fzfapp test.txt
```

Example: Replace 'world' with 'universe'

```sh
echo "hello world" | x sed 's/world/universe/'
```

Example: Globally replace all 'foo' with 'bar' in file

```sh
x sed 's/foo/bar/g' file.txt
```

Example: Print lines 2 to 5 of file

```sh
x sed -n '2,5p' file.txt
```

Example: Delete lines containing pattern

```sh
x sed '/pattern/d' file.txt
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x sed --fzfapp](/mod/sed/--fzfapp.md) | Using fzf to provide an interactive app for sed |
| [x sed --cmd](/mod/sed/--cmd.md) | Run the sed command directly |

# x seq

Generate number sequences, same functionality as GNU seq, but with a compact colon-separated range syntax (`start:step:end`) and the ability to invoke shell commands or inject functions for each element.



Differences from GNU seq:
- Uses `:` as range separator — `x seq 1:10` instead of `seq 1 10`
- Supports shell invocation — pass a shell expression, `eval` command, or function name to process each number
- Supports awk inline code — write `{ ... }` to use awk for iteration and processing
- Pure shell loop by default — no external process overhead, ideal for small ranges


::: tip
In awk mode, the loop variable is `e`. Write `{ print e ** 2; }` to print squares.
:::

::: tip
Use `awk` prefix to pass full awk program with BEGIN/END blocks: `x seq awk 1:10 '...'`.
:::

::: tip
Range syntax: `end` → 1 to end; `start:end` → start to end (auto step); `start:step:end` → full control.
:::

::: tip
Descending sequences are auto-detected: `x seq 10:1` generates 10, 9, …, 1 (step becomes -1).
:::

::: tip
By default uses pure shell loop (no external command) — avoids process startup overhead for small ranges. Use `{ ... }` awk mode for large datasets or complex processing.
:::

::: tip
Descending sequence is auto-detected (e.g. `x seq 10:1` generates 10 to 1). GNU seq requires explicit negative step (`seq 10 -1 1`) — `seq 10 1` produces no output. BSD seq infers direction like `x seq` does.
:::


## Examples

Print numbers 1 to 10 (same as `seq 1 10`).

```sh
x seq 10
```

Print numbers 5 to 10.

```sh
x seq 5:10
```

Print numbers 10 to 1 in descending order (auto step -1).

```sh
x seq 10:1
```

Print numbers 0, 5, 10, …, 50 with step 5.

```sh
x seq 0:5:50
```

Print squares of 1 to 10 using awk inline code.

```sh
x seq 1:10 '{ print e ** 2; }'
```

Print squares using shell arithmetic expression.

```sh
x seq 1:10 '"$((e**2))"'
```

Print numbers 001 to 010 with zero-padding.

```sh
x seq 1:10 eval 'printf "%03d\n" "$e"'
```

Use a shell function to process each number.

```sh
pow(){ printf "%s\n" "$((e**2))"; }; x seq 1:10 pow
```

Full awk mode with BEGIN block — accumulates A while iterating.

```sh
x seq awk 1:10 '{ print (A+=10) "\t" e }; BEGIN{ A=1; }'
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x seq awk](/mod/seq/awk.md) | Use `x seq awk <range> '<awk-body>'` to run a full awk program. The iteration is driven by awk internally. The awk body should define a `iter(e)` function body (default: `{ print e; }`). You can also include BEGIN/END blocks for setup and teardown. |

# x service

Manage system services including start, stop, restart, status check.

Supports viewing service logs, checking alive status, pause/resume services.


::: tip Service name can be with or without .service suffix.
Use the log subcommand to view real-time service log output.
:::


## Examples

Example: start nginx service

```sh
x service start nginx
```

Example: stop nginx service

```sh
x service stop nginx
```

Example: restart nginx service

```sh
x service restart nginx
```

Example: check nginx service status

```sh
x service status nginx
```

Example: view nginx service logs

```sh
x service log nginx
```

Example: check if nginx service is alive

```sh
x service isalive nginx
```

Example: pause nginx service

```sh
x service pause nginx
```

Example: resume nginx service

```sh
x service resume nginx
```

Example: register myservice for boot autostart

```sh
x service install myservice
```

Example: remove myservice from boot autostart

```sh
x service uninstall myservice
```


# x shodan

The shodan command-line interface is powered by x-cmd, mainly using posix shell, awk and curl.


::: tip
- Get shodan api key: https://account.shodan.io/
- Interactive env use `x shodan init` to initialize configuration. The configure will be saved locally.
- Run command `x shodan --cfg key=<apikey>` to add access apikey.
:::


## Examples

Retrieve port information for the IP addresses 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1 on ports 53/dns-udp and 443/https

```sh
x shodan scan create 8.8.8.8 1.1.1.1=53/dns-udp,443/https
```

Find the IP addresses for the provided hostnames google.com and facebook.com

```sh
x shodan dns res google.com facebook.com
```

Download information for hosts with port 22

```sh
x shodan host download port:22
```

Open Shodan's website in a browser and search for relevant information about  8.8.8.8:22

```sh
x shodan open 8.8.8.8:22
```

Crawl the Internet for a 443 port and https protocol using Shodan

```sh
x shodan scan add --protocol https --port 443
```

Open Shodan's website in a browser and search for relevant information about  8.8.8.8:22

```sh
x shodan open 8.8.8.8:22
```

Use Shodan to search for baidu.com and filter the results by the facet (dimension) "80"

```sh
x shodan search --facet 80 baidu.com
```

Find the IP addresses for the provided hostnames google.com and facebook.com

```sh
x shodan dns res google.com facebook.com
```

Ping queries to target hosts 8.8.8.8 and 4.4.4.4 from multiple geographical locations

```sh
x shodan geo geoping 8.8.8.8,4.4.4.4
```

DNS queries to the target host google.com from multiple geographical locations

```sh
x shodan geo dns google.com
```

Intertactive UI for viewing the details for a network alert

```sh
x shodan alert ls
```

Display data with termini table

```sh
x shodan alert trigger ll
```

Add the specified trigger to the specified &lt;Alert ID&gt;. This trigger will monitor port 22 of the target host 8.8.8.8.

```sh
x shodan alert trigger add <Alert ID> <trigger name> 8.8.8.8:22
```

Use Shodan to download some data related to Apple. (The default is the x_shodan_data.json file.)

```sh
x shodan download --limit 10 apple
```

Extract port information from the downloaded data and output the results in CSV format.

```sh
x shodan host csv -f x_shodan_data.json port
```

Listed US entities

```sh
x shodan entitydb ls
```

Search for information about GOOGL Inc. in the network database

```sh
x shodan entitydb search GOOGL
```

Get the number of searches each month with the search criteria being port 22

```sh
x shodan trend search port:22
```

Return a list of facets that can be used to get a breakdown of the top values for a property.

```sh
x shodan trend facets
```

LSearch for queries related to 80

```sh
x shodan query search 80
```

Get current IP

```sh
x shodan ip
```

ping 8.8.8.8

```sh
x shodan ping 8.8.8.8
```
## Introduction







### About Shodan



Shodan is a search engine, but instead of searching web pages, it searches for devices and systems connected to the internet (such as computers, servers, routers, webcams, traffic lights, smart home devices, and much more). You can think of it as the "Google" of the internet of things, but instead of websites, it focuses on devices.



Here are some of Shodan's key features:


- It reveals information about connected devices. Shodan can tell you a device's location, IP address, operating system, open ports, services it's running, and even who's running it.
- It can be used to discover security vulnerabilities. Hackers can use Shodan to find devices that are misconfigured or have known vulnerabilities, but security researchers and companies can also use it to identify and fix vulnerabilities in their own systems.
- It can provide insights into internet-connected trends. Researchers and businesses can use Shodan to track the popularity of certain types of devices, where they're located, and how they're being used.



Shodan provides a rich [API](https://developer.shodan.io/api) and [SDKs](https://developer.shodan.io/api/clients) in various languages, making it ideal for further development and use.



## Official Shodan CLI Implemented in Python



The official Shodan CLI is implemented in Python, and users can install it via pip following the [official installation instructions](https://help.shodan.io/command-line-interface/0-installation).



x-cmd also provides this package, and users can use the official Python version of `shodan` by simply running `x env use shodan` or `x env try shodan`. x-cmd will automatically prepare and manage the required Python environment, so users do not need to install Python themselves.



### Goals and Advantages of this Module



This module is a Shodan CLI implemented using POSIX shell, awk, and curl. It is lightweight (no need for Python, Node, etc. language runtimes), transparent, and easy to extend.



Leveraging the rich ecosystem of modules/packages in x-cmd, we are actively trying to integrate this module with other modules to achieve:


- Integration with data sources from OSV, CVE, CPE, CWE, etc.
- Generation of richer and more interactive Shodan reports.
- Leveraging the analytical and automation capabilities of LLMs to help users understand Shodan data more deeply.
- And more ...

# x shortcut

One-time configuration, permanent effect. Supports ash, bash, csh, dash, elvish, fish, nu, xonsh and more.

Set short names to replace long commands, like `xd` for `x docker`, `ll` for `ls -lah`.


::: tip
- Shortcuts are stored in a YAML config file and compiled to shell-specific code
- Use `x shortcut set --x-cmd <cmd>` to create x-cmd integrated shortcuts
- Use `x shortcut compile <shell>` to generate shell-specific alias code
- Use `x shortcut ls` to view all shortcuts
:::


## Examples

Set xd as shortcut for x docker

```sh
x shortcut set --x-cmd docker xd
```

Set ll as shortcut for ls -lah

```sh
x shortcut set --cmd 'ls -lah' ll
```

List all shortcuts

```sh
x shortcut ls
```

View configuration in human-readable format

```sh
x shortcut get --format human <name>
```

Delete shortcut mac

```sh
x shortcut unset mac
```

Enable shortcut mac

```sh
x shortcut enable mac
```

Disable shortcut mac

```sh
x shortcut disable mac
```

Rename shortcut m to mcli

```sh
x shortcut rename m mcli
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x shortcut set](/mod/shortcut/set.md) | Set the shortcut name and its target command string |
| [x shortcut unset](/mod/shortcut/unset.md) | Delete a shortcut |
| [x shortcut get](/mod/shortcut/get.md) | Get shortcut configuration content |
| [x shortcut cat](/mod/shortcut/cat.md) | View shortcut configuration file content |
| [x shortcut init](/mod/shortcut/init.md) | Initialize available shortcuts for current environment |
| [x shortcut ls](/mod/shortcut/ls.md) | List all shortcuts |
| [x shortcut rename](/mod/shortcut/rename.md) | Rename a shortcut |
| [x shortcut disable](/mod/shortcut/disable.md) | Disable shortcuts |
| [x shortcut enable](/mod/shortcut/enable.md) | Enable shortcuts |
| [x shortcut compile](/mod/shortcut/compile.md) | Compile shortcut configuration to shell-specific code files |
| [x shortcut default](/mod/shortcut/default.md) | Reset to use the default shortcut configuration file |
| [x shortcut default_merge](/mod/shortcut/default_merge.md) | Merge with the default shortcut configuration file |
