# Linux and MacOS

🎯 This document describes how to install `x-cmd` on `MacOS` systems and Linux distributions such as `Ubuntu`, `Debian`, `Fedora`, and `Alpine`.

After successful installation, welcome to read the [Getting Started Guide](/start/get-started.md) ~ This guide will help you quickly master x-cmd's core features, including auto-completion, theme customization, module management, and package management.

## Installing in POSIX Shell

If you are using a POSIX-compatible shell (such as `bash`, `zsh`, `ash`, `dash`), you can run the following commands directly to complete installation.

::: code-group

```sh [curl]
eval "$(curl https://get.x-cmd.com)"
```

```sh [wget]
eval "$(wget -O- https://get.x-cmd.com)"
```

:::

## Installing in Non-POSIX Shell

### Recommended Solution

It is recommended to install x-cmd in the system shell (e.g., bash), then activate support for the target Non-POSIX Shell:

```bash
# First install x-cmd
eval "$(curl https://get.x-cmd.com)"

# Activate fish support
x fish --setup

# Reopen fish to reload rc files
fish
```

### Installing Directly in Non-POSIX Shell

```bash
## Install x-cmd
curl https://get.x-cmd.com | sh -i

## Activate x-cmd support for fish shell
~/.x-cmd.root/bin/x-cmd fish --setup
```

### Related Shell Topic Documentation

- [fish](/start/fish.md)
- [elvish](/start/elvish.md)
- [nushell](/start/nushell.md)
- [xonsh](/start/xonsh.md)
- [tcsh](/start/tcsh.md)

## Installing in Linux Container Environment

For `CentOS`, `Fedora`, and Linux distributions with `curl` or `wget` pre-installed, you can use the methods described above directly.

### Special Handling for Minimal Container Environments

Some minimal Linux containers may lack necessary tools:

- `Debian`-based containers (e.g., `Debian`, `Ubuntu`) typically do not include `wget` and `curl` by default
- `Alpine` containers have `wget` built-in, but early versions may not support `https`

Therefore, we provide an installation method based on `docker cp`:

```bash
# Method 1: Run a new container and install x-cmd
x docker run -x -it <container name or id>

# Method 2: Install x-cmd for an existing container
x docker setup <container name or id>
```

- Reference: [docker module](/mod/docker.md)

# ls -- File Browsing

File browsing and management are frequent tasks. Beyond including yazi, eza, lf, and ranger, x-cmd also developed `ls` and `stat` that only depend on shell/awk, plus `ll` based on fzf.

Different tools suit different scenarios—choose based on actual needs.

## x-cmd Modules

::::ul
:::li ls module
- Only depends on shell/awk, no third-party dependencies
- Available with just the 1MB x-cmd core package
- Good for browsing deep directories like Java project source trees
:::

:::li stat module
- Only depends on shell/awk
- View detailed file status
:::

:::li ll module
- Depends on fzf (auto-downloaded)
- Good for searching and locating files in large folders
- Quick navigation with arrow keys
- Preview data using general-purpose tools (jq, yq, bat, etc.)
:::
::::

## pkg Tools

### eza

eza is the successor to exa, written in Rust, supporting multiple browsing modes.

```bash
x eza
```

```bash
x env use eza
eza
```

### yazi

```bash
x yazi
```

A terminal file manager written in Rust.

### lf

```bash
x lf
```

Or

```bash
x env use lf
lf
```

### ranger

A file manager written in Python.

## Flat File Location

- **find**: Traditional search command
- **fd**: More user-friendly find alternative
- **rg**: Recursively search file contents

## Generate Directory Trees

### tree command

```bash
x cosmo tree
```

### eza --tree

```bash
x eza --tree
x eza -T
```

## Summary

Different tools suit different scenarios:

| Scenario | Recommended Tool |
|----------|------------------|
| Lightweight browsing | ls, stat |
| Searching large file sets | ll |
| Modern listing | eza |
| Full file manager | yazi, lf, ranger |
| Directory trees | tree, eza -T |
| File finding | fd, rg |

x-cmd lowers the installation barrier, letting users choose the right tool for their scenario more freely.

# Introduction for System Operators

## Part of the Motivation for x-cmd Comes from Thinking About Operations Work

Characteristics of operations systems:

::::ul
:::li Online or Customer-Side Products
- Cannot have high invasiveness to local environments
- Try to ensure system components that are still working continue to work normally
- To reduce attack surface and deployment storage requirements, product systems are usually trimmed down
- Try not to use privileges for modifications to reduce impact
:::

:::li Scenarios Requiring Operations Intervention
- Need to troubleshoot and debug — need software tools
- Need rapid response — speed and stability are a contradiction
:::
::::

## There Are Several Contradictions Here

::::ul
:::li Rapid Response vs. System Stability
:::

:::li Trimmed Product Systems vs. Need for Rich Software Tools for Troubleshooting
:::

:::li No Privileges vs. Most Package Managers Require Privilege Installation
:::
::::

## The Key to Solving Problems Is Balancing and Planning Preparation

::::ul
:::li Product Release
Comes with a small set of operations tools
:::

:::li Operations Team
Has its own quick response toolset
:::

:::li Contingency System
Classify possible system failures in advance, establish SOP systems, even develop online operations systems
:::
::::

The above solutions require teams to continuously accumulate experience and improve — this is where your expertise shines.

## When Dedicated Systems Are Missing or Fail, Operators Need Tools

::::ul
:::li Universality
Tools that are universal, multi-platform available
:::

:::li Low Invasiveness
Doesn't significantly impact system stability, doesn't require high system invasiveness to install
:::

:::li Powerful
Multi-functional, professional
:::

:::li Simple Deployment
Small, doesn't take too much bandwidth and time during transfer
:::
::::

## busybox Is an Excellent Choice; Deeply Influenced by Its Philosophy, x-cmd Goes Further

::::ul
:::li Portability
Developed in posix shell and awk, with extremely strong portability. Script characteristics increase transparency; on-site operations engineers can easily make temporary customizations, extensions, and modifications
:::

:::li Small Size
Was once an on-demand download script of less than a hundred lines, now only 1.09 MB in size
:::

:::li No Privileges Required
Packages are installed in the user directory, no privileges needed, minimal system impact. Can download nearly 500 command-line tool software on demand, with hundreds of built-in modules. Even in trimmed alpine images, can quickly call up a large number of tools for troubleshooting
:::
::::

Operations work is complex; working efficiently amidst contradictions is like dancing with shackles. x-cmd provides a customizable general solution for scenarios where operations tools are missing. Although extensive extensions have been made for other work requirements (development scenarios, cloud scenarios, LLM), the basic design philosophy (portable, no privileges required) hasn't fundamentally changed. These non-core operations function enhancements have also expanded the reach of operations capabilities; operations engineers can try better operations workflows and combinations through these extensions.

For example, x-cmd can now access openai and gemini. How operations work can be enhanced through LLM is an interesting and worthwhile topic to explore.

url: /start/mod.md

# Modules in X-CMD

Each feature in X-CMD is packaged as a <u>module</u> in shell/awk code:

- Modules are loaded **on-demand** except for core modules
- Implemented primarily in POSIX Shell for lightweight operation
- Performance-critical features use shell wrappers around open-source binaries

Invoke modules directly via `x <module-name>`. Common modules also provide direct function calls.

::::ul
:::li Compression & Decompression: zuz module
- `x z` invokes `x zuz z` to compress files based on extension
- `x uz` extracts archives of any format
- [=> zuz docs](/mod/zuz.md)
:::

:::li Enhanced cd: cd module
- An enhanced version of cd similar to autojump and z
- `cd` invokes `x cd` for flexible directory navigation
- Set alias: `alias c='x cd'`
- [=> cd docs](/mod/cd.md)
:::

:::li Theme Switching: theme module
`x theme` to select themes, supports bash/zsh/dash/ash
- [theme module docs](/mod/theme.md)
- [theme quick start](/theme/.md)
:::

:::li Environment Management: env module
Combines nvm + pyenv + sdkman + direnv. Similar functionality to asdf but with different underlying implementation
- [env module docs](/mod/env.md)
:::

:::li Workspace Management: ws module
Provides <sup>workspace</sup> environment management with customizable environment variables and dedicated script modules
- [ws module docs](/mod/ws.md)
:::
::::

## Core Modules: env and pkg

X-CMD provides download, usage, and management for multi-version toolchains:

- **env**: Implements environment management functionality
- **pkg**: User-friendly wrapper module

X-CMD is not a comprehensive package manager. Its core goals:

1. Provide development runtimes for rapid script deployment (no sudo, no manual installation)
2. Provide common tools without requiring sudo privileges
3. Tools are cross-platform for easy cross-platform scripting

- [env](/mod/env.md) module docs
- [pkg list](/pkg/.md)

## Software Usage Patterns

::::ol
:::li Temporary Usage
`x <software-name>` downloads and executes on demand, **non-installation mode**
- Software can only be invoked via `x <software-name>`
- Quick and doesn't pollute the user environment
:::

:::li Current Environment Install
`x env try jq` installs jq in the current environment
- Can be invoked directly with `jq`
- Modifies current shell environment variables without affecting other shells
:::

:::li Global Install
`x env use jq` for global installation
- Binaries added to x-cmd's bin directory
- Automatically added to `$PATH`, available in all shells
:::
::::

::: warning Environment Variable Exceptions
Some software requires additional environment variables after installation, such as older Java versions needing `JAVA_HOME`.

- Environment variables are loaded only in current shell and newly started shells
- Other shells need restart or use `x env boot java`
:::

## More Modules

[=> Module list](/mod/.md) contains commonly used stable modules. Unlisted modules are also available but documentation is pending and features may change.

## FAQ

Approximately 200 modules are currently in development. Due to limited resources, only essential modules are published.

<h1 class="visually-hidden">Nushell</h1>

## Overview

Nushell is a Rust-powered shell providing a modern user interface and powerful data processing capabilities. The x-cmd toolkit integrates with Nushell to enhance its functionality and user experience.

## Installing x-cmd

::::ol
:::li One-Line Installation
Download and install x-cmd in Nushell using curl or wget:

```bash
curl https://get.x-cmd.com | sh
```

or

```bash
wget -O- https://get.x-cmd.com | sh
```
:::

:::li Activating Existing x-cmd Installation
If x-cmd is already installed but commands are not found in Nushell:

```sh
sh -c '. "$HOME/.x-cmd.root/X"; x upgrade latest; x nu --setup'
nu
```
:::
::::

## Theme Customization

While x-cmd's [theme module](/mod/theme.md) only supports POSIX shells, you can easily use ohmyposh and starship themes through x-cmd:

```bash
x starship
```

```bash
x ohmyposh
```

x-cmd provides dedicated [starship](/mod/starship.md) and [ohmyposh](/mod/ohmyposh.md) modules with automatic installation, configuration, and theme preview features. Unified theme control commands let you easily set your preferred theme.

## How `x nu --setup` Works

When running `x nu --setup`, a startup line is added to `$HOME/.config/nushell/env.nu`:

```
const ___X_CMD_ROOT = '$HOME/.x-cmd.root'; source $"($___X_CMD_ROOT)/local/data/nu/rc.nu"; # boot up x-cmd
```

This line:
- Imports enhanced functions
- Adds PATH entries
- Includes the marker comment `# boot up x-cmd.` at the end

:::tip Configuration Recommendation
If you install tools through x-cmd (such as starship, asdf) that require activation or configuration in env.nu, add your configuration code **after** the x-cmd activation code.
:::

## FAQ

:::details Support Status {open}
1. **Supports pixi installation and automatic activation**

2. **@-prefixed alias support**
   - Aliases starting with @ are mainly used for LLM modules (such as @gpt, @gemini, @o in the chat module, and @zh, @en in the writer module)
   - Since Nushell does not support @-prefixed aliases, writer module aliases are provided as `a:en`, `a:zh` instead
   - Currently, aliases cannot be disabled at startup via `x boot alias disable [c|xx|xw|xd|xg|xp|co|coco|chat|writer]` in Nushell

**Note**: The above support is currently in Beta.
:::

:::details Current Issues {open}
**Pipe issue**: When attempting to wrap x commands in functions to access Nushell environment variables, handling and detecting pipes becomes problematic. Therefore, the current x command disables environment variables and uses file-based passing instead to ensure pipes work correctly.
:::

# Performance

X-CMD's performance goals aim to balance functionality and efficiency:

::::ul
:::li Embedded System Compatibility
Ensures smooth operation on resource-constrained embedded Linux systems (such as Raspberry Pi 3/4), providing good user experience. This is the primary goal.
:::

:::li Fast Loading
Goals for quick startup:
- Full load time in interactive environments does not exceed 150ms
- Script environments do not exceed 30ms
- Ideally, 45ms and 15ms respectively on MacBook M3
:::
::::

Currently, embedded system testing is mainly conducted on Raspberry Pi 3/4 with relatively limited resources. After product stabilization, performance will be continuously optimized. X-CMD's goal is to run stably on various Linux embedded devices and provide a good CLI experience.

## Git-Bash Performance Issues and Mitigation Strategies

Git Bash's subshell implementation has efficiency issues, particularly affecting [theme module](/mod/theme.md) theme rendering. Adaptations have been made to address this issue to ensure user experience.

::::ul
:::li Upgrade Git Bash
Using newer versions of Git Bash (Bash 5 and above) can effectively improve performance because new features reduce dependency on external commands.
:::
::::

The [theme module](/mod/theme.md) provides oh-my-zsh-like theme functionality, but theme rendering and terminal UI display on Git-Bash may still experience slight lag in resource-limited hardware environments.

Although WSL2 provides a better running environment and Windows resource interoperability, providing direct running solutions for native systems remains crucial. Continuous improvements will be made to provide a smoother experience for Git Bash users.

# X-CMD PKG Introduction and Comparison

In addition to fully leveraging the powerful capabilities of POSIX Shell, AWK, and a series of Unix pre-installed tools, X-CMD modules use numerous powerful external tools (such as jq, yq, jj, fzf, etc.).

We aim to directly solve the download and installation of these external tool dependencies in a secure, minimal environmental impact way; rather than leaving these dependency installations to users, and certainly not wanting to trouble root users.

During the recent three years of development, multiple mainstream solutions have been researched. The following comparisons are not meant to conclude superiority or inferiority, but only to introduce pkg's design philosophy and applicable scenarios.

## Characteristics/Design Philosophy of [`x pkg`](/pkg/.md)

<!-- > [pkg Metadata Introduction](/pkg/meta.md) · [pkg Software Sources](/pkg/source.md) · [pkg Implementation Details](/pkg/impl.md) -->

::::ul
:::li Cross-Platform Support
Available on Windows, Linux, MacOS (BSD-like system support to be added later)
:::

:::li Streamlined pkg Count and Versions
Saving effort to implement more supply chain monitoring:

- Minimize count while covering mainstream development and system operation scenarios
- Minimize software versions while covering actively maintained mainstream versions
- Software and versions not covered by pkg are met by introducing other ecosystems
:::

:::li Reduce Overhead
Lower overhead of download size, load time, and startup time
:::

:::li Minimize Environment Changes
Minimize changes to the environment; if changes are unavoidable, explicitly state them to avoid introducing surprises that may cause bugs (No surprise).
:::
::::

## [`x pkg`](/pkg/.md) vs System Package Managers

System package managers refer to apt, dnf/yum, pacman, etc., provided by system distribution vendors.

::::ul
:::li Advantages of System Package Management
1. Relatively stable and reliable, highest integration with the operating system
2. x-cmd has already enhanced daily use in module form: [apt](/mod/apt.md)/[yum](/mod/yum.md)/[dnf](/mod/dnf.md)/[pacman](/mod/pacman.md)
:::
::::

### Limitations of System Package Management

::::ul
:::li Requires Root Privileges
- In production-level operation scenarios, root privileges are sometimes not available, or their use is discouraged
- Updating software A may incidentally update a series of system dependencies B, C, D, and these dependency updates may cause existing software to malfunction, increasing variables that disrupt system stability
- In operation scenarios, software issues caused by system dependency updates have been observed, unfortunately occurring during delivery or customer demo sites
- It's not worth risking system dependency changes for a jq, fzf, or traceroute
- High risk leads to low work efficiency
:::

:::li Old System Versions
Taking fzf as an example, the latest version on October 9, 2024 is <u>0.55.0</u>:

| System | fzf Version |
|--------|-------------|
| ubuntu 22.04 (LTS, supported until 2027) | 0.29.0 |
| ubuntu 24.04 | 0.44.1 |

- Updates for different software in differently positioned system distributions are the result of scenario positioning and release/review cost trade-offs
- Different usage scenarios require different most suitable installation methods; accommodating this diversity brings usage costs, [x install](/install/.md) exists to reduce this cost
- Too old software versions reduce work efficiency and cause users to encounter known bugs
- Inconsistency causes many potential bugs and usage issues: unsupported parameters in intermediate tools in scripts, unknown parameter errors encountered by users, difficult-to-reproduce failures caused by parameter expiration
:::
::::

### Summary

The above tool details are not where you want to spend time at work. x-cmd pkg, by simply occupying HOME directory space, can:

- Keep tool versions consistent at a given time
- Use newer version features under safe conditions
- Minimize encountering known bugs in old versions

## [`x pkg`](/pkg/.md) vs nix | brew

1. Not available on Windows
2. Although root is not needed for use, installation requires root
3. Operations personnel do not have root privileges, or are required to minimize root usage to reduce impact on system dependencies; therefore naturally cannot install nix and brew in operation target environments
4. Installation overhead is quite large, not suitable for use in small containers

## [`x pkg`](/pkg/.md) vs [pixi](/mod/pixi.md) | [asdf](/mod/asdf.md) | [pkgx](/mod/pkgx.md)

| feature | pixi | [`x pkg`](/pkg/.md) | asdf |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Development Language | rust | posix shell | bash |
| Release compressed size and dependencies | 10MB | less than 1.5MB | 3.3MB |
| Total software | 30000+ | 600+ | 800+ |
| alpine container | Many common tools cannot run | Except for极少数 (jíshǎoshù) tools, all can run | Cannot run, requires bash and git installation |
| Ecosystem maintenance | conda, commercial and community | x-cmd team | community |

### Comparison Notes

::::ul
:::li Alpine Indicator
- Heavy users of Alpine containers, therefore applicability within Alpine containers is a key design indicator
- Theoretically, container users should not directly enter containers for operations; but in actual testing and development scenarios, this need is hard to avoid
:::

:::li Pixi
- Pixi based on conda ecosystem: large quantity, high quality
- Developed with Rust: excellent in size, startup efficiency, and user experience
- Pixi's current biggest problem is that many common tools cannot be used on Alpine (such as jq)
- Conda ecosystem not available on OpenBSD, FreeBSD, NetBSD; which has always been x-cmd pkg's goal
- x-cmd currently views pixi as complementary to pkg: some x-cmd modules use tools on pixi, such as [btop](/mod/btop.md), [htop](/mod/htop.md), these packages and tools are not introduced in x-cmd pkg
:::

:::li pkgx
- Great tool, initiated by Brew's developer, developed with Typescript
- Total packages around 1500+
- Biggest problem: cannot be used on Windows and Alpine
- Provides pkgx module to help interested users quickly install and enable, with added TUI
:::
::::

### Complementarity with the Above Ecosystems and Development Guidelines

The software in this section is closest to x-cmd pkg's target scenarios and design philosophy. Future development guidelines:

1. Control pkg's management scope; software perfectly covered by pixi/conda and pkgx will not be introduced by pkg under the premise of point 2 below
2. Reduce user choice costs:
   - Strengthen [x install](/install/.md), unify tool/package names, all installation methods at a glance
   - Through module packaging, comprehensively evaluate and use the best, fastest, and safest usage methods
   - Unless there are significant factors such as system environment impact or security, try not to let users纠结 (jiūjié) whether package xx is better using pkg, pixi, or pkgx

### asdf

**With asdf as a shining example, why develop x-cmd pkg**

::::ul
:::li Bash Dependency
asdf is developed in bash and requires bash in the environment
:::

:::li Git Dependency
asdf installation depends on git:

- asdf is oriented toward development scenarios, so depending on git is a technically reasonable decision
- x-cmd assumes operation scenarios:
  - Git is rarely pre-installed on operation machines - the assumed minimal environment is Alpine image
  - In 2022, no portable git solution or mature alternative was found - until the jj project and pixi project emerged; currently [asdf module](/mod/asdf.md) solves the git dependency problem based on this
  - To install a tool software possibly less than <u>1MB</u> by downloading and installing <u>40MB+</u> of git, this overhead is quite large
:::

:::li Network Issues
asdf's metadata is managed by git, and many software package download addresses are outside China; therefore it is difficult to accelerate network for China region.
:::
::::

**x-cmd provides [asdf module](/mod/asdf.md)** to enhance asdf usage experience

1. Provides TUI for users to browse and install packages/tools interactively
2. When local environment has no git, x-cmd uses pkg to download jj to replace asdf's git dependency:
   - Does not install jj to reduce environmental impact
   - If you need to use jj directly in the current environment, you can use `x env try jj`; if you need to install in current user space, you can use `x env use jj`
3. Once the asdf module is activated, x-cmd automatically loads asdf configuration, users no longer need to manage asdf startup code in shell configuration files

**Unique Value of asdf**

asdf's internal implementation uses nvm/rbenv/pyenv, so it can recognize their configuration files:

- The above tools have accumulated a large number of developer users
- x-cmd's env tool does not兼容 (jiānróng) such configuration files; asdf will be a worry-free and effective all-in-one tool
- Currently, x-cmd does not use asdf's packages and tools except in the asdf module

:::details Other Usage Methods {open}
1. Directly use `x install asdf` to install asdf
2. If the environment lacks git that asdf depends on, x-cmd will install git through its own package management system without affecting the global environment
3. Designed asdf module, directly use `x asdf`, if asdf module is not locally available, it will automatically trigger official asdf installation
:::

## Other Interesting Directions

::::ul
:::li wasm
- Closely monitoring wasm progress
- x-cmd has added [wasmer](/pkg/wasmer.md), [wasmedge](/pkg/wasmedge.md), [wasmtime](/pkg/wasmtime.md)
- Current wasm runtime size is not small, and startup and runtime are still差强人意 (chāqiángrényì - barely satisfactory)
- Cross-platform unified security model is wasm's most important highlight - looking forward to this
:::

:::li cosmo
[cosmo](/mod/cosmo.md) is developed by legendary engineer [Justine Tunney](https://justine.lol), an amazing and highly complete project that has risen in recent years.

Recently added同名 (tóngmíng) module:
- Integrates some functions to solve common problems when using cosmo system
- Automatic download, and provides solutions for global and system installation of cosmo applications
- Provides TUI interactive application and command completion

Current [cosmo](/mod/cosmo.md) ecosystem provides more than 100 common tool software.
:::

:::li Containers and Isolation Technologies
Containers (docker, podman, bwrap) and chroot/proot:
- These tools and technologies are excellent, but can only be used on Linux
- Continuously monitoring rootless container
- x-cmd has demonstrated the power of these tools in modules
:::
::::

## Use [x install](/install/.md) Module to Choose All Above Installation Methods

1. Initially to collect all `curl | sh` form official installation scripts to avoid frequent searches for corresponding software official websites to copy and paste
2. Later planned to unify names of all common software that these tools can install (not all), then integrate into install module
3. Directly use `x install <software-name>` to install software
4. During installation, lists suitable installation methods for current system, users choose appropriate method
5. Workload is substantial, gradually being organized

- [Submit New pkg](/pkg/submit.md)

## FAQ

:::details Core Goals of x-cmd {open}
Many friends know x-cmd because it can download hundreds of software tools, but this is not x-cmd's essence and core goal.

1. Provide a small and robust posix-shell library that can be used in most current posix-shell environments
2. Based on 1, develop some traditional command lightweight encapsulations to enhance user experience
3. Allow users to deploy their or teammates' python/js scripts with one click, automatically solving download and dependency problems

At 2 and 3, encountered binary missing needing installation problems respectively. Solutions at project initiation two years ago:

1. If tools can be solved with shell and awk scripts, try to write modules to replace
2. Early provided statically compiled binaries, planned to carefully select 50 powerful and representative binaries, specially designed static-build module for this
3. As count increased, and static-build could not meet more needs, had to try developing pkg module two years ago
:::

:::details Package Management on Windows — scoop, winget, choco {open}
- Can only be used on Windows
- x-cmd has encapsulated corresponding modules, added completion and TUI interface
:::

:::details Summary {open}
1. x-cmd pkg's goal is to provide official security and source review, and provide binary software installation in a transparent way (github, npm)
   - x-cmd didn't want to do package management originally, but because it needs to install tools in minimal environment with minimal invasion (only depends on minimal basic posix command environment), pkg was designed with this goal
   - x-cmd/pkg never thought about replacing any existing third-party package management tools, let alone system package management tools
   - x-cmd pkg has 500 software, though still planning to increase, does not intend to become an all-round package management tool - only provides packages符合 (fúhé) x-cmd user scenarios and needs
   - Now pkg has another goal, to provide more行动力 (xíngdònglì) from open-source software for x-cmd's LLM module
2. x-cmd's technical essence is a bunch of shell libraries, so it uses `x <mod>` form to encapsulate and enhance existing package management tools, such as adding local and remote package information viewing and interaction, using open-source security intelligence (osv, kve, shodan) and tools (osv-scanner, grype) for vulnerability prevention, quickly setting proxy and switching mirrors:
   - System package management: [apt](/mod/apt.md), [yum](/mod/yum.md), [dnf](/mod/dnf.md), [pacman](/mod/pacman.md) ...
   - Development tool management: [asdf](/mod/asdf.md)
   - Third-party package management: [brew](/mod/brew.md), [scoop](/mod/scoop.md)
   - wasm system: [wasmer](/pkg/wasmer.md), [wasmedge](/pkg/wasmedge.md), [wasmtime](/pkg/wasmtime.md), etc.
   - [cosmo](/mod/cosmo.md) system
3. [install](/install/.md):
   - Initially to collect all `curl | sh` form official installation scripts
   - Now plans to unify names of all common software that these tools can install, integrate into install module
:::

# The pkg Module and Its Ecosystem

The initial goal was simple: quickly use common small tools in minimal system environments without privileged permissions.

As requirements grew, functionality expanded:

::::ul
:::li Multi-version Management
Supports switching between multiple versions of tools, comparable to asdf
:::

:::li Plugin Dependencies
Supports SQLite plugin-style dependencies
:::

:::li Dynamic Dependencies
Supports dynamic dependencies as an alternative to static compilation
:::

:::li Language Ecosystem Tools
Supports tools from pip/npm
:::
::::

Currently 500+ tools are indexed. The team faces significant maintenance pressure.

## Core Principles

::::ol
:::li Security & Trustworthiness
- Official project binaries have highest priority
- Self-compilation as secondary option
- Remain cautious of non-systematic third-party sources
:::

:::li No Duplication of Existing Work
- System-level software provided by system package managers
- Complex configuration applications use container images
- Integrate asdf module to supplement missing packages
- [install](/mod/install.md) module organizes all installation methods
:::

:::li Letting Go
- Abandon projects with discontinued maintenance or perfect alternatives
- Reduce cognitive burden on users
- Incorrectly added entries are removed without affecting usage
:::
::::

## Positioning Statement

Consider pkg as a **downloader for common tools and development environments**, not a package manager.

| Scenario | Recommended Solution |
|----------|---------------------|
| Serious production environments | Native system package manager |
| Applications with complex configuration | Container approach |
| Quick tool trial | `x <software-name>` |
| Development environment management | `x env` |

Additional tools will be added as needed. Priority: Security > Stability > Availability

<h1 class="visually-hidden">PowerShell</h1>

## Overview

[PowerShell](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/scripting/overview?view=powershell-7.4) is Microsoft's cross-platform command line interface and scripting language environment. Originally designed for system administration, it has expanded into a general-purpose tool supporting Windows, macOS, and Linux. This article describes how to integrate x-cmd into PowerShell on the Windows platform.

## Installing x-cmd

Currently, using x-cmd in `PowerShell` requires calling through `Git-Bash`. Ensure Git Bash is installed on your system and x-cmd is properly installed in the Git Bash environment.

::::ol
:::li Method 1: One-Line Installation (Recommended)
Execute the following PowerShell command, and x-cmd will automatically download, install, and configure:

```powershell
[System.Text.Encoding]::GetEncoding("utf-8").GetString($(Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://get.x-cmd.com/x-cmd.ps1").RawContentStream.ToArray()) | Invoke-Expression
```

This command will automatically download Git Bash and x-cmd as needed, and execute `x pwsh --setup` to complete configuration.
:::

:::li Method 2: Manual Configuration Using Git Bash
Execute in Git Bash:

```bash
x pwsh --setup
```
:::
::::

:::info Important: PowerShell Execution Policy
PowerShell's default execution policy may be Restricted, which does not allow running any scripts (including configuration files), preventing x-cmd from working properly.

Use `Get-ExecutionPolicy -List` to check the current execution policy. It is recommended to use `Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser` to set the execution policy, allowing scripts from trusted sources to run.

For more information, see [PowerShell Execution Policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_execution_policies?view=powershell-7.4) and [Set-ExecutionPolicy Documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.security/set-executionpolicy?view=powershell-7.4).
:::

## Theme Customization

Although [x-cmd theme](/mod/theme.md) only supports POSIX shells, you can achieve stunning visual effects in PowerShell through [Oh My Posh](https://ohmyposh.dev/) and [starship](https://starship.rs):

```bash
x starship
```

```bash
x ohmyposh
```

x-cmd's [ohmyposh](/mod/ohmyposh.md) and [starship](/mod/starship.md) modules provide theme previews and unified control commands. After installation and activation, the theme loads automatically when PowerShell starts, no additional configuration needed.

## How `x pwsh --setup` Works

`x pwsh --setup` adds the following to the PowerShell profile:

```powershell
if (Test-Path "$Home\.x-cmd.root\local\data\pwsh\_index.ps1") { Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process; . "$Home\.x-cmd.root\local\data\pwsh\_index.ps1" };  # boot up x-cmd.
```

This code automatically loads the `_index.ps1` file when PowerShell starts. See [`x pwsh setup` code](https://github.com/x-cmd/x-cmd/blob/main/mod/pwsh/lib/__setup#L4) and [x-cmd source](https://github.com/x-cmd/x-cmd/blob/main/mod/pwsh/lib/rc/_index.ps1) for more details.

:::info
`Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process` sets the current process permission level to `Bypass`, ensuring scripts execute smoothly.
:::

## FAQ

:::details Configuration Recommendation {open}
If you install other tools through x-cmd (such as fzf, asdf), additional configuration may be required in the profile file according to those tools' requirements. It is recommended to add custom configuration code **after** the x-cmd startup code.
:::

:::details Using @ Commands {open}
Due to the special meaning of `@` in PowerShell, some x-cmd commands (such as `@gpt`, `@gemini`) have been changed to `a:gpt`, `a:gemini` in the PowerShell environment.
:::

If you have any questions, feel free to [provide feedback](/start/community.md) at the [x-cmd source repository](https://github.com/x-cmd/x-cmd).

# X-CMD Runtime Modes on POSIX and Non-POSIX Shells

🎯 This document describes how x-cmd runs on shells like `dash`, `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, `nushell`, and `elvish`.

## POSIX Shell

x-cmd uses POSIX-compatible shell syntax to run on most systems in the lightest and most efficient way.

:::tip About POSIX Standards
This document uses the distinction between POSIX Shell and Non-POSIX Shell as an easy-to-understand explanation for users, without delving into POSIX standard specifications.
:::

During development, x-cmd aims to leverage the commonalities of mainstream POSIX Shell implementations. For example, the `local` keyword, while not part of the POSIX standard, is supported by most POSIX Shells except `KSH AJM 93` (a ksh variant). Therefore, to improve engineering capabilities and runtime efficiency, x-cmd widely uses `local` and abandons the possibility of running as a library on KSH AJM 93.

## Two Runtime Modes

::::ul
:::li Library Function Mode
Run x-cmd directly as functions in the shell.

**Advantages:**
- **Low startup overhead**: x-cmd code executes directly in the current shell process without spawning additional processes
- **Convenient state sharing**: Changes made by x-cmd application modules can be passed directly via shell variables without inter-process communication
:::

:::li External Command Mode
Launch a `POSIX Shell` as the runtime to use x-cmd.

For `Non-POSIX Shells`, since they cannot directly run x-cmd code, the system shell is used to call x-cmd as an external command.

**Actual Experience:**
- The system shell (/bin/sh) starts and runs very fast. x-cmd is organized with strict lazy loading, resulting in minimal latency
- Most x-cmd use cases are TUI applications (such as `x ollama`, `x gh`, `x ls`), which work fully in external command mode
- Compared to network latency, process startup overhead is negligible
:::
::::

## POSIX Shell -- Default Library Function Mode

In bash, dash, ash, and zsh, x-cmd runs in **Library Function Mode** by default.

::::ul
:::li Bash
`Bash` is the most common `POSIX Shell`, widely used in Linux and Unix-like environments.

**Bash 4/5**
- Mainstream Linux distributions and WSL provide Bash 4 or Bash 5 by default
- `Git for Windows` has used Bash 5 by default since 2023
- Bash in the `cosmo` ecosystem is also Bash 5

**Bash 3**
- MacOS's default `/bin/sh` is still based on Bash 3. Due to GPLv3 license restrictions, it's unlikely to be upgraded soon
- x-cmd has made corresponding workarounds and adaptations in the code
:::

:::li Zsh
Both MacOS and Kali Linux ship with `zsh` as the default login shell, offering powerful interactive capabilities and rich extension features.

zsh behaves differently from bash, ash, and dash in several ways. x-cmd adapts to these differences by leveraging strengths and avoiding weaknesses.
:::

:::li Dash
Debian and its derivative distributions (Ubuntu, Kali, Manjaro, etc.) use `dash` as `/bin/sh` by default. dash is a typical lightweight shell that runs extremely fast but lacks some advanced features.
:::

:::li Ash
The default shell for `BusyBox` and `Alpine`, widely used in Docker and lightweight Linux distributions. It's the preferred shell for minimal Linux systems.
:::
::::

## Non-POSIX Shell -- Default External Command Mode

x-cmd supports the following shells in **External Command Mode**, with adjustments made for each shell's design characteristics:

::::ul
:::li [nushell](/start/nushell.md)
Uses data-driven pipeline design with excellent data processing capabilities that align well with x-cmd's data flow philosophy.
:::
:::li [elvish](/start/elvish.md)
A functional shell with `Lisp`-style syntax, unique and innovative.
:::
:::li [xonsh](/start/xonsh.md)
A shell that combines Python syntax, offering both shell features and direct Python code execution.
:::
:::li [fish](/start/fish.md)
Excellent design trade-offs, providing rich completions and efficient interactive experience by default.
:::
:::li [tcsh](/start/tcsh.md)
FreeBSD's default login shell, featuring word-based data stream processing.
:::
:::li [powershell](/start/powershell.md)
Windows' pre-installed shell with support for object pipeline passing. Learn more about [modules](/mod/.md)
:::
::::

## FAQ

:::details Ksh Support Status {open}
x-cmd currently has limited support for Ksh (KornShell), particularly PD Ksh (OpenBSD's default shell).

- Due to Ksh 93's lack of `local` keyword support, compatibility issues significantly impact the codebase, so it's not a priority for support in the short term
- KSH AJM 93u has function variable scope issues, making library mode support unlikely, though external command mode compatibility is possible
- OpenBSD has not been fully tested, and the PKG system has not been ported to OpenBSD or FreeBSD, so PD Ksh adaptation is not currently prioritized

If you have requirements, please [submit an issue or email feedback](/start/community.md).
:::

# Startup Analysis

## Loading Process

x-cmd is installed in the `$HOME/.x-cmd.root/` directory.

::::ol
:::li Shell Configuration File Loading
Interactive bash loads `$HOME/.bash_profile` or `$HOME/.bashrc`, which contains:
```bash
[ ! -f "$HOME/.x-cmd.root/X" ] || . "$HOME/.x-cmd.root/X" # boot up x-cmd.
```
:::

:::li X Startup File
`$HOME/.x-cmd.root/X` sets the version and locates the code directory:
- Sets the default version `___X_CMD_VERSION_DEFAULT=latest`
- Sets `___X_CMD_ROOT` to point to the specific installation directory based on the version
:::

:::li Version Directory Structure
- latest, alpha, beta, v1, etc. point to 8-digit hexadecimal version directories
- The X file in the source folder loads the xrc module
- The hexadecimal version number is generated by the core code to precisely describe the version
:::
::::

## xrc Module

The xrc module handles the actual feature loading:

::::ul
:::li Base Loading
Loads necessary functions and code
:::

:::li Configuration Loading
Loads user configuration files
:::

:::li Interactive Environment Initialization
- Loads command completion features
- Configures aliases
- Loads and configures the theme module
:::
::::

# Please Support Us

## About Us

The X-CMD development team was established in 2021, dedicated to X-CMD development and ecosystem building. We are a group of developers passionate about technology, hoping to create a truly useful tool to help everyone improve efficiency.

We chose POSIX-SHELL not because we don't understand other languages (such as Rust, Go, Python, TypeScript, C), on the contrary, since 2018, predecessors of X-CMD have tried these solutions. I also have plans to gradually adopt features of other languages in appropriate parts and scenarios of X-CMD to enhance functionality and performance.

The final choice of POSIX-SHELL was a carefully considered trade-off: it has extensive runtime environments, extremely high startup efficiency, transparent code, and comprehensive advantages in I/O time-consuming scenarios.

`TypeScript` (similar to npx)

`Golang` (for startup efficiency)

`C/Rust` (for size and startup efficiency)

`Bash` (merging x-bash project)
:::
:::li ~ Now
`POSIX-SHELL` (exploring and挖掘 (wājué) POSIX-SHELL limits in performance and functionality, finalized after multiple rewrites and comparisons)

# Installing x-cmd via System Package Manager

x-cmd can be installed through the system's built-in package manager.

:::warning
The method of installing `x-cmd` via system package manager is still experimental. Please use with caution.
:::

## Characteristics of System Package Manager Installation

1. x-cmd is designed to work without privileges, so it is installed only in the current user's user space by default. The current version has not yet implemented multi-user data sharing. For `x-cmd` instances installed via system package manager, each user needs to activate and configure separately.

2. Although `x-cmd` can be called as an external command, its advantage lies in deep customization and integration with the interactive shell. Loading `x-cmd` at shell startup maximizes the advantages of modules (faster startup speed, automatic environment variable modification, etc.).

## Installation Process and Principles

Installing `x-cmd` via package manager essentially places a stable version of `x-cmd` source code in a globally readable directory (e.g., `/usr/share/x-cmd`) and places an executable bin script named `x-cmd` in `/usr/bin`.

Since system package manager installation is not suitable for modifying specific user's HOME directory, after successful installation, the user needs to explicitly call the `x-cmd` command to complete activation. This step will copy the source code from `/usr/share/x-cmd` to the user's `$HOME/.x-cmd.root` directory.

:::tip Why use copying instead of symlinks?
To avoid code missing or version inconsistency issues in the user environment when the system package manager upgrades or removes `x-cmd` in the future. This method ensures the independence and stability of each user environment.
:::

<!-- :::info About Versions
Due to submission review cycles, the x-cmd version in system package managers may be an older stable version (usually 5-10 minor versions behind). Users can upgrade to the latest version using `x upgrade` after activation.
::: -->

## Currently Supported System Package Managers

::::ol
:::li Step 1: Select package manager installation based on system

| System Package Manager | Installation Command |
|-------------|---------|
| homebrew | `brew install x-cmd` |
| aur | `yay -S x-cmd` or `paru -S x-cmd` |
| apt ⏳ | `sudo apt install x-cmd` |
| apk ⏳ | `sudo apk add x-cmd` |
| dnf ⏳ | `sudo dnf install x-cmd` |
| pacman ⏳ | `sudo pacman -Sy x-cmd` |

⏳ = Waiting for community review
:::

:::li Step 2: Activate in current user environment after successful installation
```bash
x-cmd
```

The activation command will install `x-cmd` to the user directory (`$HOME/.x-cmd.root`) and configure the shell environment.

**Please be sure to execute this step!**
:::

:::li Step 3: (Optional) Configure non-POSIX shell

Step 2 will not automatically configure loading for non-POSIX shells. Users need to explicitly set:

| Non-POSIX Shell | Configuration Command |
|---------------|---------|
| fish | `x-cmd fish --setup` |
| elvish | `x-cmd elv --setup` |
| nushell | `x-cmd nu --setup` |
| xonsh | `x-cmd onsh --setup` |
| csh | `x-cmd csh --setup` |

If the shell has already loaded x-cmd, you can directly use `x` instead of `x-cmd`.
:::
::::

## Future Development Directions

::::ul
:::li Multi-user shared x-cmd source code
The current system installation and activation strategy is very conservative, with stability and availability as primary goals. x-cmd source code is small (only 1.5MB gzipped), so storage optimization needs are not significant.
:::
:::li Shared [x-cmd pkg](/pkg.md) to avoid duplicate downloads (High Priority)
1. **Primary optimization -- Network**: Prioritize optimizing the download cache sharing mechanism between users to avoid duplicate downloads of installation packages. Use strict hash verification to prevent user cache tampering or spoofing.
2. **Secondary optimization -- Storage**: Consider using symlinks or hard links to achieve sharing of software installations between multiple users. This requires users to use privilege mode or specific users/groups to manage shared software space.
:::
::::

## FAQ

:::details Why support system package manager installation when there is already an install script? {open}

System package managers better fit the habits of distribution users, naturally integrate into the system's software management workflow, and unify installation, upgrade, uninstallation, and version management. They are also more suitable for Docker, CI/CD, and enterprise environments. In addition, system package managers provide system-level installation: install once for all users on the system. Therefore, supporting system package managers is not meant to replace the install script, but to help x-cmd better integrate into the ecosystem of each distribution.

:::

:::details Cannot use `x` command after installation? {open}
Please ensure that you have executed the `x-cmd` command to activate in the current user.

If it still doesn't work, please check whether your shell configuration file (e.g., `.bashrc`, `.zshrc`, etc.) is correctly configured with x-cmd environment variables and shell functions. You can try restarting the shell or manually sourcing your shell configuration file.
:::

<!-- :::details System package manager installed `x-cmd` version is too old? {open}
The `x-cmd` version in system package managers usually lags slightly behind the latest stable version. After activating `x-cmd`, you can use the `x upgrade` command to upgrade to the latest version.

Note that this will only upgrade the `x-cmd` version in the current user directory; the version in the system global directory remains the old version.
::: -->

:::details How to uninstall `x-cmd` installed via system package manager? {open}
Use the corresponding package manager command to uninstall `x-cmd`. For example, systems using `apt` can use the `sudo apt remove x-cmd` command to uninstall.

After uninstallation, you may need to manually delete the `$HOME/.x-cmd.root` directory and clean up configurations related to `x-cmd` in shell configuration files.
:::

:::details Why is it necessary to copy `x-cmd` source code to the user directory? {open}
As mentioned above, this is to avoid affecting the user's `x-cmd` environment when the system package manager upgrades or removes `x-cmd`. Copying source code ensures the independence and stability of each user's `x-cmd` environment.
:::

:::details What is the difference between system package manager installation and manual installation? {open}
The main differences lie in installation location and version management:
- System package manager installation installs `x-cmd` to the system global directory and manages versions via the system package manager
- Manual installation installs `x-cmd` to the user directory and manages versions by the user
- System package manager installation requires manual user activation, while manual installation usually completes activation automatically
:::

<h1 class="visually-hidden">tcsh</h1>

## Overview

tcsh is a C shell with programmable command line completion, command line editing, and other features. The x-cmd toolkit integrates with tcsh to enhance its functionality and user experience.

## Installing x-cmd

::::ol
:::li Using curl
Download and install x-cmd in tcsh using curl:

```sh
curl https://get.x-cmd.com | sh
tcsh
```
:::

:::li Using wget
Download and install x-cmd in tcsh using wget:

```sh
wget -O- https://get.x-cmd.com | sh
tcsh
```
:::

:::li Activating Existing x-cmd Installation
If x-cmd is already installed but commands are not found in tcsh, run the following command to activate:

```sh
sh -c '. "$HOME/.x-cmd.root/X"; x upgrade latest; x tcsh --setup'
tcsh
```
:::
::::

## FAQ

:::details Support Status {open}
**Supported Systems/Environments:** Linux, MacOS, WSL, Cygwin, MSYS2 (such as Gitbash)

**Tools Provided by x-cmd:**
- [Common command wrappers](/mod/zuz.md): cd, ip, ps, tar, apt, brew, etc., smarter than native commands
- [Lightweight package management](/pkg/.md): Implemented in shell and awk for quickly obtaining common software
- [Practical website CLI](/mod/cht.md): API wrappers for github.com, cht.sh, etc.
- [AI tools](/mod/openai.md): CLI for ChatGPT/Gemini/Jina.ai, etc.

**Note**: The above support is currently in Beta.
:::

# Supported Terminals

x-cmd is designed for cross-platform command-line environments. Its core features work independently of graphical components or specific terminal capabilities. As long as the terminal emulator supports the VT100 standard, you can use x-cmd's main commands without additional configuration.

::::ul
:::li No Dependencies for Basic Features
Whether using macOS's built-in Terminal.app, Linux tty, or Windows PowerShell, x-cmd runs its basic commands in all these environments.
:::

:::li Icon and Character Support
Certain modules or integrated third-party tools (like `x theme`, `lsd`, `starship`, etc.) use icons to enhance the user experience and depend on special fonts such as [Nerd Fonts](/start/font.md). If the terminal is not properly configured, icons may display as garbled characters or question marks.

Installing and enabling fonts with icon extensions ([font configuration](/start/font.md)) is recommended, especially for the following tools:
- **File listing tools**: Such as [lsd](/pkg/lsd.md), which uses icons to distinguish directories, files, and symbolic links
- **Terminal prompt themes**: Such as [x theme](/mod/theme.md), [starship](/mod/starship.md), [ohmyposh](/mod/ohmyposh.md)
:::

:::li Image Display Support
x-cmd is compatible with tools that can preview images directly in the terminal (such as [yazi](/pkg/yazi.md)). These tools rely on terminal support for the **Sixel graphics protocol** or similar graphic extensions.

Not all terminals currently support Sixel. Using a terminal with image display capabilities is recommended to enable such advanced features.
:::
::::

## Third-Party Terminals

Here are some popular third-party terminal emulators we have tested:

| Terminal  | Platform             | Sixel Image Support | Notes                                  |
|-----------|----------------------|---------------------|----------------------------------------|
| Alacritty | Linux, macOS, Windows| ❓ Unknown          | Fast and lightweight, but no image display |
| Ghostty   | Linux, macOS, Windows| ❓ Unknown          | Modern design, still in development    |
| Tabby     | Linux, macOS, Windows| ✅ Supported        | Cross-platform and visually appealing, image preview available |
| Terminus  | Linux, macOS, Windows| ❓ Unknown          | Electron-based, user-friendly interface |
| Kitty     | Linux, macOS         | ⚠️ Not Sixel, but supports images | Uses proprietary image protocol, not Sixel-compatible |

System-built-in terminals (like macOS Terminal.app or Linux distribution defaults) typically prioritize stability and may lack advanced features such as graphics display. Many users therefore choose more feature-rich third-party terminals.

We welcome all excellent terminal solutions, whether open-source, commercial, or proprietary. If you have recommendations to share, feel free to post them in [GitHub Discussion #224](https://github.com/x-cmd/x-cmd/discussions/224).

## FAQ

:::details What should Windows users do when encountering display compatibility issues? {open}

Windows Terminal may have display compatibility issues in certain scenarios (for example, when using tools like `tmux` or `fzf` in a `git-bash` environment). If you encounter such problems, consider using the third-party terminals recommended on this page that support Windows to work around the issue.
:::

When choosing a terminal, consider balancing functional requirements with personal preferences. x-cmd is committed to providing broad compatibility and continuously adapting to mainstream terminal trends.

# Uninstalling x-cmd

Given that x-cmd is still in early development, some features may not yet be fully developed. We apologize for any inconvenience caused. To facilitate users in restoring their system environment, the uninstallation method is placed in a prominent position.

## Uninstallation Principles

x-cmd aims to be green and portable, so the uninstallation process is very simple. x-cmd's modifications to user directory files are limited to the following two aspects:

1. x-cmd downloads all code and runtime files to the `$HOME/.x-cmd.root` directory
2. To automatically load x-cmd when starting bash and zsh, loading code is added to `.bashrc` and `.zshrc` files: `[ ! -f "$HOME/.x-cmd.root/X" ] || . "$HOME/.x-cmd.root/X"`

## Uninstallation Methods

::::ol
:::li Manual Uninstallation

Based on the principles above, the uninstallation steps are as follows:

1. **Remove loading code:** In `.bashrc` and `.zshrc` files (or the corresponding shell's startup configuration file), find the lines containing `.x-cmd` and delete them
2. **(Optional) Delete x-cmd folder:** If you want to completely remove x-cmd's code, data, and packages, delete the `$HOME/.x-cmd.root` directory
:::
:::li Uninstall using command

1. **Clear auto-loading:** Execute the `x boot clear` command to remove the code that auto-loads x-cmd from the startup configuration file
2. **(Optional) Delete x-cmd folder:** Manually delete the `$HOME/.x-cmd.root` directory: `rm -rf ~/.x-cmd.root`
:::
::::

## Notes

:::warning Deleting `$HOME/.x-cmd.root` may cause running x-cmd instances to malfunction
Deleting this directory may cause running x-cmd instances to malfunction because they rely on code, configuration, or temporary files in that directory.

Recommendations:
1. **Close all x-cmd related shell processes before deleting**
2. **Prioritize removing loading code:** If you do not wish to immediately delete the `$HOME/.x-cmd.root` directory (e.g., concerned about disk space usage), it is recommended to only delete the loading code. Wait until all related shell processes are confirmed to be closed (e.g., after restarting the system) before deleting the directory

The `$HOME/.x-cmd.root` directory usually only contains decompressed code and configuration files, occupying limited space; but it also contains binary files and caches, which may occupy more disk space.
:::

## FAQ

:::details Why don't we provide an x-cmd process detection mechanism? {open}
Currently, any scheme to detect whether x-cmd is running in other shells brings some unacceptable side effects:

1. **Requires a background process to remain in memory**
2. **Requires writing files, which may cause file residue** — If the shell exits abnormally, the cleanup function may not execute, leaving residual files
3. **Increases startup time**

A background process solution may be considered after v6.0.0, with detailed explanation to be provided at that time.
:::

# Upgrading to the Latest Version

## Quick Start

```bash
x upgrade
```

Or, re-run the installation script:

```bash
eval "$(curl https://get.x-cmd.com)"
```

## Explanation

We only release versions that have passed internal rigorous testing. `latest` always points to the latest stable version, and the installation script automatically downloads and updates.

**Upgrade Methods:**

::::ol
:::li Using the installation script
`eval "$(curl https://get.x-cmd.com)"` — This script supports both first-time installation and upgrades.
:::
:::li Using the `x upgrade` command
This command first checks if a new version exists, and if so, executes method 1.
:::
::::

## Upgrade Does Not Affect Open Shells

To ensure the stability of open shells and the reliability of running POSIX Shell scripts, the upgrade process does not delete existing x-cmd code. Shell environments that have loaded old versions are not affected by new versions.

::::ol
:::li Scenario Example
1. You have an open Shell (Shell-A) that has loaded the version pointed to by `latest` (e.g., v0.1.15)
2. You perform an upgrade operation, and `latest` is updated to v0.2.0
3. After the upgrade:
   - Shell-A continues to use x-cmd v0.1.15
   - Newly opened Shells will use x-cmd v0.2.0
:::
:::li How is the Shell that executed the upgrade command handled?
1. If the Shell that executed the upgrade command has not loaded x-cmd, it will load the latest version after the upgrade
2. If the Shell that executed the upgrade command has already loaded x-cmd, it will not immediately load the latest version after the upgrade. The system will start a new Shell in that Shell and load the latest version of x-cmd
:::
::::

## [x-cmd Runtime Mode](/start/shell.md)

### x-cmd as a POSIX Shell Library

For POSIX Shell, x-cmd is a library rather than an external script or command. Therefore, hot-plugging is very difficult.

Hot-plugging was attempted, but due to frequent environment variable modifications (users also modify environment variables when using the shell), and the need to maintain x-cmd's efficient operation and code simplicity and maintainability, this design was eventually abandoned. Therefore, the design avoids loading different versions of x-cmd in one shell, **ensuring it is loaded only once**.

### For Nushell, Elvish, Tcsh, Xonsh, Powershell

For these shells, x-cmd is more like an external command; currently, there is no locking of the x-cmd version in open non-POSIX shells.

In the future, there are plans to lock the x-cmd version in non-POSIX shell environments to improve environment stability.

# Users and Design Philosophy

::::ul
:::li Beginner-Friendly
Easy to get started. Even seasoned developers may have areas of knowledge they're unfamiliar with, which can cause anxiety when encountering unfamiliar domains. We strive to make entry-level features (usually also common features) of each domain/module very easy to use
:::

:::li Targeting Advanced Users
Overall design targets advanced users; x-cmd aims to be a flexible and powerful tool. If simplified, it would lose not only flexibility but also introduce additional concepts and models — these aren't needed by users familiar with the domain, but instead increase management costs and possibility of operational errors
:::
::::

## AI and Network

::::ul
:::li AI Positioning
AI will help users simplify x-cmd usage, but x-cmd usage shouldn't depend on AI. Throughout development, deterministic algorithms are used whenever possible, or at least deterministic algorithm alternatives are provided — maybe one day we'll need to use x-cmd against Skynet
:::

:::li Network Dependency
x-cmd relies on the network for rapid capability delivery, but external network shouldn't be mandatory; internal network usage will be a focus for security enhancement — don't want to be taken out by Cylon in one shot
:::
::::

# On X-CMD's Meaning of "Wen" (文)

**From utility, X is drawn from these five meanings:**

::::ul

:::li Execution
Execution

:::li Extension

:::li Exploration
Curiosity and exploration, the core driving force of civilization's development

:::li Cross
The multiplication effect of various powerful tools
:::

**From meaning - People and X:**

People and X form the character "Wen" (文), also the totem of the x-cmd team. X is the tool, people are the subjects.

## X and the "Wen" Totem

In 2019, I implemented TypeShell, which can run TypeScript and JavaScript anywhere (15MB single executable compressed with [upx](/pkg/upx.md)), but soon discovered [npx](/mod/npx.md) and [deno](/pkg/deno.md). These two tools made me realize the goal must be elevated to any code -- Execute Any script... Naturally, `x` became the command.

In this process, I tried implementing with TypeScript, Golang, C, and Bash, finally adopting the unfamiliar Shell + AWK as the final implementation solution. After three years of effort, x-cmd finally took shape and became practical. In this process, `x` and `文` gradually became our "tribal totem" (wén).

Combining x-cmd's capabilities, as the "tribal priest", I have some quirky interpretations of the `x` totem.

### Thor's Hammer, Cloud, Lightning

::::ol
:::li Powerful Execution Tool
Can download binaries or scripts based on x-cmd to implement any functionality -- like Thor's hammer.
:::

:::li Extension of Local Capabilities Brought by Cloud Computing
x-cmd's goal is to use the network to bring cloud capabilities into the terminal.
:::

:::li CROSS and Multiplication Effect
During development, I realized that combining various cloud CLIs with local command tools can produce huge multiplication effects, also fitting Unix design philosophy -- using text as the linking medium (zàitǐ), small and beautiful tool combinations solving problems.
:::

:::li Lightning Born from the Cloud
Thor's hammer's strongest power comes from lightning born from the `cloud`. This imagery echoes (àn hé) that people using x-cmd as a binder to integrate local and cloud capabilities brings super combination power.
:::
::::

### Zhu Shu Wen (朱书文字) and the "Wen" Totem

::::ol
:::li Archaeological Discovery
In the continuous thinking about programming languages, human language, and writing, I saw an interesting archaeological discovery, [Zhu Shu Wen Zi (朱书文字)](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%9C%B1%E4%B9%A6%E6%96%87%E5%AD%97).
:::

:::li Four Thousand Years of Heritage
Although Zhu Shu Wen is not a mature writing system, four thousand years later, the symbol (文) in the pottery writing looks so familiar to descendants.
:::

:::li The Starting Point of Civilization
Interestingly, this `文` character symbol is the earliest writing recognizable in current Chinese archaeology. And the emergence of writing is a milestone event in human abstract ability and civilization, marking the beginning of civilization. When we see words like `Wénzì (文字)`, the `wen` (文) character inside evokes infinite emotion (gǎnkǎi).
:::

:::li People on Top, X on Bottom
Looking closely at the Zhu Shu `文` character, you can see `人` (person) on top and `乂` on bottom:

- **People on top, no longer celestial phenomena on top**: People trying to discover and master patterns
- **About '乂'**: The single character can be understood as weeding (agricultural civilization), extended to mean governance. But looking solely at the shape of Wen, according to Shuowen Jiezi, it represents symbols. This is actually very vivid because `乂` looks very much like cracks on turtle shells, such as the `yao` (爻) in the Bagua Liu Yao (八卦六爻), which also originated from this
- **Symbolizing it, patterning it, naming it, ruling it**: Superstition eventually ends, patterns continuously iterate. The light of reason first appears (chū xiàn), human civilization begins
:::

:::li Two Dimensions of the Totem
This is the imagery I take, people and X, forming the two dimensions of this totem.
:::

:::li Carrier of Thought
`文` is not only communication but also the carrier of thought; what writing serializes is civilization (wénmíng), the operating system installed in the brains of future generations.
:::

:::li Another Character in the Pottery Writing
Interestingly, among the two characters in the pottery writing, some interpret them as Wen Yao, others as Wen Ming or Wen Ling.

- Yao ruling the world with Wen De is a beautiful legend of Han Confucians, [Bamboo Annals](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%AB%B9%E6%9B%B8%E7%B4%80%E5B9%B4) although not necessarily completely true, describes something more in line with human nature, [How Taosi Flat Pot Was Inscribed with "Wen Ling"](https://www.cssn.cn/kgxc/kgxc_kgsb/202308/t20230803_5676783.shtml)
- Another interpretation is Wen Yi, the character Yi is very interesting with much room for imagination. This is also the romance left for us by our ancestors
:::
::::

### People x AI

::::ul
:::li The Convergence of Human Thought
The convergence of human thought always excites people, only what we will increasingly witness is that the party exchanging thoughts is more often LLM/AI.
:::
:::li The Next Stage of Human Civilization
This is the next stage of human civilization: People x AI.
:::
::::

## Finally

In a world of changing winds and clouds, humanity's乘风破浪 into the unknown is the continuous driving force of civilization's advancement. This is the story of `People` and `x`. This x can be plain and unremarkable, or brilliant and colorful. You decide.

# Installing and Using x-cmd on Windows Systems

🎯 This document describes how to install and use `x-cmd` in `WSL`, `Git-Bash`, `Cygwin`, and `Mingw` environments on Windows systems.

## Installing x-cmd

::::ol
:::li Method 1: Using shell script installation (for command-line users)
Suitable for WSL, Git-Bash (Git-For-Windows), Cygwin, MinGw environments. The installation method is the same as [installation on Linux](/start/linux.md):

::: code-group

```bash [curl]
eval "$(curl https://get.x-cmd.com)"
```

```bash [wget]
eval "$(wget -O- https://get.x-cmd.com)"
```

:::

:::tip
- `x-cmd` can run on `WSL1`, but `WSL1` development has stalled, and the PKG system is not adapted for `WSL1`. It is recommended to use `WSL2`
- `x-cmd` has performance optimizations for `Git-Bash`, but due to its mechanisms, there is still some performance difference compared to `WSL2`
:::
:::

:::li Method 2: Using `x-cmd.bat` script installation (for command-line beginners)
[`x-cmd.bat`](https://get.x-cmd.com/x-cmd.bat) is a batch script specially prepared for Windows users, requiring no administrator privileges:

1. [Download `x-cmd.bat`](https://get.x-cmd.com/x-cmd.bat)
2. Double-click to run and wait for the installation to complete. The command-line interface will open automatically after installation
3. After the first installation, `x-cmd.bat` can be used as a quick launcher. It is recommended to place it on the desktop

<video id="video" controls preload>
  <source id="mp4" src="/image/start/x-bat-install.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

:::info About Windows SmartScreen Warning
- Windows SmartScreen blocks content from unknown sources, which is a security mechanism
- The `x-cmd.bat` downloaded from the x-cmd official website (HTTPS) has open-source code hosted on [GitHub](https://github.com/x-cmd/get/blob/main/x-cmd.bat)
- We are seeking Windows SmartScreen certification. Currently, manual allowance is required to bypass the block
:::
:::

:::li Method 3: Using PowerShell script installation (for PowerShell users)
```powershell
[System.Text.Encoding]::GetEncoding("utf-8").GetString($(Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://get.x-cmd.com/x-cmd.ps1").RawContentStream.ToArray()) | Invoke-Expression
```

This script will automatically download `x-cmd.bat`, execute the installation, and configure `x pwsh --setup`.

:::warning Execution Policy
- To execute PowerShell scripts, you may need to adjust the execution policy:
- View current policy: `Get-ExecutionPolicy -List`
- Modify policy to allow script execution: [`Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.security/set-executionpolicy)
- Reference: [PowerShell Execution Policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_execution_policies?view=powershell-7.4), [Set-ExecutionPolicy Documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.security/set-executionpolicy)
:::
:::
::::

## Common Installation Issues

### No Installation Permission

If you are a Windows PowerShell user, you may encounter Git for Windows installation permission restrictions during the installation process:

1. Download the corresponding architecture installation package from the [gitbash releases page](https://github.com/git-for-windows/git/releases/) (e.g., Git-${version}-64-bit.tar.bz2) and extract it
2. Run `bash.exe` in the `bin` directory
3. Run `eval "$(curl https://get.x-cmd.com)"` in the opened terminal to complete the installation

## Using x-cmd

### On POSIX Shell (Bash, Zsh)

After successful installation, welcome to read the [Getting Started Guide](/start/get-started.md) ~ This guide will help you quickly master x-cmd's core features.

### On Non-POSIX Shell (Fish, Elvish, Nushell, Xonsh)

After successful installation, run the corresponding command to automatically load x-cmd when opening the target shell:

```bash
x fish --setup
```

This command will add a line of code to load x-cmd in Fish's configuration file.

More Non-POSIX Shell documentation:
- [fish](/start/fish.md)
- [elvish](/start/elvish.md)
- [nushell](/start/nushell.md)
- [xonsh](/start/xonsh.md)
- [tcsh](/start/tcsh.md)

## Windows Package Manager Enhancement

x-cmd provides the following modules to improve the package manager experience:

::::ul
:::li [x scoop](/mod/scoop.md)
An open-source tool manager supported by the scoop community; provides fast software search and proxy/mirror configuration features.
:::
:::li [x choco](/mod/choco.md)
A veteran Windows software tool manager.
:::
:::li [x winget](/mod/winget.md)
A software tool manager officially provided by Microsoft; provides fast software search and proxy/mirror configuration features.
:::

## WSL2 Usage Experience Enhancement

### Better Interaction with Windows in WSL Environment

- If WSL is detected, desktop application behavior will use Windows GUI apps: `x open <file|url>`, `x browse <file|url>` will open Windows' default browser
- The [pwsh module](/mod/pwsh.md) uses PowerShell to implement host information retrieval and management

### wslx and wslr Commands

Starting from v0.5.10, `wslx` and `wslr` commands and the [wsl module](/mod/wsl.md) are provided to improve wsl usage:

```bash
# Run x ls in wsl environment
wslx ls

# Run jq in wsl environment, wslr will load the binpath under wsl default user space
wslr jq
```

## FAQ

:::details [Installing x-cmd with restricted software installation](#no-installation-permission) {open}
If you encounter git for windows installation restrictions during the x-cmd installation process, please refer to the solution in the "No Installation Permission" section.
:::

:::details Why doesn't x-cmd support Busybox-For-Windows? {open}
Currently x-cmd cannot run directly on **Busybox-For-Windows**:
- `busybox for windows` lacks emulation of some system files
- Compatibility would lead to overly complex internal design and reduce engineering quality
- Considering actual user scenarios and the increasing popularity of WSL2, development in this technical direction is temporarily not pursued
:::

:::details x-cmd's Optimization Efforts on Windows {open}
1. Despite Git-Bash performance issues, x-cmd has made adaptations in the theme and other modules to ensure user experience
2. WSL2 provides a nearly perfect Linux experience, and x-cmd operates efficiently on it
3. For Windows users, modules such as [pwsh](/mod/pwsh.md), [scoop](/mod/scoop.md), [winget](/mod/winget.md), [choco](/mod/choco.md) are provided
:::

# Development Preview Version x7

x7 is aimed at expert users, designed to:

- Let them quickly experience the latest features and capabilities of x-cmd
- Fix bugs in experimental modules and enhance functionality in a timely manner
- Achieve hour-level update and feedback improvement cycles

## Introduction to x7

x7 has been iterating internally within the development team for two years as an internal test version for testing new features and modules before official release.

Currently updated weekly, it may be adjusted to bi-weekly or monthly updates in the future. A daily build version (nightly build) was considered, but concerns about the increased version count bringing unnecessary complexity led to the decision against it.

Recent user collaboration has been very pleasant, and we believe expert users can handle the complexity brought by rolling releases (such as potential bugs and inconsistencies). Therefore, the decision was made to make the internal test version public, in order to:

- Allow expert users to quickly experience the latest features and capabilities
- Obtain feedback and make adjustments faster
- Users can update to the latest development version through x7 and provide feedback immediately, enabling more efficient iteration

## Risk Warning

:::danger Never use x7 in production environments.
In addition to potentially containing bugs and unstable features, x7 cannot guarantee that shell sessions opened before an update can continue to load the initialized x-cmd version after the update.
:::

Specific explanation:
1. An opened shell initialized the x7 version of x-cmd (e.g., commit x11111)
2. After x7 updates, the GitHub code repository commit becomes x22222
3. The original shell session will directly load the module code from x22222, potentially causing unpredictable behavior

The official release has resolved this issue, ensuring that each shell session uses code from only one commit version; however, this feature has not yet been implemented in x7.

Reasons for adopting this simplified approach:
1. **Reduced management complexity:** Properly handling this issue would require introducing a large number of intermediate versions under the `v` directory and introducing a garbage collection mechanism to clear versions no longer in use
2. Users typically restart shells frequently
3. The x-cmd core is increasingly stable, so this issue has limited impact on expert users
4. Other internal versions also use this simplified mode, with no major issues found in three years

Although x7 is open to all users, it is only recommended for invited users. We will continue to maintain high-frequency updates for the official release, ensuring all users receive the latest bug fixes and feature enhancements.

## Using x7

```bash
x upgrade x7
```

Or

```bash
eval "$(curl https://get.x-cmd.com/x7)"
```

Note that in x7 mode, the `x upgrade` command still updates the x7 version.

To switch to the stable version:

```bash
x upgrade latest
```

Or

```bash
eval "$(curl https://get.x-cmd.com)"
```

## x7 Hosted on [codeberg.org](https://codeberg.org/x-cmd/x7)

x7 is currently hosted on codeberg.org rather than GitHub. Main reasons:

1. Compared to GitHub (github.com), Codeberg (codeberg.org) is relatively accessible in mainland China
2. Hosting on both Github and Codeberg simultaneously would increase unnecessary complexity, synchronization issues, and maintenance burden
3. Experimenting with hosting more code on codeberg

We look forward to the development of codeberg and hope users can have more experience using codeberg.

## Thanks

Thank you for your feedback, we will continue to improve!

<h1 class="visually-hidden">Xonsh</h1>

## Overview

xonsh is a Python-powered shell that supports mixing Python and shell commands in the command line. The x-cmd toolkit integrates with xonsh to enhance its functionality and user experience.

## Installing x-cmd

::::ol
:::li Using curl
```sh
curl https://get.x-cmd.com | sh
xonsh
```
:::

:::li Using wget
```sh
wget -O- https://get.x-cmd.com | sh
xonsh
```
:::

:::li Activating Existing x-cmd Installation
If x-cmd is already installed but commands are not found in xonsh:

```sh
sh -c '. "$HOME/.x-cmd.root/X"; x upgrade latest; x onsh --setup'
xonsh
```
:::
::::

## Changes Made by `x onsh --setup` to .xonshrc

When running `x onsh --setup`, a startup line is added to `$HOME/.xonshrc` to enable the [x-cmd xonshrc](https://github.com/x-cmd/x-cmd/blob/main/mod/onsh/lib/rc/xonshrc) module when xonsh starts.

### Activation Code

```
test -e "$HOME/.x-cmd.root/local/data/xonsh/xonshrc" && source "$HOME/.x-cmd.root/local/data/xonsh/xonshrc" # boot up x-cmd.
```

- Ends with the marker comment `# boot up x-cmd.`
- Purpose: Import enhanced functions, add PATH entries
- Strategy: Minimize code deletion from .xonshrc to prevent user configuration loss

:::tip Configuration Recommendation
If you install tools through x-cmd (such as starship, asdf) that require activation or configuration in .xonshrc, add your configuration code **after** the x-cmd activation code.
:::

## FAQ

:::details Support Status {open}
**Supported Systems/Environments:** Linux, MacOS, WSL, Cygwin, MSYS2 (such as Gitbash)

**Tools Provided by x-cmd:**
- [Common command wrappers](/mod/zuz.md): cd, ip, ps, tar, apt, brew, etc., smarter than native commands
- [Lightweight package management](/pkg/.md): Implemented in shell and awk for quickly obtaining common software
- [Practical website CLI](/mod/cht.md): API wrappers for github.com, cht.sh, etc.
- [AI tools](/mod/openai.md): CLI for ChatGPT/Gemini/Jina.ai, etc.

**Note**: The above support is currently in Beta.
:::

:::details Current Issues {open}
1. **@ command invocation issue**

   In xonsh, `@<name>` is interpreted as an annotation. When no arguments are provided (such as `@gemini`), xonsh waits for a decorated function to be passed. You can input `;` to avoid this, e.g., `@gemini ;`.

2. **Pipe issue**

   When attempting to wrap x commands in functions to access xonsh environment variables, handling and detecting pipes becomes problematic. Therefore, the current x command disables environment variables and uses file-based passing instead to ensure pipes work correctly.
:::
