# About Weekdays

`x ccal` supports various weekday naming conventions, aiming to accommodate different users' habits. (From the author's perspective, implementing these was purely for fun~)

As early as the pre-Qin period, China already adopted a seven-day cycle, distinguishing these seven days by the seven celestial bodies (the Seven Luminaries: Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn). This tradition is still preserved in Japan and Korea today, using the names Sun, Moon, Fire, Water, Wood, Gold, Earth. In ancient times, the order of these celestial bodies might have differed, but they all shared the characteristic of placing the Sun first.

During the late Qing and early Republic periods, Chinese people gradually adopted "星期" (xingqi, literally meaning planet and cycle, indicating its origin) combined with numbers, or "礼拜" (libai) as names. However, no matter how simplified, the seventh day is never called "星期七" or "礼拜七", but rather "星期日/天" (Sunday/Heaven) or "礼拜日" (Sunday). If computers had been invented 50 years earlier, there might have been terms like "星期零" or "礼拜零" (0 resembles the character for Sun/Day, which is quite philosophical).

Chinese also has the term "周" (zhou), which in this context, the concept of celestial bodies has faded, emphasizing more the nature of the cycle.

In `x ccal`, you can freely set different weekday names:

```bash
x ccal --cfg wdtitle=yao     # Uses the Seven Luminaries names still preserved in Japan and Korea
x ccal --cfg wdtitle=xingqi  # Uses 星期日...星期六 (Sunday...Saturday)
x ccal --cfg wdtitle=zhou    # Uses 周日...周六 (Sunday...Saturday)
x ccal --cfg wdtitle=libai   # Uses 礼拜日...礼拜六 (Sunday...Saturday)

x ccal init # Modify the wdtitle attribute in the interactive interface
```

![ccal_cfg](/image/mod/ccal.1_6.webp)

[Reference](https://zh-classical.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%98%9F%E6%9C%9F)

## The First Day of the Week

As a programmer, I personally prefer the scheme starting with `Day (0)`, so [`x ccal`](/mod/ccal.md) defaults to Sunday as the first day of the week. Of course, users can adjust this according to their needs.

Different organizations and cultures have different considerations for this. For example, in the ISO 8601 date and time standard, the first day of the [standard week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Week_dates) is Monday.

Therefore, we provide flexible configuration options:

```bash
x ccal --cfg wdstart=0    # Starts on Sunday, default
x ccal --cfg wdstart=1    # Starts on Monday
x ccal --cfg wdstart=2    # Starts on Tuesday

x ccal init # Modify the start attribute in the interactive interface
```

This concludes the technical introduction and design philosophy regarding weekdays and dates in [`x ccal`](/mod/ccal.md).

## Digression: Ten-Day Cycle, From Sun Worship to Shooting the Suns

As mentioned above, the weekly cycle always places the Sun first. From a modern astronomical perspective, this is because we are in the solar system, centered around the Sun. But a deeper reason is rooted in humanity's ancient sun worship.

In fact, besides the seven-day cycle, there is also the ancient custom of a ten-day cycle. This custom is still preserved today, for example, we often divide a month into three "旬" (xun), with ten days (or approximately ten days) constituting one "旬". If you look at the structure of the character "旬", it also contains "日" (sun/day). Tracing back to oracle bone script, it is a cross (十字) plus a cyclical arc shape (日), perfectly illustrating the concept of a cycle.

The most famous and interesting story of the ten-day cycle is arguably Hou Yi shooting the suns. I first heard this story at the age of 7 ("Five Thousand Years of Culture"). The story goes that the Heavenly Emperor had ten sun sons, originally each sun was on duty for one day (perhaps the origin of the term "值日", meaning 'on duty for the day'), while the other nine rested on a tree (perhaps similar to the World Tree in the Norse Odin system). But one day, all ten suns suddenly jumped into the sky to play, and the weather immediately became scorching hot and dry, causing a great catastrophe for humanity. Humans were helpless (for ancient agricultural societies, this was undoubtedly a fatal blow, hence records of witches exposing themselves to the sun to pray for rain; this kind of sacrifice ritual left a deep impression on me, frankly speaking, the book "Classic of Mountains and Seas" is somewhat unsuitable for children).

At this point, a celestial being named Hou Yi stepped forward, holding a divine bow, and shot down the suns one by one. Perhaps because he was shooting too enthusiastically, fortunately someone reminded him, so one sun was left in the end. From then on, the surviving sun obediently went to work, changing from `on duty one day, rest nine` to `no rest all year`.

The Heavenly Emperor was thus enraged, and as punishment, demoted Hou Yi and his wife Chang'e to mortals, denying them eternal life. Chang'e, seeking eternal life, overdosed on medicine and fled to the moon. Hou Yi was later betrayed by his apprentice and died from a hidden arrow. (Perhaps this story wants to tell us that behind success... there are always hidden dangers?)

Later, when I read about the history of the Xia and Shang dynasties, specifically Taikang losing his state and Shaokang's restoration, I learned that Hou Yi was actually "后" (Hou, meaning leader) Yi (his name), and as the leader of the Youqiong clan, he expelled Taikang and overthrew the Xia regime. This is the historical "shooting the suns". And later, reading about Hou Yi being murdered and usurped by his subordinate Han Zhuo, I immediately thought of the apprentice who injured him with a hidden arrow in the myth.

Even later, reading about King Wu Yi of Shang shooting the sky, and the reforms in the late Shang period such as gradually simplifying sacrificial rites, appointing minor officials, adopting primogeniture, marginalizing nobles and priests, and monopolizing oracle bone divination to further centralize power, I could vaguely see the shadow of the "ten suns worship gradually evolving into one sun in the sky" within them.

## Materialized Artifacts: The Bronze Sacred Tree of Sanxingdui

Specifically regarding archaeological artifacts, the Bronze Sacred Tree of Sanxingdui must be mentioned. Thanks to the archaeologists' nearly ten years of restoration efforts, we can once again see how the concepts of the ten-day worship and being on duty were materialized in ancient times – our generation has seen many ancient objects that even Sima Qian never saw.

Furthermore, Sanxingdui is not an alien civilization, nor is it ancient Egyptian civilization. The "Eastern Origin of Sanxingdui" theory is supported by relatively sufficient archaeological evidence. From an archaeological perspective, this also seems related to the Yellow Emperor tribe's conquest of Sanwei (San Miao, Chi You). I will add relevant materials later.

The sacred tree in the image above only has nine suns; the "center position" at the top of the tree is empty – Sanxingdui has multiple burial pits, and a host of divine artifacts were deliberately damaged and buried (as a form of suppression). Perhaps they can never be fully restored – or perhaps, the tenth sun is in the sky. (This is like some seven-story pagodas only having five stories, one in the sky, one on the ground, primarily relying on abstract imagination and sublimation~)

# Chronology Systems

## Our Country Adopts the Gregorian Calendar

The Gregorian calendar, known as the Western calendar during the Qing Dynasty, is the standard calendar used in China. After the establishment of the Republic of China, Mr. Sun Yat-sen, upon assuming the provisional presidency, immediately issued the "Order to Adopt the Solar Calendar".

On September 27, 1949, the First Plenary Session of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference decided that the People's Republic of China would adopt the universally used Common Era (AD) chronology system.

> **AD One == Yuanshi One**: Emperor Ping of Han, Liu Kan, ascended the throne in the year before Common Era One (BC 1). Due to his youth, Wang Mang held power and changed the era name to [`Yuanshi`](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%85%83%E5%A7%8B/3167180) the following year (i.e., Common Era One). Therefore, the `Yuanshi First Year` of Emperor Ping of Han is `Common Era One`. This adds another piece of evidence to the argument that [Wang Mang was a time traveler](https://www.bing.com/search?q=王莽是个穿越者).

## No Year Zero in AD and Numerical Representation of BC Years

The Common Era chronology system designates the year of Jesus' birth as the first year, i.e., Common Era One (AD 1). The year before Common Era One (BC 1) is the year before the first year, not Common Era Zero.
Therefore, the year following BC 1 is AD 1.

For ease of calculation, for years before the Common Era, a negative sign is used, and the numerical value is increased by one:

| Event                                     | Numerical Representation | Common Era Chronology |
| :---------------------------------------- | :----------------------- | :-------------------- |
| Article Written                           | 2025                     | AD 2025               |
| Birth of Jesus, Emperor Ping of Han Changes Era (Yuanshi Year 1) | 1                        | AD 1                  |
| Qin Shi Huang Destroys Qi, Unifies China  | -220                     | BC 221                |
| Battle of Muye, King Wu Conquers Yin      | -1045                    | BC 1046               |

This also **gives rise** to a question – does the 21st century begin in 2000 or 2001?

Official documents generally recognize 2001 as the first year of the 21st century, and 2000 as the last year of the **20th** century. For example, the [New Year's Address for 2001: Jointly Create a Beautiful New Century](https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2001/content_61231.htm) mentions "extending congratulations for the first New Year of the new century".

## Xuanyuan (Yellow Emperor) Chronology, Daoist Calendar

1.  Uses the traditional Chinese lunar calendar, not the Gregorian calendar.
2.  According to Daoist teachings, the Yellow Emperor began his reign at the age of 20, which corresponds to BC 2697.
3.  Therefore, the formula is `(Lunar Calendar) Year + 2697 Years`.

-   [Baidu Baike on "Yellow Emperor Chronology"](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E9%BB%84%E5%B8%9D%E7%BA%AA%E5%B9%B4/3152927)
-   [CPPCC Proposal: Proposal on Establishing the Xuanyuan Chronology (XY)](https://ihistory.ifeng.com/mip/43334638/news.shtml)

Disagreements:

1.  The calculation process is not necessarily widely accepted. The era is distant, and historical texts may contain errors or forgeries, lacking archaeological support, making it difficult to unify.
2.  Mr. Sun Yat-sen's "Order to Adopt the Solar Calendar" also introduced the Yellow Emperor Chronology as a reference. The "Circular on Calendar and Era Change" stipulated: "The Republic of China shall adopt the solar calendar, with the 4609th year of the Yellow Emperor's era, which is the 13th day of the 11th month of the Xinhai year, as the first day of the first year of the Republic of China."
3.  The widely used Yellow Emperor calendar is based on the lunar calendar, but the aforementioned CPPCC proposal, to be compatible with the Gregorian calendar, directly uses `(Gregorian Calendar) Year + 2697`.

Current Approach:

1.  I believe that, like the Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches, the Yellow Emperor calendar is more about paying tribute to traditional culture.
2.  Since the Gregorian calendar is widely used, changing the era would incur costs. Therefore, the role of the Yellow Emperor chronology is not for practical use but for tribute.
3.  Given this, it should be carried through consistently, using the traditional Chinese lunar calendar as the basis for the Yellow Emperor chronology. The current implementation of [`x ccal`](/mod/ccal.md) **calculates the Yellow Emperor chronology based on the lunar calendar**.

We have adopted the more concise term `Xuanyuan xxxx Year`:

1.  `(The Yellow Emperor) received the state at Youxiong, resided at Xuanyuan Hill, hence taking it as his name and also his appellation.`
2.  Refer to [Wikipedia](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%BB%84%E5%B8%9D) for reference.
3.  Legend has it he was born on the third day of the third lunar month; a common saying is "Second day of the second month, the dragon raises its head; third day of the third month, Xuanyuan is born."

## Buddhist Calendar

1.  The year of the Buddha's (Shakyamuni's) Nirvana is the first year of the Buddhist calendar - BC 543.
2.  Disagreements arise regarding whether to use the Gregorian or lunar calendar year. Note that different countries' time zones may lead to differences in the date of the full moon.
3.  The specific date of the Buddha's Nirvana (Vesak Day) varies among different Buddhist traditions. For example, Theravada Buddhist regions (such as Thailand, Sri Lanka, etc., and parts of Yunnan, China) usually set it on the fifteenth day of the fourth lunar month (the full moon day of the fourth month), while Japan designates it as April 8th of the Gregorian calendar.

Since [`x ccal`](/mod/ccal.md) is primarily for Chinese users, its implementation uses the year of the Buddha's Nirvana (BC 543) as the first year of the Buddhist calendar. Regarding the specific date of the Buddha's Nirvana (Vesak Day), the date differs in different traditions; for example, Theravada Buddhist regions usually set it on the fifteenth day of the fourth lunar month.

**First Buddhist Conference:**

-   [Conference Website](https://wfbhq.org/general-conference-detail.php?id=015000018)
-   [Conference Communiqué](https://wfbhq.org/uploads/conferences/015000018/01505/Resolution-1st.pdf)
-   [Conference Proceedings](https://wfbhq.org//uploads/conferences/015000018/01507/Record-of-Proceedings-1st.pdf)

> Quote: The Conference also pledged to the government of countries where Buddhist communities are to be found to recognize the first full moon day of May as Buddha Day or Vesak Day.

This quote refers to a resolution from the First Conference of the World Fellowship of Buddhists regarding the date of Vesak Day, suggesting that the first full moon day of May in the Gregorian calendar be recognized as Vesak Day; this is the day of Nirvana, which is the first day of the first year of the Buddhist calendar.

**Popular Science Article Referenced in This Article:**

[By what calendar is "Buddha's Birthday" celebrated?](https://www.163.com/dy/article/F6AG8O7L05239F82.html)

# Auspicious and Inauspicious Days

Folk customs regarding auspicious and inauspicious days can only be viewed as a social and cultural phenomenon, belonging to a form of mysticism that cannot be disproven. However, I believe they serve two purposes:

1.  **Alleviating Decision Fatigue**: When deciding where to eat lunch at the company, those of us with decision fatigue wrote a random number generator to determine the restaurant for the day. In my view, auspicious/inauspicious days can serve as a substitute for random numbers, helping people with decision fatigue allocate their decision-making energy to areas where it is truly needed.
2.  **Community Coordination**: For example, happy events and sad events should ideally not be held on the same day.

Of course, my primary motivation is curiosity! Curiosity is the biggest driving force behind this [ccal module](/mod/ccal.md) ~

## Currently Integrated Features of `x ccal`

```bash
x ccal              # Interactive view
x ccal i            # View today
x ccal i 2008-8-8   # View the opening day of the Beijing Olympics
x ccal i 2025-6-8   # View June 8, 2025. Note that this day is a San Niang Sha day.
```

## Common Taboos

### [San Niang Sha](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%89%E5%A8%98%E7%85%9E/3683402) (also mistakenly called San Yang Sha)

1.  Wedding ceremonies should avoid San Niang Sha days.
2.  Background Story: San Niang was an independent, modern-minded single woman who firmly refused to tolerate displays of affection. While protecting single people, she potentially created more single people.
3.  It is said that if a wedding takes place on a "San Niang Sha" day, the bride's auspicious energy will be overwhelming. Therefore, the bride should wear a red veil and be sheltered by a red umbrella during the wedding.

Folk tradition holds that the 3rd, 7th, 13th, 18th, 22nd, and 27th days of each lunar month are San Niang Sha days. However, in reality, the Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches of the day must also be considered:

```markdown
The 3rd day coinciding with a Geng Wu day
The 7th day coinciding with a Xin Wei day
The 13th day coinciding with a Wu Shen day
The 18th day coinciding with a Ji You day
The 22nd day coinciding with a Bing Wu day
The 27th day coinciding with a Ding Wei day
```

Thus, the actual probability of occurrence is very low. Interestingly, in June 2025, the month when this module was completed, the 8th day is indeed a San Niang Sha day.

### Yang Gong Ji

On Yang Gong Ji days, it is advised not to hold weddings, undertake construction, visit relatives, travel far, or take long journeys.

There are thirteen Yang Gong Ji days throughout the year: the 13th of the 1st month, the 11th of the 2nd month, the 9th of the 3rd month, the 17th of the 4th month, the 15th of the 5th month, the 13th of the 6th month, the 11th of the 7th month, the 29th of the 7th month, the 27th of the 8th month, the 25th of the 9th month, the 23rd of the 10th month, the 21st of the 11th month, and the 19th of the 12th month.

This custom is currently prevalent in areas such as Shijiazhuang City and Lingshou County in Hebei Province, and among the Hakka people in Dongshan, Chengdu, Sichuan Province.

Reference: [Yang Gong Ji](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%9D%A8%E5%85%AC%E5%BF%8C%E6%97%A5/3630656)

## Jian Chu Twelve Day Officers

The Jian Chu Twelve Day Officers are a traditional Chinese method for selecting auspicious dates. These twelve deities, named Jian, Chu, Man, Ping, Ding, Zhi, Po, Wei, Cheng, Shou, Kai, and Bi, take turns presiding over each day in a cycle. The presiding deity determines the auspiciousness or inauspiciousness of the day and the activities suitable for it.

The origin of the Twelve Day Officers is unclear, but it can be traced back to the late Warring States period. In the "Day Books" found in the Jiudian Chu Slips and Yunmeng Qin Slips, there are twelve deity names referred to as "Chu". Based on the regions where they circulated, they are divided into Qin Chu in the Qin state and Chu Chu in the Chu state. Both regions had twelve deity names, which were not entirely identical, suggesting a possible common origin. Because the calendars used by the Chu and Qin states differed, the starting month and day for calculating Jian Chu also differed, with a two-month difference between them, but both followed a twelve-day cycle. The Qin slip "Day Book" integrated both Chu Chu and Qin Chu.

The mnemonic rhyme for the auspiciousness of the twelve stars is: "Jian, Man, Ping, Shou are black; Chu, Wei, Ding, Zhi are yellow; Cheng and Kai are all usable; Po and Bi should not be encountered."

-   **Yellow Path Days (Auspicious Days)**: Chu, Wei, Ding, Zhi. Among these, Cheng and Kai days are particularly suitable for all matters.
-   **Black Path Days (Inauspicious Days)**: Jian, Man, Ping, Shou. Among these, Po and Bi days are unsuitable for all matters.

| Star | Explanation                                                                                                                               |
| :--- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Jian | Refers to the beginning of something not yet completed. All matters can be undertaken, but construction should be avoided.                |
| Chu  | Refers to the meaning of clearing away. It is very auspicious for getting rid of the old and welcoming the new.                            |
| Man  | Refers to the meaning of completeness. Auspicious for sacrifices, but inauspicious for other matters. Most unsuitable for weddings.        |
| Ping | Refers to the meaning of smoothness. Both happy and sad events can be held.                                                               |
| Ding | Refers to everything being settled. Suitable for adoption, business, visits, exams, etc. Inauspicious for other unfortunate matters.      |
| Zhi  | Refers to being stubborn and inflexible in all matters. All happy and sad events should be avoided.                                       |
| Cheng | Refers to the accomplishment of all matters. Both happy and sad events can be undertaken.                                                 |
| Shou | Refers to the meaning of collecting or gathering. Only suitable for collecting, demanding, or burial. Inauspicious for other unfortunate matters. |
| Po   | Refers to the meaning of breaking or shattering. Avoid all happy and sad events. This day is referred to as the Xing Po day.              |
| Wei  | Refers to the meaning of being cautious in all matters. Matters can be undertaken but with caution; major matters should be treated as minor. |
| Kai  | Refers to being open and smooth, everything can be done.                                                                                  |
| Bi   | Refers to being blocked or closed. Suitable for collecting or burial, but unsuitable for other matters.                                   |

**References:**

-   [Wikipedia Jian Chu Twelve Deities](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%BB%BA%E9%99%A4%E5%8D%81%E4%BA%8C%E7%A5%9E)
-   [Baidu Baike Twelve Day Officers](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%8D%81%E4%BA%8C%E5%BB%BA%E6%98%9F/2146343)
-   [Twelve Day Officers](https://www.huaxia.com/c/2023/06/26/1718541.shtml)

## Rokuyō

Rokuyō first appeared in "Kong Ming Liu Yao Xing" (Zhuge Liang's Six Stars), while another theory attributes its creation to "Li Chunfeng" of the Tang Dynasty (one of the authors of the Tui Bei Tu).

In Japan, after entering the Meiji era, annotations predicting auspiciousness and inauspiciousness on calendars were considered superstition and prohibited by the government. Only "Rokuyō" was allowed to remain, which led to its rapid popularization among the Japanese public.

The current Japanese Rokuyō differs from the ancient Chinese version, and even differs from the Rokuyō before the late Edo period.

`x ccal` includes Japanese Rokuyō, partly out of curiosity and partly because these terms are used in daily life.

**Calculation Formula**: `(Lunar Month + Lunar Day) % 6`
A remainder of zero is Taian, a remainder of one is Shakku, and the sequence follows below.

The following content is based on [Japanese Wikipedia Rokuyō](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%85%AD%E6%9B%9C)

### Taian: All Things Peaceful

Taian (たいあん) is considered a day suitable for all matters, meaning "great auspiciousness".

It is considered the most auspicious day among the Rokuyō, said to be lucky in all endeavors with no unsuccessful outcomes. "Taian" originates from "Tai An" (great peace), hence activities like weddings and Jōtō-shiki (ridgepole-raising ceremonies) are often chosen to be held on Taian days. Many people also choose this day for car registration, vehicle delivery, groundbreaking ceremonies for buildings, or property handover.

### Shakku: Quarrels --

-   Unsuitable for happy events, official business, lawsuits, or contracts. Only noon (11 AM to 1 PM, the Wu hour) is considered auspicious during the day; the rest of the time is inauspicious.
-   It is said that the Onmyōdō's Akajita day and Akaguchi day, or Taishaku (大赤), were combined and became one of the Rokuyō as an inauspicious day. Akajita day is considered the day presided over by the deity Akajita, who governs the western gate of Jupiter. Among the six subordinate Rakshasa deities guarding the gates, the third one is a threatening presence, so lawsuits and contracts should be avoided on this day. Additionally, Akaguchi day is considered the day presided over by the deity Akaguchi, who governs the eastern gate of Jupiter. Among the eight subordinate great demon deities, the fourth one, Happatsu-sotsu, is a presence that obstructs people's arguments, so lawsuits and contracts should also be avoided on this day. Akajita day has a 6-day cycle, and Akaguchi day has an 8-day cycle, so the cycles are different, but it is believed that these were summarized and incorporated into one of the Rokuyō, becoming "Shakku".
-   Because this day contains the character "赤" (red), caution should be exercised regarding fire and sharp objects. This means being mindful of things associated with "death" on this day.

**Difference from Chinese Chiku Day:**

-   The third day of the first lunar month each year (also called Chi Gou Ri). According to traditional Chinese customs, it is easy to have arguments and disputes with others on this day. To avoid inviting verbal conflict, people do not go out to visit relatives and friends, but stay at home to worship deities. Hence, Chi Kou Ri is also called "Xiao Nian Chao" (Minor New Year's Day).
-   [Wikipedia](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E8%B5%A4%E5%8F%A3)

> **Li's Comment**: Suitable for staying home. It's best not even to play RPGs.

### Senshō: First Strike Wins

Senshō (せんしょう or せんかち in Japanese pronunciation) is a day suitable for completing tasks early, embodying the meaning of "first strike wins". It is said to be auspicious in the morning and inauspicious in the afternoon. This day is considered auspicious for handling urgent matters or engaging in lawsuits. In the past, it was also written as "Sokki" (速喜, quick joy) or "Sokichi" (即吉, immediate auspiciousness).

> **Li's Comment**: Don't be a 'wait-and-see' person; buy early and enjoy early.

### Tomobiki: Indecisive Outcome

-   Tomobiki (ともびき) is considered a day where the outcome is indecisive, neither good nor bad. Alternatively, when interpreted as "no win, no loss" or "attracting friends," it can be considered an auspicious day.
-   Tomobiki days are auspicious in the morning and evening, but inauspicious at noon.
-   It is believed that holding a funeral on a Tomobiki day will "pull friends to the underworld" (i.e., death). Therefore, funeral-related businesses and crematories may be closed on Tomobiki days. However, since Rokuyō is unrelated to Buddhism, some sects (such as Jōdo Shinshū) may hold funerals on Tomobiki days. Furthermore, an increasing number of local governments are abolishing the rule for crematories to close on Tomobiki days.
-   It is said that the superstition of avoiding funerals on Tomobiki days originally stemmed from confusion with "Tomobiki" (友曳), which is completely unrelated to Rokuyō. Tomobiki (友曳) is a custom referring to avoiding travel in the direction corresponding to the day's zodiac sign, or avoiding holding funerals on that day. Due to the identical pronunciation, it is believed that the two were confused.
-   Additionally, when dealing with celebratory events, some people interpret the aforementioned "no win, no loss" as "marital harmony" and thus choose this day for wedding ceremonies, or send wedding return gifts on this day to "share happiness."
-   Although the reading "ともびき" is common, its origin is the Chinese word "Liú Yǐn" (留引). Since it was read in Japanese and assigned the characters "ともびき" (友引), it is unrelated to "attracting friends." "Liú Yǐn" means that current matters continue or stagnate, and it is a "day to assess the situation and take action." If things are good, they continue; if they are bad, countermeasures should be taken.

### Senpu: First Mover Loses --

A day when urgent matters should be avoided. It is said that disputes and official business are also unfavorable, and it is best to remain calm in all matters. It means "the first to act will lose," corresponding to Senshō. It is said that on Senpu days, the morning is inauspicious and the afternoon is auspicious.

In the past, "Senpu" was sometimes written as "Shōkichi" (小吉, minor auspiciousness) or "Shūkichi" (周吉, surrounding auspiciousness), and was considered an auspicious day. The current interpretation arose from a forced interpretation of the characters.

> **Li's Comment**: No need to wake up early on this day; sleeping until noon can ward off disaster.

### Butsumetsu: All Merits Dissipate

Butsumetsu (ぶつめつ) is the most inauspicious day among the Rokuyō. Originally called "Kyomō" (虚亡), meaning no win or loss, it was later also called "Kūbō" (空亡). People interpreted it as everything being empty, so it was renamed "Butsumetsu" (物滅, things perish), and then transformed to mean the absence of Buddha's merits, thus using the character "佛" (Buddha). However, critics point out that historically, the notation "佛滅" first appeared in the "Banreki Ryōmen Kagami" compiled in Enkyō 4 (1747), and subsequent editions also used this notation, while the notation "物滅" first appeared in the "Ansei Zassho Banreki Taisei" (1854).

Butsumetsu day is considered unsuitable for all matters. It is the most inauspicious day in Rokuyō, and there is a custom of avoiding celebratory events such as weddings. Few people choose to hold weddings on this day. Therefore, some wedding venues offer discounts on Butsumetsu days. While other Rokuyō have multiple readings, Butsumetsu only has one reading, "ぶつめつ".

People often mistakenly interpret it literally as the day of Buddha's (Shakyamuni's) Nirvana (death). In the "Bunsei Ni U no Toshi Nenjū Kyōkun Uta Zen" from Bunsei 2 (1819), there is already an explanation for Butsumetsu: "It is said to be the anniversary of Buddha's death, unsuitable for all matters...". However, as mentioned above, Rokuyō did not originate from Buddhism and is unrelated to it. The day of Shakyamuni's death is considered to be February 15th, and it is merely a coincidence that the 15th of the second lunar month is always a Butsumetsu day.

Some also say: "On this day, one should be cautious in all matters, illness will be prolonged, but Buddhist services are permissible."

Furthermore, some interpret "物滅" (things perish) as "once things perish, new things begin," believing that this day is more suitable for starting new things than "Taian."

# x ccal tiaoxiu

View upcoming holidays, weekends, and make-up work days from a starting date.



Output fields: date, weekday, xiuxi (假/工/休), reason
- 假 = 假日 (holiday or holiday-adjacent weekend)
- 工 = 工作日 (make-up work day)
- 休 = 休息日 (regular weekend)


::: tip
TTY outputs colorful table / Pipe outputs TSV format
:::


## Examples

View next 30 days of holidays and weekends

```sh
x ccal tiaoxiu -n 30
```

View full year holidays and weekends

```sh
x ccal tiaoxiu -n 365 2026-01
```

Show holidays and work days only, exclude plain weekend rest

```sh
x ccal tiaoxiu --hide-plain-rest -n 30
```

## Usage

```sh
x ccal tiaoxiu [FLAGS] <#1>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | Start date (YYYY-MM-DD, defaults to today) |


## Flags

| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `-n`, `--count` | Number of days to look ahead (default: 50) |
| `--hide-plain-rest` | Exclude normal weekend rest days (休), show only holidays (假) and make-up work days (工) |
| `--yml` | Output in YML list format. |
| `--tsv` | Output in TSV (tab-separated values) format |
| `--csv` | Output in CSV (comma-separated values) format |
| `--tty` | Force TTY mode (table format output) |

# x cd (1) - History Directory

## Interactive History Directory Search

Running the `x cd` command, **x-cmd** provides an interactive APP where users can search history directories and navigate to them.

```sh
x cd
```

Additionally, `x cd` provides the `c` command as a short name. For example, `c <dir>` is equivalent to `x cd <dir>`.

## Filter History Directories by Keyword

Running the `c ,[keyword]` command ensures that the interactive APP only displays history directories related to the keyword.

For example, to ensure the interactive APP only displays history directories whose paths contain the string "src":

```sh
c ,src           # Equivalent to `x cd ,src` command
```

::: tip Quick Jump
If only one directory matches the keyword filter, it switches directly to that directory instead of providing an interactive APP.
:::

## Preserve Original `cd` Command Usage Habits

The `c` command preserves the original usage habits of the `cd` command. Transitioning from `cd` to `c` won't add extra burden to users.

::::ul
:::li `c ..` - Jump to parent directory
:::li `c -` - Switch to previous directory
::::

---
url: /mod/cd/cookbook-2.md
---

# x cd (2) - Directory Backtracking

## Interactive Search for Parent Directories

The `c ...` command is an alias for the `c -b` command. After executing the `c ...` command, **x-cmd** will provide an interactive app allowing users to search and jump to all parent directories.

```sh
c ...
```

![c ...](/image/mod/cd.2_1.webp)

When using the `cd` command, `..` usually represents the parent directory. Therefore, **x-cmd** uses `...` to represent all parent directories.


## Backtracking to Parent Directories Matching a Keyword

Executing the `c .../[keyword]` command ensures that the opened interactive app only displays parent directories related to the keyword.

For example, to ensure that the opened interactive app only displays parent directories containing the string "src" in their path:

```sh
c .../src        # Equivalent to the `c -b src` command
```

![c .../src](/image/mod/cd.2_2.webp)


---
url: /mod/cd/cookbook-3.md
---

# x cd (3) - Abbreviation Exploration and Forward Exploration

## Exploring Directories using Abbreviated Paths

The `c` command supports searching for directories using abbreviated paths and jumping to them.

For example, with the command `c /u/b`. First, it checks if the `/u/b` directory exists. If it exists, it immediately changes the directory; otherwise, the user can choose to create the `/u/b` directory or search for similar directories (e.g., `/usr/bin`, `/Users/bun`).

```sh
c /u/b
```

If multiple similar directories exist, **x-cmd** will provide an interactive app for the user to further search and jump to the desired directory.

## Forward Exploration of Subdirectories

After executing the `c -f` command, **x-cmd** will provide an interactive app allowing the user to search and jump to all subdirectories.

```sh
c -f
```

Executing the `c -f [keyword]` command ensures that the opened interactive app only displays subdirectories related to the keyword.

For example, to ensure that the opened interactive app only displays subdirectories whose path contains the string "theme":

```sh
c -f theme
```

url: /mod/cd/cookbook-4.md

# x cd (4) - Directory Alias

## Setting a Directory Alias

`c -r <...>` is a shorthand for the `x cd --relm <...>` command.

Use the following command to set the directory alias `xcbin` to point to the `~/.x-cmd.root/bin` directory.

```sh
c -r set xcbin ~/.x-cmd.root/bin
```

## Using a Directory Alias

Generally, if a path starts with a colon `:`, it indicates the use of a directory alias.

For example, using the **directory alias `xcbin`** set in Demo 1 to jump to the `~/.x-cmd.root/bin` directory.

```sh
c :xcbin
```

## Listing Existing Directory Aliases

In an interactive scenario, **x-cmd** provides an interactive APP that allows users to quickly search and view existing directory aliases.

```sh
c -r ls
```

After selecting an option in the interactive APP and pressing Enter, a further operation menu will be provided, such as switching to the corresponding folder, deleting the directory alias, etc.

## Deleting a Directory Alias

Delete the directory alias `xcbin` set in Demo 1.

```sh
c -r rm xcbin
```

# x choco - Simplify Windows Package Management Using Chocolatey

## Introduction

The `x choco` module is a command-line tool designed for Windows system developers and administrators. It leverages the powerful Chocolatey package manager to simplify the installation, updating, and uninstallation of Windows software. `x choco` runs in environments like WSL2 or Git Bash without switching to PowerShell, improving work efficiency.


## Main Features

`x choco` provides the following core features:

::::ul

::: li **Package installation**
Use `install` for packages from Chocolatey feeds or local `nuspec` / `nupkg` files.

```bash
# Install package from Chocolatey source
x choco install <package_name>

# Install from local nuspec file
x choco install <path/to/nuspec>

# Install from local nupkg file
x choco install <path/to/nupkg>
```
:::

::: li **Uninstall**
Use `uninstall` to remove one or many packages (or `all`—use carefully).

```bash
# Uninstall single package
x choco uninstall <package_name>

# Uninstall multiple packages
x choco uninstall <package_name1> <package_name2> ...

# Uninstall all packages (use with caution!)
x choco uninstall all
```
:::

::: li **Proxy settings**
`x choco proxy` configures HTTP/HTTPS proxies for restricted networks.

```bash
# Configure proxy (example)
x choco proxy --http-proxy http://your_proxy:port --https-proxy http://your_proxy:port
```
:::

::: li **Elevated runs**
Use `x choco admin` when a Chocolatey operation must run as administrator.

```bash
# Install package with admin privileges
x choco admin install <package_name>
```
:::

::: li **Native `choco` passthrough**
`x choco -- <choco_command>` forwards to the stock Chocolatey CLI for full feature coverage.

```bash
# Execute native choco search command
x choco -- search <keyword>
```
:::

::::


## Advanced Usage

### Configuration Files

(This section can be supplemented with explanations about configuration files, such as how to configure default sources and how to manage multiple configuration files for different environments.)


### Completion Hints

`x choco` provides command completion functionality, making it convenient for users to quickly input commands and parameters. (This section can be supplemented with instructions on how to enable completion hints.)


## Examples

Here are some usage examples for `x choco`:

::::ul

::: li Install Git

```bash
x choco install git
```
:::

::: li Uninstall Node.js

```bash
x choco uninstall nodejs
```
:::

::: li Search for packages containing "python"

```bash
x choco -- search python
```
:::

::: li Update Chocolatey with admin privileges

```bash
x choco admin upgrade chocolatey
```
:::

::::


## Summary

The `x choco` module greatly improves Windows system package management efficiency by simplifying Chocolatey usage. It is easy to use, powerful, and ideal for Windows developers and system administrators. Please visit [https://x-cmd.com](https://x-cmd.com) for more information.

# x cht - Command Line Cheat Sheet for Developers

## Introduction

The `x cht` module is a powerful command-line tool that helps developers quickly look up cheat sheets for various commands and programming languages. The module's data source is [cheat.sh](https://cht.sh/), a community-maintained knowledge base containing numerous programming languages, database systems, and Unix/Linux commands. `x cht` provides concise and clear examples for quick reference and specific feature lookup, like a "cheat sheet" you carry with you.

::: tip
Compared to lengthy help documentation, `x cht` provides more concise and easier-to-understand usage examples, helping you quickly master command usage. It complements `x tldr` and traditional help documentation:
- `x tldr`: Provides most commonly used short examples
- Help documentation: Provides detailed explanations
- `x cht`: Covers various features and usage of commands
:::


## Main Features

`x cht` provides the following main features:

:::: ul

::: li **Direct lookup**
Run `x cht <command|language>` for a command or language sheet—e.g. `x cht ls`, `x cht python`.
:::

::: li **Keyword search**
`x cht -s <keyword>` searches sheets with case-insensitive, recursive, and word-boundary options—e.g. `x cht -s python`, `x cht -s -r regex`.
:::

::: li **Special sheet types**
Also available:

- `x cht :learn <language>` — `learn-x-in-minutes` style intros
- `x cht :1line <language>` — one-liner collections
- `x cht :weirdness <language>` — odd or fun snippets

:::

::::

## Usage Examples

Here are some usage examples for `x cht`:

::::ul

::: li Get cheat sheet for `ls` command:

```bash
x cht ls
```
:::

::: li Get cheat sheet for Python language:

```bash
x cht python
```
:::

::: li Search for cheat sheets containing the "regex" keyword (case-insensitive, recursive search):

```bash
x cht -s -i -r regex
```
:::

::: li Get beginner-friendly Python cheat sheet:

```bash
x cht :learn python
```
:::

::: li Get one-liner code collection for Python:

```bash
x cht :1line python
```
:::

::: li List all available cheat sheets:

```bash
x cht -l
```
:::

::: li View `x cht` help information:

```bash
x cht -h  # or x cht --help or x cht :h
```
:::

::::


## Summary

`x cht` is an efficient and convenient command-line tool that helps developers quickly look up cheat sheets for various commands and programming languages, greatly improving development efficiency. Through concise commands and powerful search capabilities, `x cht` becomes a capable assistant in your development process. It is recommended to use in combination with `x tldr` and help documentation for more comprehensive information.

# x claude attribution



# Claude Code Quick Start Guide - x claude Tutorial

This guide will help you understand x claude's common features in minutes and quickly get started with Claude Code, experiencing the capabilities of an intelligent AI programming agent.

## 1. Zero Barrier! Auto-Install and Launch Claude Code

**You don't need to manually install Claude Code**. When you run the x claude command, x-cmd automatically detects whether Claude Code is installed in the current environment.
If not yet installed, x-cmd will automatically download, install, and configure it for you, with no manual operation required throughout the process. No need to manually deploy Node.js or handle dependency installation.

## 2. Model Freedom! Connect Claude, DeepSeek, Gemini, ChatGPT, Kimi, GLM, and More AI Models

### Connect Claude Official Models

Claude Code uses Anthropic's Claude series models (such as Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Opus 4.1, etc.) by default. Using these models requires logging into your Claude account.

- Login methods: When you first run x claude, the system will automatically prompt you to log in. You can choose either:
    * Claude.ai account (recommended): Suitable for individual subscription users. Simply log in with your Claude.ai account, no additional configuration needed.
    * Claude Console account: Suitable for developers and enterprise users. Log in via API Key, billed by actual usage, providing more flexible payment methods and higher usage quotas.

![1](/image/mod/claude.1_1.webp)

After login is complete, your credentials will be automatically encrypted and saved locally. No need to repeat login for subsequent use, the system will automatically read the saved credential information.

### Connect DeepSeek/Gemini and Other Models

Besides the Claude series models, x claude also supports connecting other AI models as the backend driver for Claude Code.

For example, you can easily switch Claude Code to use the DeepSeek model:
```bash
x deepseek init
x claude ds
```

![2](/image/mod/claude.1_2.webp)

After executing the above commands, Claude Code will automatically use the DeepSeek model for dialogue and programming assistance. Similarly, you can also connect Gemini, Kimi, Zhipu, and other models as needed.

For more detailed model connection methods, please refer to the corresponding documentation:
- [Connect GLM Model](/mod/claude/cookbook-2.md)
- [Connect DeepSeek Model](/mod/claude/cookbook-5.md)

## 3. Terminal Black Tech! Call x-cmd in Claude Code Dialogue

Claude Code has built-in terminal command execution capabilities. You can directly call `x` commands to perform system operations or scripts in the dialogue. Specific operations are as follows:

![3](/image/mod/claude.1_3.webp)

1. Use the `!` key in Claude Code dialogue to enter Bash mode (Bash mode).
2. Continue inputting the `x` command you want to execute (such as `x ip` command) in the dialogue box. After pressing Enter, Claude Code executes the command in the terminal environment and automatically incorporates the output into the dialogue context for further analysis, formatting, or processing.

You can also have Claude Code proactively call command line to complete tasks by mentioning x-cmd in the dialogue:

```bash
> Use x-cmd to get and analyze network interface information
```

Claude Code generates commands based on instructions, executes them, and returns structured results.

## 4. Extend AI Skills! Manage Claude Agent Skills with x-cmd

Claude Code supports the Agent Skills mechanism, allowing your Claude Code to better handle specific complex tasks through extended Skills, such as writing technical documents following brand guidelines, performing advanced data analysis, or reviewing code according to best practices. You can manage these Skills through the `skill` command of the `x claude` module. Here are common usage examples:

1. Query available professional skills (Skills): You can use the `x claude skill ll` command to query the list of Agent Skills shared by the **x-cmd platform and community**.
2. Add professional skills for Claude Code: After determining the needed skills, use the `x claude skill use` command to quickly install from remote repositories or local paths.

![4](/image/mod/claude.1_4.webp)

> Important: After installation is complete, please be sure to restart Claude Code to ensure the new Agent Skills are successfully loaded and activated.

For more content about `x claude skill`, please refer to the following article:
- [x claude skill - AI Agent Professional Skill Management](/mod/claude.md)

# Claude Code Connect to Moore Threads Domestic GPU Tutorial - x claude mthreads Configuration Guide

## 🤔 Why Choose `x claude mthreads`?

1.  **🇨🇳 Domestic Independent and Controllable**: MTT S5000 domestic GPU provides full-precision computing capabilities, deep optimization of software and hardware collaboration, no more worries about computing power "bottlenecks".
2.  **⚡ High Cost-Performance**: Limited-time 30-day free trial, daily limit of 100 developers; subsequent package prices are only 1/3 of Claude Pro, with usage more than 3 times.
3.  **🧠 Programming Model**: GLM-4.7 model ranks in the first tier of the Code Arena leaderboard, optimized specifically for code scenarios.
4.  **🔧 Zero Barrier Access**: Say goodbye to tedious configuration, no need to study environment variables or Base URL, complete adaptation in 10 seconds.

## 🚀 Quick Start

You don't need to configure complex proxies or manually edit `config` files, just follow these steps:

### 1️⃣ Configure Moore Threads API Key

After obtaining the [Moore Threads API Key](https://code.mthreads.com/), you don't need to manually modify complex configuration files. Simply use `x-cmd`'s interactive command to complete environment initialization.

```bash
# Configure mthreads API key
x mthreads init
```

- **Interactive Configuration**: The system will prompt you to enter the API Key you just obtained and set the AI model to use (such as glm-4.7).

- **Automatic Save**: x-cmd will automatically configure the key securely into global environment variables for subsequent calls by `x claude` and mthreads-related modules.

### 2️⃣ One Command Opens a New World

Enter directly in the terminal:

```bash
x claude mt
```

Once setup is complete, it will automatically complete all adaptation work for you (including dependency installation and environment configuration) and directly launch the familiar Claude Code interface.

### 3️⃣ Start Coding!

Now you can give it commands as usual:
*   "Help me refactor this Python project and optimize performance bottlenecks."
*   "Based on the latest Chinese technical documentation, help me write a module."
*   "Analyze potential issues in this code and explain in Chinese."

You'll find that it not only responds quickly but also that GLM-4.7's comprehension capabilities in Chinese programming scenarios are very accurate.

## ❓ Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### ❌ Q1: Will using x claude mt affect Claude Code's original functionality?

No. The essence of `x claude mt` is replacing the underlying inference engine (Model Backend). Claude Code's powerful Agent capabilities (such as reading files, executing test commands, searching code) are still retained, it just now follows the GLM-4.7 model's instruction scheduling.

### 🔑 Q2: Do I need to enter the API Key every time I use it?

No. `x-cmd` will securely manage your configuration. After the first configuration is complete, you only need to enter `x claude mt` to directly enter working state.

### 💪 Q3: Is GLM-4.7's programming capability really strong enough?

GLM-4.7 is a highly efficient programming model deeply optimized by Moore Threads in collaboration with Silicon Flow, ranking in the first tier of the Code Arena leaderboard. In actual testing, it has strong logical reasoning capabilities for long contexts. Combined with MTT S5000's full-precision computing power, both response speed and code quality are guaranteed.

### 🌐 Q4: What's the difference from other domestic model adapters (such as x claude kimi)?

Both provide excellent domestic model experiences, but with slightly different focuses:
- **x claude kimi**: Kimi Code model has more advantages in ultra-long context (2 million words) and Chinese document understanding, suitable for handling large-scale legacy code bases.
- **x claude mt**: Based on MTT S5000 domestic GPU computing power, GLM-4.7 performs excellently in code generation speed, with more competitive pricing, suitable for users pursuing cost-effectiveness and domestic alternatives.

# Claude Code Switch to Gemini 3.0 Model Tutorial - x claude router Configuration Guide

::: warning Important Notice
**claude-code-router is no longer functional.** Claude Code changed its internal authentication logic in version 2.x, but claude-code-router has not been adapted. The project's last code update was on 2026-01-06, and it appears to have been discontinued.

See [claude-code-router GitHub Issue](https://github.com/musistudio/claude-code-router/issues) for details.
:::

**`x claude router`** integrates [claude-code-router](https://github.com/musistudio/claude-code-router), allowing Claude Code to no longer be limited to Anthropic's models but to connect to Gemini 3.0.

## Step 1: Obtain Gemini API Key

To experience Gemini 3.0, you first need a key:

1.  Visit [Google AI Studio Platform](https://aistudio.google.com/app/api-keys) and log in with your Google account.
2.  Click **"Get API key"** to create a key.
    *   *Google provides a free tier for the Gemini series, sufficient to cover most personal developer Coding needs.*
    *   *Currently, there is no free tier for gemini-3-pro-preview in the Gemini API. You need to upgrade your Google account to a paid account to continue experiencing Gemini 3.0.*

## Step 2: Configure Routing Strategy

After obtaining the API Key, follow these steps to complete the configuration.

```bash
# 1. Configure Gemini API key
x gemini init
# You can also configure Gemini's API Key through x-cmd -> x gemini --cfg apikey="<your_api>"

# 2. Configure claude code to use Gemini 3.0 model
x claude router setup --gemini gemini-3-pro-preview
```

## Step 3: Launch Claude Code!

Everything is ready, now it's time to witness the "strongest on Earth" capabilities.

```bash
# Launch! Let Gemini 3.0 officially take over your Claude Code
x claude router code
```

- **Frontend Languages**: JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS
- **Scripting Languages**: Shell, Bash, PowerShell
- **Other Languages**: SQL, YAML, JSON, Markdown

In multilingual mixed projects, MiniMax M2.5 can accurately understand interaction logic between different languages and provide high-quality code suggestions.

# Claude Code Connect to Kimi Code Model Tutorial - AI Programming Assistant That Better Understands Chinese

## 🤔 Why Choose `x claude kimi`?

1.  **⚡ Simplified Configuration**: Say goodbye to tedious configuration, no need to read Claude Code documentation to figure out how to modify environment variables or Base URL.
2.  **🤝 Best of Both Worlds**: Retain Claude Code's excellent task orchestration and terminal execution capabilities while enjoying Kimi's deep expertise in Chinese comments and localized code standards.
3.  **⚡ Quick Configuration**: The entire adaptation process takes less than 5 seconds.

## 🚀 Quick Start

You don't need to configure complex proxies or manually edit `config` files, just follow these steps:

### 1️⃣ Configure Kimi Code API Key

After obtaining the [Kimi Code API Key](https://www.kimi.com/code/console), you don't need to manually modify complex configuration files. Simply use `x-cmd`'s interactive command to complete environment initialization.

```bash
# Configure Kimi Code API key
x kimi init
```

- **Interactive Configuration**: The system will prompt you to enter the API Key you just obtained and set the AI model to use (such as kimi-for-code).

- **Automatic Save**: x-cmd will automatically configure the key securely into global environment variables for subsequent calls by `x claude` and kimi-related modules.

### 2️⃣ One Command Opens a New World

Enter directly in the terminal:

```bash
x claude kimi
```

After configuration is complete, it will automatically complete all adaptation work for you (including dependency installation and environment configuration) and directly launch the familiar Claude Code interface.

### 3️⃣ Start Coding!

Now you can give it commands as usual:
*   "Help me analyze the performance bottleneck of this React component."
*   "Based on the latest Chinese interface documentation, help me write an API call module."
*   "Add detailed Chinese comments to this logic."

You'll find that it not only responds quickly but also understands Chinese requirements very accurately.

## ❓ Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### ❌ Q1: Will using x claude kimi affect Claude Code's original functionality?

No. The essence of `x claude kimi` is replacing the underlying inference engine (Model Backend). Claude Code's powerful Agent capabilities (such as reading files, executing test commands, searching code) are still retained, it just now follows Kimi's instruction scheduling.

### 🔑 Q2: Do I need to enter the API Key every time I use it?

No. `x-cmd` will securely manage your configuration. After the first configuration is complete, you only need to enter `x claude kimi` to directly enter working state.

### 💪 Q3: Is Kimi's model really strong enough for handling code?

`x claude kimi` connects to the **kimi-for-code** model specifically optimized for code scenarios. In actual testing, it has strong logical reasoning capabilities for long contexts, especially when handling large-scale legacy code bases. Combined with Claude Code's search functionality, the results often exceed expectations.

# Activate DeepSeek-V4-Pro Max Mode and 1M Context, Unleash the Full Power of China's Flagship Model

DeepSeek-V4-Pro is currently China's strongest coding model:

- **Top-Tier Code Performance**: Codeforces 3206 (surpassing GPT-5.4), LiveCodeBench 93.5, SWE Verified 80.6%
- **Million-Token Context**: 1M context window, effortlessly handling large codebases
- **Max Reasoning Mode**: Significantly deeper reasoning when enabled, optimized for complex programming tasks

`x claude ds` comes pre-configured with Max mode and 1M context out of the box—no manual tuning required.

## Quick Start

### Step 1: Configure DeepSeek API Key

After obtaining an API Key from the [DeepSeek Platform](https://platform.deepseek.com/api_keys), configure it with a single command:

```bash
x deepseek --cfg apikey=<DeepSeek API Key>
```

### Step 2: Launch Claude Code

```bash
x claude ds
```

That's it.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### Q: What does `x claude ds` configure automatically?

`x claude ds` handles three things behind the scenes:

| Configuration | Auto-Set Value | Purpose |
|--------|-----------|------|
| Model | `deepseek-v4-pro[1m]` | Activates million-token context window |
| Reasoning Mode | `max` | Enables the strongest reasoning capability |
| Subagent Model | `deepseek-v4-flash` | Automatically switches to lightweight model for simple tasks, balancing speed and cost |

`max` mode dramatically increases reasoning depth, allowing the model to think more thoroughly before responding. The improvement is especially noticeable for complex algorithms, multi-file refactors, and non-trivial bug fixes.

### Q: Why is DeepSeek-V4-Pro + Max mode the top choice for coding?

DeepSeek-V4-Pro's API pricing is only 1/5 to 1/10 of mainstream international models. For developers who frequently use AI-assisted programming, long-term use can save over 80% in costs.

### Q: How do I set DeepSeek-V4-Pro as Claude Code's default model?

Run the following command to write the `x claude ds` DeepSeek configuration to `~/.claude/settings.json`. After that, every `claude` command will automatically use DeepSeek:

```bash
x claude use ds
```

### Q: Do I need to manually enable Max mode or 1M context?

No. `x claude ds` uses the `deepseek-v4-pro[1m]` model with reasoning effort set to `max` by default—no configuration needed.

### Q: What's the difference between V4-Flash and V4-Pro?

| | V4-Pro | V4-Flash |
|---|---|---|
| Positioning | Flagship, strongest code capability | Lightweight, extreme cost-efficiency |
| Total Parameters | 1.6T | 284B |
| Active Parameters | 49B | 13B |
| Best For | Complex architecture, large refactors | Daily completions, simple Q&A |

`x claude ds` uses V4-Pro as the main model and V4-Flash as the subagent model, balancing performance and cost.

# Claude Code OpenRouter Multi-Model Gateway Tutorial - x claude openrouter Configuration Guide

[OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai) is a unified LLM API gateway that aggregates hundreds of models from vendors like Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, and DeepSeek behind a single OpenAI-compatible interface. This tutorial walks you through the entire integration with `x claude openrouter`.

## 🚀 Quick Start

The whole flow takes just three steps: get a Key → initialize the config → launch Claude Code.

::::ol
:::li Get an OpenRouter API Key
Go to [openrouter.ai/keys](https://openrouter.ai/keys) to sign up and create a new API Key. We recommend creating a dedicated Key for Claude Code so you can manage usage and quotas by purpose later.
:::

:::li Configure OpenRouter
Run a single command to enter the interactive setup:
```bash
x openrouter init
```
The system will prompt you to paste the API Key you just obtained, and you can also set a default primary model and a sub-agent model at the same time. Once setup is complete, x-cmd securely writes the Key, the endpoint, and the default models into environment variables for `x claude openrouter` and other OpenRouter-related modules to read.

![1](/image/mod/claude.4_1.webp)
:::

:::li Launch Claude Code
After initialization, run this in your terminal:
```bash
x claude openrouter
```
x-cmd will automatically inject the following environment variables into the Claude Code process:

- `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` — routes requests to the OpenRouter gateway
- `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<your OpenRouter Key>` — replaces the official authentication
- `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` — the default primary model used at startup
- `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL` — the lightweight model used by sub-agents

Once started, you can talk to Claude Code exactly as before: file reads/writes, code search, terminal commands, Agent Skills, and other capabilities are unaffected by the backend swap.
:::
::::

## 🧠 Switching Models Inside Claude Code

The real value of the OpenRouter gateway is "one endpoint, many models." Once you're connected, you can switch the underlying model without restarting Claude Code:

- **Specify before launch**: During `x openrouter init`, pick a primary model and a sub-agent model — for example `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`, `openai/gpt-5.4`, `google/gemini-2.5-pro`, `deepseek/deepseek-chat`, etc.
- **Switch on the fly**: In a Claude Code conversation, use the `/model` command to pick the model for the current session — the switch takes effect instantly.
- **Compare on demand**: In the same project, use different models for different sub-tasks (e.g. Claude for architecture design, a cheaper Flash model for completions and lightweight work).

The full model catalog is available at [openrouter.ai/models](https://openrouter.ai/models), with filters for price, context length, tool-call support, and more.

## ❓ Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### 💸 Q1: What does it cost to use OpenRouter?

OpenRouter uses transparent token-based billing and is usually more cost-effective than calling vendor APIs directly. You can view usage and costs in real time on the OpenRouter console.

### 🛠️ Q2: Will Claude Code's original features be affected?

No. `x claude openrouter` only swaps out the inference engine. Claude Code's core capabilities — file operations, code search, terminal execution, and more — are fully preserved.

### 🚀 Q3: Which model is best for me?

That depends on your specific needs:
- Want the latest tech-stack support → **GPT-5**
- Care most about code quality and architecture → **Claude 4.5 Sonnet**
- Need strong multilingual support → **Gemini Pro**
- Prefer the open-source ecosystem → **Llama 3**

We recommend trying different models in real projects to find the AI partner that best fits your workflow.

# Claude Code Status Bar Theme Customization Tool - x claude stl 70+ Color Schemes

Use the `x claude stl` command to control the status bar at the bottom of the Claude Code terminal interface, creating your personal immersive Claude Code development environment.

- 📊 Information Overview: The status bar is not just decoration, it's a dashboard. It can display current model, token consumption, working path, and context status in real-time, giving you a clear view of environment information while programming.
- 🎨 Style Definition: Break free from the default interface. By switching between multiple color themes like el, ice, dracula, etc., integrate Claude Code into your terminal color scheme.
- 🚀 Quick Switching: No tedious configuration files needed, just one command to freely switch between different layouts and styles, meeting aesthetic needs in different scenarios.

## Default Theme (el)

If you want to use the default el (Elegant) theme style, you can directly run the setup command. This is typically the recommended initial configuration method.

```bash
x claude stl setup
```

![1](/image/mod/claude.5_1.webp)

## More Themes

`x claude stl` supports multiple popular color schemes. Use the `--theme` parameter to specify your preferred theme.

### Ice Theme

Suitable for users who prefer a fresh, cool-toned interface.

```bash
x claude stl setup --theme ice
```

![2](/image/mod/claude.5_2.webp)

### Dracula Theme

Classic dark high-contrast theme, suitable for long programming sessions.

```bash
x claude stl setup --theme dracula
```

![3](/image/mod/claude.5_3.webp)

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### Q1: What themes are supported?

`x claude stl` currently has 70+ carefully selected color schemes built-in, covering everything from classic Solarized and Monokai to modern Dracula and Nord styles, sufficient to meet the aesthetic needs of most developers.

You don't need to memorize all theme names. After entering `x claude stl setup --theme`, press the TAB key to view and select from all currently supported theme lists.

### Q2: Do I need to restart Claude Code after changing themes?

No. x-cmd aims to provide a seamless configuration experience. Typically, after running the command and successfully switching themes, the configuration takes effect immediately. You don't need to interrupt your current workflow or restart Claude Code, the new status bar style will be instantly presented at the bottom of your terminal.

### Q3: Can I fully customize colors or layouts?

User customization features are not currently available.

The current mechanism is based on quick switching between preset high-quality theme libraries. If the existing theme library cannot meet your needs, or if you have a specific color scheme you'd like to see included, feel free to [submit an Issue in the project repository](https://github.com/x-cmd/x-cmd), and we'll consider adding support in future updates.

# Claude Code Session Management Tool - x claude session Interactive History Review and Cleanup

As the frequency of using Claude Code increases, a large number of session history files will accumulate locally. These historical records are often filled with a large amount of worthless data, such as empty sessions, temporary sessions with only one test sentence, and may even contain sensitive project information that should not be retained. Moreover, this redundant data not only takes up space but also makes it extremely difficult to use the `resume` command to restore work, and manually confirming and deleting these files one by one is too tedious.

To address this, `x claude sess` provides a complete toolset that helps you quickly trace history through an **FZF interactive interface** and provides convenient cleanup mechanisms to keep your development environment clean.

## Core Highlight: FZF Interactive Preview

`x claude sess` integrates the FZF terminal application, allowing you to browse conversations through an interactive interface, intuitively seeing when sessions occurred, which projects they belong to, and brief content.

**This is the best tool for reviewing "What did I have Claude change last week?"**

![1](/image/mod/claude.6_1.webp)

Run the following command to launch:

```bash
x claude sess
```

Additionally, after finding the target session, simply select it and press Enter to bring up the action menu. You can quickly perform the following operations without memorizing complex command parameters:

![2](/image/mod/claude.6_2.webp)

- Resume conversation: Directly restore context and continue unfinished tasks.
- View details: Read the complete content of the session in full-screen mode.
- Delete session: Directly clean up this useless or erroneous session.

## Stay Tidy: Session Cleanup

When too many historical sessions affect work efficiency, regular cleanup is necessary. `x claude sess rm` provides safe and flexible deletion functionality.

### 1. Safe Preview (Dry Run)

Before executing deletion, it's recommended to first view what will be deleted to prevent accidental deletion of important records:

```bash
# Only display sessions that will be deleted, do not execute actual operation
x claude sess rm --dry-run <session_id>
```

![3](/image/mod/claude.6_3.webp)

### 2. Batch Deletion

Supports deleting multiple specified session IDs at once, quickly cleaning up garbage sessions:

```bash
x claude sess rm <session_id_1> <session_id_2> <session_id_3>
```

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### Q1: Can I view all Claude Code history without entering specific project directories?

Yes. Using `x claude sess ls -a` can list historical sessions under all project paths on this machine. Similarly, in FZF interactive mode, global indexes are typically loaded (depending on specific configuration), allowing you to search for context across projects.

### Q2: How can I view the complete content of an old session without deleting it?

If you don't need interactive search and just want to quickly print out the content of a session (for example, to copy into a document), you can use the `cat` or `preview` command:

- `x claude sess preview <session_id>`: Displays the conversation flow in a concise and readable format (what User asked, what Assistant answered), suitable for quick review.
- `x claude sess cat <session_id>`: Outputs conversation data in TSV/JSON format, suitable for secondary processing (such as counting token usage, analyzing prompt patterns).

# Claude Code Auto-Configure MCP Servers and Skill Packs - x claude create Complete Guide

## ✨ Core Features: One-Stop Environment Setup

`x claude cr` will automatically configure the following core components for you:

- 🔌 **MCP Servers**: Automatically install and configure the most practical Model Context Protocol servers.
- 🎯 **Skill Pack System**: Pre-install practical skill packs such as frontend design and skill creation to extend Claude's professional capabilities.
- 🛠️ **Development Toolchain**: Integrate Chrome DevTools, code analysis tools, etc., to create a complete development ecosystem.

## 🚀 Quick Start

### 1️⃣ Basic Environment: Ready with One Click

Run the following command in the project root directory to quickly set up a standard development environment:

```bash
x claude cr
```

This will automatically configure:
- 🐙 **GitHub MCP**: Directly read GitHub repository code, create PRs, and manage Issues in conversations.
- 🧠 **Memory MCP**: Give Claude long-term memory to remember your project specifications and preferences.
- 💭 **Sequential-thinking MCP**: Enable "deep thinking" mode, making AI steps more rigorous when handling complex logic.
- 📁 **Filesystem MCP**: Provide safer, more compliant local file operation capabilities.
- 🎨 **Skill Packs**: Pre-install frontend design and skill creation tools to make AI more business-aware.

### 2️⃣ Advanced Mode: Customize as Needed

If you're a full-stack developer or need specific toolchains, we also support more flexible configurations:

*   **Want browser control capabilities?** (Web scraping, UI testing)
    ```bash
    x claude cr --chrome
    ```
*   **Need deep code analysis?** (Use Serena engine for refactoring suggestions)
    ```bash
    x claude cr --serena
    ```
*   **Adults want it all?** (Install all available tools, build complete configuration)
    ```bash
    x claude cr --all
    ```

## ❓ Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### Q1: If I've already configured Claude Code, will running this overwrite my configuration?

**Rest assured, it won't.** `x claude cr` uses an incremental configuration strategy. It will intelligently detect existing MCP servers and tools, **only installing missing parts**. Your original custom configurations will be preserved.

### Q2: What should I do if an error occurs during installation?

Usually, it's because basic dependencies (such as `npm` or `python`) are missing. `x claude cr` will attempt automatic repair, but if it fails, please check your network connection or permissions. You can also diagnose issues through `x claude doctor` (if this feature exists) or by viewing logs.

### Q3: How do I remove these configurations?

`x claude cr` focuses on "installation". If you want to remove an MCP server, you can use Claude Code's MCP management command:

```bash
x claude mcp remove <server-name>
```

Or manually edit configuration files for cleanup.

### Q4: What is Sequential-thinking? What's it for?

This is a powerful MCP tool. It forces Claude to perform structured logical reasoning in a hidden block before outputting code. **For complex refactoring tasks or algorithm problems, enabling this feature can significantly reduce AI hallucination rates and improve code accuracy.**

Project URL: https://github.com/musistudio/claude-code-router
:::


## Examples

Start the claude-code-router service

Regenerate the routing configuration using Google Gemini (gemini-3-pro-preview)

Use Claude Code to generate a “Hello World” example


## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x claude router setup](#x-claude-router-setup) | Regenerate the claude-code-router configuration file based on the model provider |

Regenerate the claude-code-router configuration file based on the model provider


- **Examples**:

Regenerate the routing configuration using Google Gemini (gemini-2.5-flash)

```sh
x claude router setup
```

Regenerate the routing configuration using Google Gemini (gemini-3-pro-preview)

```sh
x claude router setup --gemini gemini-3-pro-preview
```

Generate the routing configuration using DeepSeek (deepseek-chat) with an explicitly provided API key

```sh

```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x claude router setup [OPTIONS]
```

- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--gemini` |  | Use Google Gemini as the model provider |
| `--openai` |  | Use OpenAI as the model provider |
| `--deepseek` |  | Use DeepSeek as the model provider |
| `--openrouter` |  | Use OpenRouter as the model provider |
| `--apikey` |  | Explicitly specify the API key (if not specified, it will attempt to be obtained from the corresponding module) |
| `--proxy` |  | Set a proxy for API requests, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:7890 |

# x claude session

Manage local Claude Code sessions

## Examples

Launch the FZF app to interactively browse and manage local sessions (alias of `x claude sess fz`)

```sh
x claude sess
```

List sessions from all projects in TSV format

```sh
x claude sess ls -a -t
```

Preview removal of a session without actually deleting it

```sh
x claude sess rm --dry-run <sessionId>
```

Remove multiple specified local sessions

```sh
x claude sess rm <sessionId-1> <sessionId-n>
```

Preview a session in a concise, human-readable form

```sh
x claude sess preview <sessionId>
```

Extract specified session content to the default directory

```sh
x claude sess extract --session <sessionId>
```

Extract specified session content to ./out directory

```sh
x claude sess extract --session <sessionId> --output ./out
```

Export current project session data

```sh
x claude sess export
```

Export current project session data to backup.tar.gz file

```sh
x claude sess export -p . -o backup.tar.gz
```

Export current project session data and upload to hub

```sh
x claude sess export -o -
```

Import session data from backup.tar.gz to current project

```sh
x claude sess import backup.tar.gz
```

Import session data from backup.tar.gz to specified project

```sh
x claude sess import -p /path/to/project backup.tar.gz
```

# x claude use

Configure claude-code to use a specified third-party model provider


::: tip Use the `use` command to switch claude-code to a third-party model provider (e.g., DeepSeek, Kimi, etc.).
This command modifies ~/.claude/settings.json to set the appropriate environment variables.

Supported providers: ds/deepseek, kimi, mm/minimax, mt/mthreads, glm/zhipu, sili, openrouter, doubao, ali, baidu, tencent, custom/other



Choosing the right approach:
- For on-demand use with different models, use commands like `x claude mm` (MiniMax), `x claude glm` (Zhipu), `x claude or` (OpenRouter), etc. These commands fetch the API key from the corresponding module and run claude-code directly
- If you want the `claude` command to permanently use a specific provider (e.g., always use Zhipu glm when running `claude`), use `x claude use glm`, which writes the configuration to ~/.claude/settings.json
- If you only want to use a specific provider for the current project, use `x claude use --project glm`, which writes the configuration to .claude/settings.local.json in the current project
:::


## Examples

Configure claude-code to use the DeepSeek V4 model (global)

```sh
x claude use ds
```

Use Zhipu glm model for the current project (project-level only)

```sh
x claude use --project glm
```

Use MiniMax model for the current project (project-level only)

```sh
x claude use --project mm
```

Configure claude-code to use Xiaomi Token Plan

```sh
x claude use other "https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/anthropic" MIMO_API_KEY mimo-v2.5-pro
```

Configure claude-code to use the local ollama service with the gpt-oss:20b model

```sh
x claude use other "http://localhost:11434" "ollama" "gpt-oss:20b"
```

## Usage

```sh
x claude use [FLAGS] <#1> <#2> <#3> <#4> <#5>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | Model provider name<br>`ds` &#124; `deepseek` &#124; `kimi` &#124; `mm` &#124; `minimax` ... |
| `#2` | Custom API endpoint URL |
| `#3` | API key |
| `#4` | Model name |
| `#5` | Fast model name (optional, defaults to model name) |


## Flags

| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--project`, `-p` | Write configuration to project-level settings.local.json (.claude/settings.local.json) instead of global |

# <span class="flex items-center justify-between gap-1"><span>x claw</span> <span class="text-x-brand">🔥</span></span> connect

Connect to IM platform(s) and activate message listener channel. Supports multiple platforms at once.


::: tip
Automatically ensures the corresponding IM background service is started before connecting. The background service is auto-started on connect and stopped on disconnect.
:::

::: tip
When connecting to a Feishu group, the chatid is the group ID starting with oc_. Use `x feishu group ls` to list available groups and their IDs. Make sure Feishu app is configured first (x feishu init).
:::

::: tip
View active connections with `x claw connect --ls`
:::


## Examples

Scenario: After service is up, connect WeChat, Telegram, and all Feishu groups at once

```sh
x claw connect weixin telegram feishu:groups
```

Scenario: Connect to a specific Feishu group on demand (e.g. for a particular discussion)

```sh
x claw connect feishu:oc_xxx
```

Scenario: Connect WeChat alone, suitable for single-platform-only setups

```sh
x claw connect weixin
```

Scenario: Check which IM connections are currently active

```sh
x claw connect --ls
```

## Usage

```sh
x claw connect [FLAGS] <#1>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | IM platform identifier, multiple allowed. Format is `im` or `im:chatid`.
weixin, telegram, qywx can be used directly; feishu requires chatid, e.g. `feishu:groups` or `feishu:oc_xxx`.
<br>`weixin` &#124; `telegram` &#124; `qywx` &#124; `feishu` &#124; `feishu:groups` |


## Flags

| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--ls` | List currently activated connections |
