### x gh run ls

Interactive UI show workflow runs information


- **Examples**:

Interactive table displaying the workflows of the x-cmd/xx repository

```sh
x gh action run ls -r x-cmd/xx
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gh run ls [OPTIONS] [FLAGS]
```

- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; |  | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--branch` &lt;branch&gt; |  | Returns workflow runs information associated with a branch |
| `--actor` &lt;username&gt; |  | returns someone workflow runs information |
| `--event` &lt;event&gt; |  | Returns workflow runs information triggered by the event you specify |
| `--sta`, `--status` &lt;status&gt; |  | Returns workflow runs information with the check run status |
| `--created` &lt;ISO 8601&gt; |  | Returns workflow runs information created within the given date-time range |
| `--check_suite_id` &lt;id&gt; |  | Returns workflow runs information with the check_suite_id that you specify |
| `--page` &lt;num&gt; |  | target page |
| `--yml` |  | output yml data |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; | per_page data number |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |
| `--csv` | output csv data |
| `--exclude_pull_requests` | Not pull requests are omitted from the response |

# x gh secret

GitHub secret management

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x gh secret ls](#x-gh-secret-ls) | List secrets |
| [x gh secret set](#x-gh-secret-set) | Create or update secrets |
| [x gh secret rm](#x-gh-secret-rm) | Remove secrets |


### x gh secret ls

List secrets


- **Examples**:

List x-cmd organization secrets

```sh
x gh secret ls --org x-cmd
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gh secret ls [OPTIONS] [FLAGS]
```

- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--app` &lt;app_name&gt; |  | List secrets for a specific application |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--org` &lt;org_name&gt; | The organization name. The name is not case sensitive |
| `--secret_name` &lt;secret_name&gt; | Filter by organization secret name to list selected repos |
| `--page` &lt;num&gt; | target page |
| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; | per_page data number |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |
| `--csv` | output csv data |
| `--yml` | output yml data |


### x gh secret set

Create or update secrets


- **Examples**:

Create or update &lt;org_name&gt; organization action secrets

```sh
x gh secret set --org <org_name> <secret_name>=<secret_value>
```

Create or update &lt;owner/repo&gt; repository action secrets

```sh
x gh secret set --repo <owner/repo> <secret_name>=<secret_value>
```

Set multiple secrets imported from the ".env" file to &lt;owner/repo&gt; repository action secrets

```sh
x gh secret set --repo <owner/repo> --file .env
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gh secret set [OPTIONS] [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | Target secrets. &lt;secret_name&gt;=&lt;secret_value&gt; |


- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--file`, `-f` &lt;file_path&gt; |  | Load secret names and values from a dotenv-formatted file |
| `--app` &lt;app_name&gt; |  | Set the application for a secret. default action |
| `--visibility` &lt;visibility&gt; |  | Set visibility for an organization secret |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--org` &lt;org_name&gt; | The organization name. The name is not case sensitive |


### x gh secret rm

Remove secrets


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gh secret rm [OPTIONS] [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | The secret names |


- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--app` &lt;app_name&gt; |  | Target the application for a secret. default action |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--org` &lt;org_name&gt; | The organization name. The name is not case sensitive |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Ignore remove prompt interception |

::: tip * About Generating a new GPG key:

* ASCII-armored format e.g like: `-----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----...`

```sh

```

| Argument | Description |

| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--name` &lt;name&gt; | A descriptive name for the new key |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |

| [x gh wf view](#x-gh-wf-view) | List workflow runs summary for a workflow |
| [x gh wf run](#x-gh-wf-run) | Run a workflow by creating a workflow_dispatch event |
| [x gh wf disable](#x-gh-wf-disable) | Disable a workflow |
| [x gh wf enable](#x-gh-wf-enable) | Enable a workflow |


### x gh wf ls

Interactive UI show workflow information


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gh wf ls [OPTIONS] [FLAGS]
```

- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; |  | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--yml` |  | output yml data |
| `--page` &lt;num&gt; |  | target page |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; | per_page data number |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |
| `--csv` | output csv data |


### x gh wf ll

List the workflow in a repository


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gh wf ll [OPTIONS] [FLAGS]
```

- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; |  | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; |  | per_page data number |
| `--page` &lt;num&gt; |  | target page |


- **Flags**:

| ------- | ------- |

| `--csv` | output csv data |

### x gh wf view

List workflow runs summary for a workflow


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gh wf view|v [OPTIONS] [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | workflow ID (obtain by `x gh action workflow ls`) |


- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; |  | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--branch` &lt;branch&gt; |  | Returns workflow runs associated with a branch |
| `--actor` &lt;username&gt; |  | returns someone workflow runs |
| `--event` &lt;event&gt; |  | Returns workflow run triggered by the event you specify |
| `--sta`, `--status` &lt;status&gt; |  | Returns workflow runs with the check run status |
| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; |  | per_page data number |
| `--page` &lt;num&gt; |  | target page |
| `--created` &lt;ISO 8601&gt; |  | Returns workflow runs created within the given date-time range |
| `--check_suite_id` &lt;id&gt; |  | Returns workflow runs with the check_suite_id that you specify |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |
| `--exclude_pull_requests` | Not pull requests are omitted from the response |


### x gh wf run

Run a workflow by creating a workflow_dispatch event


- **Examples**:

Run the &lt;workflow_name is Lint&gt; workflow by creating a workflow_dispatch event

```sh
x gh action workflow run --repo <owner/repo> Lint
```

Run &lt;remote file .github/workflows/lint.yml&gt; workflow_dispatch event and use key and values parameter

```sh
x gh action workflow run --repo <owner/repo> -f name=x-cmd -f msg=hello lint.yml
x gh action workflow run --repo <owner/repo> --inputs '{"name":"x-cmd","msg":"hello"}' lint.yml

```

Run a workflow_dispatch event and use key and values parameter from stdin

```sh
echo '{"name":"x-cmd"}' | x gh action workflow run --repo <owner/repo> --inputs - .id=<workflow_id>
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gh wf run|dispatch [OPTIONS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | workflow &lt;name&gt; or &lt;relative_file_path&gt; or .id=&lt;workflow_id&gt; |


- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; |  | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--ref` &lt;branch&#124;tag&gt; |  | The git reference for the workflow. Empty will get default branch |
| `--inputs` &lt;key_val_json&gt; |  | Input keys and values parameter in the workflow file. '-' from stdin |
| `--field`, `-f` &lt;key=val&gt; |  | Input &lt;key&gt;=&lt;value&gt; parameter in the workflow file |

# x git ci

Record changes to the repository with optional AI-generated commit message


::: tip Without `-m`, automatically calls AI to generate a Conventional Commits compliant message based on `git diff`.
With `-m`, uses the specified message. Other arguments are passed through to native `git commit`.
:::


## Examples

Example: Auto-generate commit message with AI (based on git diff)

```sh
x git ci
```

Example: Commit with specified message

```sh
x git ci -m 'feat: add user login'
```

Example: Combine -m with --author

```sh
x git ci -m 'fix: typo' --author='name@email.com'
```

## Usage

```sh
x git ci|commit <#n>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#n` | extends `git commit` options (--amend, --author, -S, etc.) |

# x git cl

Lightweight clone, skip LFS large files (GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1)


::: tip `cl` is a lightweight version of `clone`, sets GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 to skip LFS files.
Good for quickly browsing repository code without large files.

Use `clone` for full clone (including LFS files).
:::


## Examples

Example: Lightweight clone GitHub repo, skip LFS

```sh
x git cl :gh/x-cmd/x-cmd
```

## Usage

```sh
x git cl [OPTIONS] [FLAGS] <#1> <#2>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | repository path or URL (supports :gh/:gt/:gl shortcuts) |
| `#2` | directory |


## Options

| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `-o`, `--origin` &lt;name&gt; |  | use &lt;name&gt; instead of 'origin' to track upstream |
| `-b`, `--branch` &lt;branch&gt; |  | checkout &lt;branch&gt; instead of the remote's HEAD |
| `-u`, `--upload-pack` &lt;path&gt; |  | path to git-upload-pack on the remote |
| `-j`, `--jobs` &lt;n&gt; |  | number of submodules cloned in parallel |
| `--separate-git-dir` &lt;gitdir&gt; |  | separate git dir from working tree |
| `--depth` &lt;depth&gt; |  | create a shallow clone of that depth |


## Flags

| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--recursive` | initialize all contained submodules |
| `--shallow-submodules` | any cloned submodules will be shallow |

# x git clone

Full clone with all options, auto-apply gitconfig after clone


::: tip `clone` is full-featured clone command, supports all git clone options.
Auto-enters directory and applies `x git config apply` after clone.

Supports various URL shortcuts:
- `:gh/user/repo` → git@github.com:user/repo
- `:gt/user/repo` → git@gitee.com:user/repo
- `:gl/user/repo` → git@gitlab.com:user/repo
- `repo` → auto-completes with default owner
:::


## Usage

```sh
x git clone [OPTIONS] [FLAGS] <#1> <#2>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | repository path or URL (supports :gh/:gt/:gl shortcuts) |
| `#2` | directory |


## Options

| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `-o`, `--origin` &lt;name&gt; |  | use &lt;name&gt; instead of 'origin' to track upstream |
| `-b`, `--branch` &lt;branch&gt; |  | checkout &lt;branch&gt; instead of the remote's HEAD |
| `-u`, `--upload-pack` &lt;path&gt; |  | path to git-upload-pack on the remote |
| `-j`, `--jobs` &lt;n&gt; |  | number of submodules cloned in parallel |
| `--separate-git-dir` &lt;gitdir&gt; |  | separate git dir from working tree |
| `--depth` &lt;depth&gt; |  | create a shallow clone of that depth |


## Flags

| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--recursive` | initialize all contained submodules |
| `--shallow-submodules` | any cloned submodules will be shallow |

# x git - Git Command Enhancement Tool

As a developer, do you work with Git every day? `x git` adds a series of practical features on top of native Git, making your Git workflow more efficient.

## Quick Start

```sh
x git status          # View status
x git br              # View branches
x git lg              # View commit history
```

## Common Operation Enhancements

Say goodbye to tedious Git operations:

::::ul
:::li `x git undo`
Undo the last operation, whether it's staging or committing, easily rollback
:::

:::li `x git recent`
View recently accessed branches for quick switching
:::

:::li `x git clean`
Clean untracked files with interactive selection support
:::
::::

## Interactive Operations

Interactive selection with fzf:

```sh
x git add -p          # Interactive staging
x git br fz           # Interactive branch selection
x git checkout fz     # Interactive checkout
```

## Commit Templates

Standardize commit messages, starting with templates:

```sh
x git commit          # Commit using template
x git cm "fix: bug"   # Quick commit
```

## Enhanced Logs

View more intuitive commit history:

```sh
x git lg
```

## Alias Reference

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `x git st` | status |
| `x git br` | branch |
| `x git co` | checkout |
| `x git lg` | Enhanced log |

::: tip
`x git` is fully compatible with native Git commands. You can freely choose to use enhanced features or native commands.
:::

# x git sp

Mainly for optimizing access to Bitbucket, Codeberg, GitHub, and GitLab in China, including setting up short names and configuring proxies

## Examples

Set http, https, and socks5 proxies for github, gitlab, codeberg, and bitbucket, with the address localhost:9999；This is the most common scenario

```sh
x git sp setup localhost:9999

```

View the configuration status of the current service provider

```sh
x git sp status

```

Clear the contents of setup

```sh
x git sp cleanup
```

Configure short names and set proxies using HTTP/SSH

```sh
x git sp setup --http socks5://localhost:9999 --ssh localhost:9999

```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x git sp setup](#x-git-sp-setup) | Initialize configuration service provider short name and set proxy |
| [x git sp cleanup](#x-git-sp-cleanup) | Clear the contents of setup |
| [x git sp status](#x-git-sp-status) | View the configuration status of the current service provider |


### x git sp setup

Initialize configuration service provider short name and set proxy


- **Examples**:

Set http, https, and socks5 proxies for github, gitlab, codeberg, and bitbucket, with the address localhost:9999；This is the most common scenario

```sh
x git sp setup localhost:9999

```

Setting up short names and configuring proxies using HTTP/SSH

```sh
x git sp setup --http socks5://localhost:9999 --ssh localhost:9999

```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x git sp setup [OPTIONS]
```

- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--http` |  | Setup proxy using the http protocol |
| `--ssh` |  | Setup proxy using the SSH protocol |
| `--proxy` |  | Setup proxy using both http and SSH protocols |


### x git sp cleanup

Clear the contents of setup


- **Usage**:

```sh
x git sp cleanup
```

### x git sp status

View the configuration status of the current service provider


- **Usage**:

```sh
x git sp status
```

# x gl cl

shortcut for `x gl repo clone`

## Usage

```sh
x gl cl [OPTIONS] [FLAGS] <#1> <#2>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | &lt;ownerPath&gt;/&lt;repoPath&gt; (default ownerPath: current user) |
| `#2` | directory |


## Options

| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `-o`, `--origin` &lt;name&gt; |  | use &lt;name&gt; instead of 'origin' to track upstream |
| `-b`, `--branch` &lt;branch&gt; |  | checkout &lt;branch&gt; instead of the remote's HEAD |
| `-u`, `--upload-pack` &lt;path&gt; |  | path to git-upload-pack on the remote |
| `-j`, `--jobs` &lt;n&gt; |  | number of submodules cloned in parallel |
| `--separate-git-dir` &lt;gitdir&gt; |  | separate git dir from working tree |
| `--depth` &lt;depth&gt; |  | create a shallow clone of that depth |


## Flags

| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--recursive` | initialize all contained submodules |
| `--shallow-submodules` | any cloned submodules will be shallow |

### x gl group ls

List all groups


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gl group ls [OPTIONS] [FLAGS]
```

- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--sort` |  | Order groups in asc or desc order |
| `--order_by` |  | Order groups by |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--search` | Return the list of authorized groups matching the search criteria |
| `--skip_groups` | Skip the group IDs passed |
| `--min_access_level` | Limit to groups where current user has at least this access level |
| `--owned` | Limit to groups explicitly owned by the current user |
| `--statistics` | Include group statistics |
| `--all_available` | Show all the groups you have access to |
| `--top_level_only` | Limit to top level groups, excluding all subgroups |
| `--with_custom_attributes` | Include custom attributes in response |
| `--per_page` | Results per page (max 100) |
| `--page` | Page number of the results to fetch |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |

### x gl group mr

List group merge request


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gl group mr [OPTIONS] [FLAGS]
```

- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--with_labels_details` |  | If true, the response returns more details for each label in labels field: :name, :color, :description, :description_html,:text_color.Default is false |
| `--with_merge_status_recheck` |  | If true, this projection requests (but does not guarantee) that the merge_status field be recalculated asynchronously |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--id` | The ID or URL-encoded path of the repo owned by the authenticated user |
| `--assignee_id` | Returns merge requests assigned to the given user id |
| `--author_id` | Return prs created by the given user id |
| `--author_username` | Return prs created by the given username |
| `--approved_by_ids` | Returns merge requests which have been approved by all the users with the given id, with a maximum of 5 |
| `--approver_ids` | Returns merge requests which have specified all the users with the given id as individual approvers |
| `--approved_by_usernames` | Returns merge requests which have been approved by all the users with the given username, with a maximum of 5 |
| `--created_after` | Return merge requests created on or after the given time. Expected in ISO 8601 format |
| `--created_before` | Return merge requests created on or before the given time |
| `--labels` | Return merge requests matching a comma-separated list of labels |
| `--milestone` | Return merge requests for a specific milestone |
| `--my_reaction_emoji` | Return merge requests reacted by the authenticated user by the given emoji |
| `--not` | Return merge requests that do not match the parameters supplied |
| `--non_archived` | Return merge requests from non archived projects only. Default is true |
| `--order_by` | Return requests ordered by created_at, title, or updated_at fields. Default is created_at |
| `--reviewer_id` | Returns merge requests which have the user as a reviewer with the given user id |
| `--reviewer_username` | Returns merge requests which have the user as a reviewer with the given username |
| `--scope` | Return merge requests for the given scope. Defaults to created_by_me |
| `--search` | Search merge requests against their title and description |
| `--sort` | Return requests sorted in asc or desc order. Default is desc |
| `--state` | Return all merge requests or just those that are opened, closed, locked, or merged |
| `--source_branch` | Return merge requests with the given source branch |
| `--target_branch` | Return merge requests with the given target branch |
| `--updated_after` | Return prs updated on or after the given time |
| `--updated_before` | Return prs updated on or before the given time |
| `--view` | If simple, returns the iid, URL, title, description, and basic state of merge request |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |

# x gl issue

issue management

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x gl issue ls](#x-gl-issue-ls) | List repo issue |
| [x gl issue create](#x-gl-issue-create) | Create repo issue |
| [x gl issue edit](#x-gl-issue-edit) | Edit repo issue |
| [x gl issue rm](#x-gl-issue-rm) | Delete repo issue |
| [x gl issue reopen](#x-gl-issue-reopen) | Reopen repo issue |
| [x gl issue close](#x-gl-issue-close) | Close repo issue |


### x gl issue ls

List repo issue


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gl issue ls [OPTIONS] [FLAGS]
```

- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--sort` |  | Return issues sorted in asc or desc order. Default is desc |
| `--order_by` |  | Return issues ordered by fields. Default is created_at |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--group`, `-g` &lt;group_path&#124;.id=group_id&gt; | Namespace for the new repo or .id=Namespace ID |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; or .id=&lt;repo_id&gt; |
| `--state` | Return all issues or just those that are opened or closed |
| `--labels` | Comma-separated list of label names, issues must have all labels to be returned |
| `--milestone` | Returns issues assigned to milestones title (None, Any) |
| `--assignee_id` | Return issues assigned to the given user id |
| `--assignee_username` | Return issues assigned to the given username |
| `--author_id` | Return issues created by the given user id |
| `--author_username` | Return issues created by the given username |
| `--search` | Search issues against their title and description |
| `--page` | target page |
| `--per_page` | per page data number |
| `--confidential` | Filter confidential or public issues |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gl issue create

Create repo issue


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gl issue create [OPTIONS] [FLAGS]
```

- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--issue_type` |  | The type of issue |
| `--confidential` |  | Set an issue to be confidential. Default is false |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; or .id=&lt;repo_id&gt; |
| `--title` | The title of an issue |
| `--iid` | The internal ID of the project issue (requires administrator or project owner riglts) |
| `--created_at` | When the issue was created |
| `--due_date` | The due date |
| `--description` | The description of an issue. Limited to 1,048,576 characters |
| `--assignee_id` | The ID of the user to assign the issue to. Only appears on GitLab Free |
| `--assignee_ids` | The IDs of the users to assign the issue to |
| `--discussion_to_resolve` | The ID of a discussion to resolve |
| `--epic_id` | ID of the epic to add the issue to. Valid values are greater than or equal to 0 |
| `--epic_iid` | IID of the epic to add the issue to. Valid values are greater than or equal to 0 |
| `--labels` | Comma-separated label names for an issue |
| `--merge_request_to_resolve_discussions_of` | The IID of a merge request in which to resolve all issues |
| `--milestone_id` | The global ID of a milestone to assign issue |
| `--weight` | The weight of the issue. Valid values are greater than or equal to 0 |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gl issue edit

Edit repo issue


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gl issue edit|ed [OPTIONS] [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |

| `--description` | The description of an issue. Limited to 1,048,576 characters |
| `--due_date` | The due date |
| `--epic_id` | ID of the epic to add the issue to. Valid values are greater than or equal to 0 |
| `--epic_iid` | IID of the epic to add the issue to. Valid values are greater than or equal to 0 |
| `--labels` | Comma-separated label names for an issue |
| `--milestone_id` | The global ID of a milestone to assign issue |
| `--remove_labels` | Comma-separated label names to remove from an issue |
| `--title` | The title of an issue |
| `--updated_at` | When the issue was updated |
| `--weight` | The weight of the issue. Valid values are greater than or equal to 0 |
| `--discussion_locked` | Flag indicating if the issue discussion is locked If the discussion is locked only project members can add or edit comments |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |

### x gl mr ls

List repo merge requests


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gl mr ls [OPTIONS] [FLAGS]
```

- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--state` |  | Return all merge requests or just those that are opened, closed, locked, or merged |
| `--sort` &lt;asc/desc&gt; |  | Sort by asc or desc |
| `--order_by` |  | Return requests ordered by created_at or updated_at fields |
| `--scope` &lt;val&gt; |  | Return merge requests for the given scope |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; or .id=&lt;repo_id&gt; |
| `--labels` | Return merge requests matching a comma-separated list of labels |
| `--milestone` | Return merge requests for a specific milestone |
| `--search` | Search merge requests against their title and description |
| `--target_branch` | Return merge requests with the given target branch |
| `--source_branch` | Return merge requests with the given source branch |
| `--author_id` | Return merge requests created by the given user id |
| `--assignee_id` | Returns merge requests assigned to the specific user id |
| `--approver_ids` | Returns merge requests which have specified all the users with the given id as individual approvers |
| `--author_username` | Return merge requests created by the given username |
| `--page` | target page |
| `--per_page` | per page data number |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gl mr create

- **Examples**:

In the &lt;owner/repo&gt; repo,Create merge request titled &lt;title&gt; from &lt;source_branch&gt; branch to &lt;target_branch&gt; branch

```sh

```

```sh

```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |

| `--title` | Title of merge requests |
| `--source_branch` | Source branch of merge request |
| `--target_branch` | Target branch of merge request |
| `--labels` | Labels for the merge request |
| `--squash` | Squash commits into a singcodee commit when merging |
| `--description` | Description of the merge request |
| `--assignee_id` | The user ID to assign the merge request |
| `--assignee_ids` | The users ID to assign the merge request,Set to 0 or provide an empty value to unassign all assignees |
| `--milestone_id` | The milestone ID |
| `--allow_collaboration` | Allow commits from members who can merge to the target branch |
| `--allow_maintainer_to_push` | Alias of allow_collaboration |
| `--approvals_before_merge` | Number of approvals required before this can be merged |
| `--remove_source_branch` | Flag indicating if a merge request should remove the source branch when merging |
| `--target_project_id` | The target repo |
| `--reviewer_ids` | The ID of the users added as a reviewer to the merge request |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |

| [x gl repo mr merge](#x-gl-repo-mr-merge) | Merge repo merge requests |
| [x gl repo mr rm](#x-gl-repo-mr-rm) | Remove repo merge requests |
| [x gl repo mr info](#x-gl-repo-mr-info) | Get repo merge requests information |


### x gl repo mr ls

List repo merge requests


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gl repo mr|pr ls [OPTIONS] [FLAGS]
```

- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--state` |  | Return all merge requests or just those that are opened, closed, locked, or merged |
| `--sort` &lt;asc/desc&gt; |  | Sort by asc or desc |
| `--order_by` |  | Return requests ordered by created_at or updated_at fields |
| `--scope` &lt;val&gt; |  | Return merge requests for the given scope |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; or .id=&lt;repo_id&gt; |
| `--labels` | Return merge requests matching a comma-separated list of labels |
| `--milestone` | Return merge requests for a specific milestone |
| `--search` | Search merge requests against their title and description |
| `--target_branch` | Return merge requests with the given target branch |
| `--source_branch` | Return merge requests with the given source branch |
| `--author_id` | Return merge requests created by the given user id |
| `--assignee_id` | Returns merge requests assigned to the specific user id |
| `--approver_ids` | Returns merge requests which have specified all the users with the given id as individual approvers |
| `--author_username` | Return merge requests created by the given username |
| `--page` | target page |
| `--per_page` | per page data number |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gl repo mr create

Create repo merge requests


- **Examples**:

In the &lt;owner/repo&gt; repo,Create merge request titled &lt;title&gt; from &lt;source_branch&gt; branch to &lt;target_branch&gt; branch

```sh
x gl repo mr create --repo <owner/repo> --source_branch <source_branch> --target_branch <target_branch> --title <title>
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gl repo mr|pr create [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; or .id=&lt;repo_id&gt; |
| `--title` | Title of merge requests |
| `--source_branch` | Source branch of merge request |
| `--target_branch` | Target branch of merge request |
| `--labels` | Labels for the merge request |
| `--squash` | Squash commits into a singcodee commit when merging |
| `--description` | Description of the merge request |
| `--assignee_id` | The user ID to assign the merge request |
| `--assignee_ids` | The users ID to assign the merge request,Set to 0 or provide an empty value to unassign all assignees |
| `--milestone_id` | The milestone ID |
| `--allow_collaboration` | Allow commits from members who can merge to the target branch |
| `--allow_maintainer_to_push` | Alias of allow_collaboration |
| `--approvals_before_merge` | Number of approvals required before this can be merged |
| `--remove_source_branch` | Flag indicating if a merge request should remove the source branch when merging |
| `--target_project_id` | The target repo |
| `--reviewer_ids` | The ID of the users added as a reviewer to the merge request |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |

### x gl repo mr merge

Merge repo merge requests


- **Examples**:

Merge the merge request with id 16533 in the &lt;owner/repo&gt; repo

```sh
x gl repo mr merge --repo <owner/repo> 16533
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gl repo mr|pr merge [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | merge request id |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; or .id=&lt;repo_id&gt; |
| `--sha` | if present, then this SHA must match the HEAD of the source branch, otherwise the merge will fail |
| `--merge_commit_message` | Custom merge commit message |
| `--squash_commit_message` | Custom squash commit message |
| `--squash` | If true, the commits are squashed into a singcodee commit on merge |
| `--merge_when_pipeline_succeeds` | If true, the merge request is merged when the pipeline succeeds |
| `--should_remove_source_branch` | If true, removes the source branch |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |

# Checking GPU load on macOS, no more switching back and forth

Checking GPU load on macOS is surprisingly hard — System Report only has hardware info, and Activity Monitor doesn't show GPU utilization. When running models or debugging graphics, you often want to know if the GPU is actually doing anything, but there's no single place to see both hardware info and current load.

`x gpu` combines hardware info and real-time load in one command.

## Quick Start

```bash
x gpu          # hardware info + real-time load
```

![x gpu](/image/mod/gpu.1_1.webp)

Subcommands for different needs:

- **`x gpu`**: hardware info + real-time load in one view, the most comprehensive
- **`x gpu info`**: hardware info only — GPU model, core count, Metal version and other static fields
- **`x gpu stat`**: real-time load only — GPU utilization and memory usage

## FAQ

### Q: What metrics does GPU utilization include?

`x gpu stat` outputs three dimensions of utilization: **GPU utilization** (overall compute load), **Renderer utilization** (render pipeline load), and **Tiler utilization** (vertex processing load). You need all three to fully assess GPU activity — looking at just one can be misleading.

### Q: Why does info show display information?

macOS's `system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType` reports GPU and display info together. `x gpu info` preserves this, making it easy to evaluate the machine's full graphics capability in one command — GPU specs, Metal capabilities, and connected displays.

### Q: How do Metal capability fields relate to actual performance?

`raytracing: True` means the hardware supports ray tracing acceleration, but actual performance depends on the GPU model — M1 ray tracing performance is far below M3. These fields are better used to **determine feature availability** (can it run) rather than evaluate performance (how fast). For performance assessment, use `x gpu stat` real-time utilization.

### Q: Why can't I read utilization data for NVIDIA GPUs on Linux?

`x gpu stat` reads `gpu_busy_percent` and `mem_busy_percent` from `/sys/class/drm/card*/device/` on Linux, with zero dependencies. However, NVIDIA's proprietary driver (`nvidia` kernel module) **does not expose full utilization data through the DRM subsystem** — `/sys/class/drm/` may not have corresponding entries or data may be empty.

### Q: What's the difference between integrated and discrete GPU data on dual-GPU laptops?

Linux laptops commonly have an integrated GPU (Intel/AMD) + discrete GPU (NVIDIA) configuration. `x gpu` lists all GPU devices under `/sys/class/drm/`, but note:

- Integrated GPU utilization data is typically complete and available
- Discrete GPU utilization data depends on the driver type
- After switching the active GPU (e.g. using `prime-run` or `optimus-manager`), use `x gpu info --fresh` to force refresh the cache

# `x gram` - Install an "Emergency Brake" for AI, Building the Final Security Barrier for Developers

As AI Agent penetration in development environments continues to increase, we are facing unprecedented security challenges.

::: danger
Imagine this nightmare scenario:
- 7x24 hour uninterrupted background processes
- Capable of self-replication and wake-up
- Unrestricted network access permissions
- System-level tool invocation permissions
:::

While we hope events like "moltbook" remain just hype, open-source models with safety restrictions removed (such as the dolphin series) already exist. **While enjoying the convenience brought by AI, we must prepare for the worst-case scenario.**

`x gram` is such a "last resort" tool—when agents behave abnormally, lose control, or even show signs of self-replication, it can forcefully terminate related processes and safely handle sensitive data.

## Level 0: Daily Control and Quick Cleanup

Suitable for environment reset after development work ends, preventing background residues.

```bash
# Terminate all known agent processes
x gram stop 0
```

> **Scope:** One-click kill mainstream agents like OpenClaw, Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, Devin and their derived network request processes.

## Level 1: Deep Cleanup (Including Runtimes)

When agents start "messing around" through scripting languages, you need to kill not just the Agent but also the tools it invokes.

```bash
# Terminate Python, Node.js, Deno and other runtimes simultaneously
x gram stop 1
```

> **Scope:** Ensure related interpreter processes are completely terminated, preventing residual scripts from continuing to run in the background.

## Level 2: Network Isolation (Pull the Plug)

Prevent malicious agents from "calling for help" through the network or uploading your local privacy.

```bash
# Cut off all processes connecting to ports 80/443
x gram stop 2
```

> **Scope:** Physical-level disconnection of HTTP/HTTPS connections, achieving complete network-level isolation.

## Level 8+: Memory Data "Safe House"

When performing higher-level cleanup (Level 8+), `x gram stop` refuses crude deletion. We adopt a **"isolate first, cleanup later"** strategy:

::::ol
:::li Automatic Identification
Locate agent memory files (such as `soul.md`, `memory.md`)
:::

:::li Safe Archiving
Package and move to `~/.x-cmd.gram/` isolation zone
:::

:::li Thorough Cleanup
Shred sensitive data at the original location
:::

:::li Permission Lockdown
Restrict access permissions to archived files
:::
::::

```bash
# Cleanup all agent memories in user directory
x gram stop 8

# System-level thorough cleanup (high-risk operation, use with caution)
x gram stop 9
```

## FAQ

### Q1: Why do I need this tool?

::: tip
Like preparing a fire extinguisher for a fire. Although large-scale AI shīkòng (失控 / AI out of control) has not yet broken out, the speed of technological evolution requires us to prepare for a rainy day. `x gram stop` is an emergency response tool specifically designed for AI safety.
:::

### Q2: Will this harm my normal development?

::: warning
This tool is positioned as a "last resort". In normal development workflows, you should rely on permission management; only use this tool when suspecting agent anomalies or needing to completely reset the environment.
:::

### Q3: How to recover isolated data?

Data is safe, just locked up.

```bash
# View isolation zone
ls ~/.x-cmd.gram/

# Restore access permissions (operate after confirming file safety)
chmod +r ~/.x-cmd.gram/[archive_file].tar
```

## Conclusion

> **We are not against AI development. X-CMD itself is committed to promoting command-line AIization.**

But while enjoying the benefits of technology, maintaining necessary vigilance and holding the right to "emergency brake" is the performance of every developer being responsible for themselves and their systems.

::: info
In this era of rapid AI advancement (kuángbēn (狂奔) / AI advancing wildly), let us both look up at the stars and hold tight the reins in our hands.
:::

# x gt cl

shortcut for `x gt repo clone`

## Usage

```sh
x gt cl|clone [OPTIONS] [FLAGS] <#1> <#2>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `#2` | directory |


## Options

| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `-o`, `--origin` &lt;name&gt; |  | use &lt;name&gt; instead of 'origin' to track upstream |
| `-b`, `--branch` &lt;branch&gt; |  | checkout &lt;branch&gt; instead of the remote's HEAD |
| `-u`, `--upload-pack` &lt;path&gt; |  | path to git-upload-pack on the remote |
| `-j`, `--jobs` &lt;n&gt; |  | number of submodules cloned in parallel |
| `--separate-git-dir` &lt;gitdir&gt; |  | separate git dir from working tree |
| `--depth` &lt;depth&gt; |  | create a shallow clone of that depth |


## Flags

| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--recursive` | initialize all contained submodules |
| `--shallow-submodules` | any cloned submodules will be shallow |

# x gt codeurl

Get Gitee source url


## Usage


## Arguments

# x gt issue

issue management

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x gt issue ls](#x-gt-issue-ls) | List issue |
| [x gt issue info](#x-gt-issue-info) | Get issue info |
| [x gt issue create](#x-gt-issue-create) | Create issue |
| [x gt issue edit](#x-gt-issue-edit) | Edit issue |


### x gt issue ls

List issue by owner



`x gt issue ls` is multi-command merge sugar to conveniently use
* `x gt user issue`
* `x gt repo issue ls`
* `x gt enterprise issue ls`

If you need more control options or using in script, Please use them


- **Examples**:

List current user issues

```sh
x gt issue ls
```

List &lt;owner/repo&gt; repo issues

```sh
x gt issue ls <owner/repo>
```

List &lt;enterprise_address&gt; enterprise issues

```sh
x gt issue ls <enterprise_address>
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt issue ls [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | owner path(enterprise&#124;owner/repo) [optional: use current user] |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--direction` &lt;asc,desc&gt; | sort direction |
| `--state` &lt;open,progressing,closed,rejected&gt; | issue state |
| `--labels` &lt;label(separator ,)&gt; | labels filter |
| `--page` &lt;num&gt; | target page |
| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; | per_page data number |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gt issue info

Get issue info



`x gt issue info` is multi-command merge sugar to conveniently use
* `x gt repo issue info`
* `x gt enterprise issue info`

If you need more control options or using in script, Please use them


- **Examples**:

Get &lt;issue_number&gt; issue information from &lt;owner&gt;/&lt;repo&gt; repo

```sh
x gt issue info --owner <owner>/<repo> <issue_number>
```

Get &lt;issue_number&gt; issue information from &lt;owner&gt;/&lt;repo&gt; repo

```sh
x gt issue info <owner>/<repo>/<issue_number>
```

Get &lt;issue_number&gt; issue information from &lt;enterprise_address&gt; enterprise

```sh
x gt issue info --owner <enterprise_address> <issue_number>
```

Get &lt;issue_number&gt; issue information from &lt;enterprise_address&gt; enterprise

```sh
x gt issue info <enterprise_address>/<issue_number>
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt issue info [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | issue number(Case sensitive.Not with #) |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--owner` &lt;owner_path&gt; | owner path(repo path or enterprise) |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gt issue create

Create issue


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt issue create [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--owner` &lt;path&gt; | Provide owner name(enterprise,ownerPath/RepoPath) |
| `--title` &lt;title&gt; | issue title |
| `--body` &lt;str&gt; | issue describe (support markdown) |
| `--type` &lt;issue_type&gt; | custom issue type |
| `--assignee` &lt;user_login&gt; | issue assignee |
| `--collaborators` &lt;user_login(separator ,)&gt; | issue collaborators |
| `--milestone` &lt;id&gt; | milestone ID |

| `--program` &lt;id&gt; | project ID |
| `--security` | Mark private issue |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |

# x gt notification

notification management

| ------- | ------- |

| [x gt notification ll](#x-gt-notification-ll) | List all notification with terminal table |
| [x gt notification info](#x-gt-notification-info) | Show notification detail information |
| [x gt notification mark](#x-gt-notification-mark) | Mark notifications as read |


### x gt notification ls

List all notification with interactive UI


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt notification|n ls [OPTIONS] [FLAGS]
```

- **Options**:


| Name, Shorthand | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ------- |
| `--unread` |  | Only get unread messages (default as true) |
| `--participating` |  | shows notifications in which the user is directly participating or mentioned (default as false) |
| `--type` |  | Filter notifications of specified types (default as all) |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--since` &lt;ISO 8601&gt; | show results that were last updated after the given time |
| `--before` &lt;ISO 8601&gt; | show notifications updated before the given time |
| `--ids` | Specify a set of notification IDs separated by ',' |
| `--page` &lt;num&gt; | target page |
| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; | per_page data number |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |
| `--csv` | output csv data |
| `--yml` | output yml data |

- **Usage**:

| `--participating` |  | shows notifications in which the user is directly participating or mentioned (default as false) |
| `--type` |  | Filter notifications of specified types (default as all) |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--since` &lt;ISO 8601&gt; | show results that were last updated after the given time |
| `--before` &lt;ISO 8601&gt; | show notifications updated before the given time |
| `--ids` | Specify a set of notification IDs separated by ',' |
| `--page` &lt;num&gt; | target page |
| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; | per_page data number |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |

# x gt org

## Examples

List all organizations for the user

```sh
x gt org ls
```

Add the &lt;user&gt; member to the &lt;org&gt; and grant them admin privileges

```sh
x gt org membership add --org <org> --role admin <user>
```

List all public repositories under an organization with interactive UI

```sh
x gt org repo ls --type public x-cmd
```

Create &lt;repo_name&gt; repo on &lt;org_path&gt; organization

```sh
x gt org repo create <org_path>/<repo_name>
```

View closed issues with the label "bug" in the x-cmd organization

```sh
x gt org issue --labels bug --state closed --org x-cmd
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x gt org ls](#x-gt-org-ls) | List all organizations |
| [x gt org info](#x-gt-org-info) | Show org information |
| [x gt org create](#x-gt-org-create) | Create org |
| [x gt org membership](#x-gt-org-membership) | org membership management |
| [x gt org repo](#x-gt-org-repo) | org repo management |
| [x gt org issue](#x-gt-org-issue) | List organization issue |
| [x gt org apply](#x-gt-org-apply) | Manage org by declare configure |


### x gt org ls

List all organizations


- **Examples**:

List all organizations for the user

```sh
x gt org ls
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt org ls [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--page` &lt;num&gt; | target page |
| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; | per_page data number |
| `--admin` | List only authorized users managed org |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |
| `--csv` | output csv data |
| `--yml` | output yml data |


### x gt org info

Show org information


- **Examples**:

View the information about the x-cmd organization

```sh

```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt org info [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | organization path |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--json`, `-j` | Output raw JSON data |


| Name | Description |

| [x gt org membership edit](#x-gt-org-membership-edit) | Update org membership role |
| [x gt org membership rm](#x-gt-org-membership-rm) | Remove org membership |

| Name, Shorthand | Description |

| `--role` &lt;all,member,admin"&gt; | member role filter |
| `--page` &lt;num&gt; | target page |
| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; | per_page data number |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |
| `--csv` | output csv data |
| `--yml` | output yml data |

### x gt org repo create

Create origanization repo


- **Examples**:

Create &lt;repo_name&gt; repo on &lt;org_path&gt; origanization

```sh
x gt org repo create <org_path>/<repo_name>
```

Create &lt;repo_name&gt; repo on &lt;org_path&gt; origanization

```sh
x gt org repo create --org <org_path> <repo_name>
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt org repo create [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | repo name |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--org` &lt;org_path&gt; | organization space path |
| `--access` &lt;private,public&gt; | repo access |
| `-p`, `--path` &lt;path&gt; | repo path |
| `--description` &lt;desc&gt; | repo description |
| `--homepage` &lt;url&gt; | repo homepage |
| `--gitignore_template` &lt;template_name&gt; | Git Ignore template |
| `--license_template` &lt;license_name&gt; | License template |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |
| `--no_issue` | Ban repo issue |
| `--no_wiki` | Ban repo wiki |
| `--no_comment` | Ban repo comment |
| `--auto_init` | Initialize the repository with README |


### x gt org repo edit

Edit origanization repo configure


- **Examples**:

Change the x-cmd repository to a private repository

```sh
x gt org repo edit --access private x-cmd/x-cmd
```

Rename the repository "x-cmd" to "myrepo"

```sh
x gt org repo edit --name myrepo x-cmd/x-cmd
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt org repo edit|ed [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--name` &lt;rename&gt; | repo rename |
| `--access` &lt;private,public&gt; | repo access |
| `-p`, `--path` &lt;path&gt; | repo path |
| `--description` &lt;desc&gt; | repo description |
| `--homepage` &lt;url&gt; | repo homepage |
| `--default_branch` &lt;branch_name&gt; | repo default branch |
| `--default_merge_method` &lt;way&gt; | repo default merge PR way |
| `--no_issue` | Ban repo issue |
| `--no_wiki` | Ban repo wiki |
| `--no_comment` | Ban repo comment |
| `--no_security_hole` | Ban repo issue public access |
| `--no_pull_requests` | Ban repo pull request |
| `--no_online_edit` | Ban repo online edit |
| `--no_lightweight_pr` | Ban repo lightweight pr |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Ignore edit access private prompt interception |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gt org issue

List organization issue


- **Examples**:

List the issues in the x-cmd organization

```sh
x gt org issue --org x-cmd
```

View closed issues with the label "bug" in the x-cmd organization

```sh
x gt org issue --labels bug --state closed --org x-cmd
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt org issue [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--org` &lt;org_path&gt; | organization path |
| `--direction` &lt;asc,desc&gt; | sort direction |
| `--sort` &lt;created,updated&gt; | sort way |
| `--state` &lt;open,progressing,closed,rejected&gt; | issue state |
| `--filter` &lt;assigned,created,all&gt; | issue filter |
| `--labels` &lt;label(separator ,)&gt; | labels filter |
| `--page` &lt;num&gt; | target page |
| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; | per_page data number |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gt org apply

Manage org by declare configure


- **Examples**:

Use org.yml declare configure manage org

```sh
x gt org apply ./org.yml
```

Use org.yml declare configure manage org, And alias configure's user 'bot' to 'x-cmd-bot'

```sh
x gt org apply ./org.yml bot=x-cmd-bot
```

Use stdin declare configure data manage org

```sh
cat ./org.yml | x gt org apply -
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt org apply <#1> <#n>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | declare file path(yml, json), stdin '-' |
| `#n` | alias name list |

# x gt pr

pull request management

## Examples

List &lt;owner/repo&gt; state is open PR

```sh
x gt pr ls --repo <owner/repo>
```

pass review, pass test, Squash Merge &lt;pr_number&gt; PR on &lt;owner/repo&gt;

```sh
x gt pr assign review --repo <owner/repo> <pr_number>
x gt pr tester test --repo <owner/repo> <pr_number>
x gt pr merge --repo <owner/repo> --merge_method squash <pr_number>

```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x gt pr set](#x-gt-pr-set) | Setup repo review and tester repo configure |
| [x gt pr ls](#x-gt-pr-ls) | List pull request |
| [x gt pr create](#x-gt-pr-create) | Create pull request |
| [x gt pr edit](#x-gt-pr-edit) | Edit pull request |
| [x gt pr info](#x-gt-pr-info) | Show pull request info |
| [x gt pr log](#x-gt-pr-log) | List pull request log |
| [x gt pr commit](#x-gt-pr-commit) | List pull request commit message |
| [x gt pr browse](#x-gt-pr-browse) | Open pull request in browser |
| [x gt pr merge](#x-gt-pr-merge) | Merge pull request |
| [x gt pr assign](#x-gt-pr-assign) | repo pull request assigner management |
| [x gt pr tester](#x-gt-pr-tester) | repo pull request tester management |


### x gt pr set

Setup repo review and tester repo configure


- **Examples**:

Setting x-foo and x-bar as assignees and testers for &lt;owner/repo&gt; repo

```sh
x gt repo pr set --repo <owner/repo> --assignees "x-foo,x-bar" --testers "x-foo,x-bar"
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt pr set [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--assignees` &lt;userlist(separator ,)&gt; | assignees username list |
| `--testers` &lt;userlist(separator ,)&gt; | testers usrename list |
| `--assignees_number` &lt;num&gt; | number of reviewers |
| `--testers_number` &lt;num&gt; | number of tester |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gt pr ls

List pull request


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt pr ls [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--state` &lt;open,merged,closed,all&gt; | pr state |
| `--head` &lt;branch&gt; | source branch |
| `--base` &lt;branch&gt; | target branch |
| `--since` &lt;ISO 8601&gt; | since update date |
| `--sort` &lt;created,updated...&gt; | sort way |
| `--direction` &lt;desc,asc&gt; | sort direction |
| `--milestone_number` &lt;id&gt; | milestone id |
| `--labels` &lt;labels(separator ,)&gt; | filter by labels |
| `--page` &lt;num&gt; | target page |
| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; | per_page data number |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |
| `--csv` | output csv data |
| `--yml` | output yml data |


### x gt pr create

Create pull request


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt pr create [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--title` &lt;title&gt; | pull request title |
| `--head` &lt;branch&gt; | source branch |
| `--base` &lt;branch&gt; | target branch |
| `--body` &lt;content&gt; | pull request content |
| `--milestone_number` &lt;id&gt; | milestone id |
| `--labels` &lt;labels(separator ,)&gt; | labels |
| `--issue` &lt;issue_id&gt; | related issue id |
| `--assignees` &lt;userlist(separator ,)&gt; | assignees username list |
| `--testers` &lt;userlist(separator ,)&gt; | testers usrename list |
| `--assignees_number` &lt;num&gt; | number of reviewers |
| `--testers_number` &lt;num&gt; | number of tester |
| `--close_related_issue` | close related issue after merge |
| `--prune_source_branch` | delete source branch after merge |
| `--draft` | set pr as draft |
| `--squash` | use squash merge PR |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |

### x gt pr assign review

- **Usage**:


- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |

| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; | per_page data number |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |
| `--csv` | output csv data |
| `--yml` | output yml data |

# x gt repo hook

repo webhooks management

## Examples

Setting default push webhooks for &lt;owner/repo&gt; repo

```sh
x gt repo hook create --repo <owner/repo> --url <remote url>
```

Only Setting issue webhooks for &lt;owner/repo&gt; repo

```sh
x gt repo hook create --repo <owner/repo> --url <remote url> --no_push_events --issues_events
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x gt repo hook ls](#x-gt-repo-hook-ls) | List repo webhook |
| [x gt repo hook create](#x-gt-repo-hook-create) | Create repo webhook |
| [x gt repo hook info](#x-gt-repo-hook-info) | Show repo webhook detailed information |
| [x gt repo hook edit](#x-gt-repo-hook-edit) | Edit repo webhook configure |
| [x gt repo hook rm](#x-gt-repo-hook-rm) | Remove repo webhook |
| [x gt repo hook test](#x-gt-repo-hook-test) | Try repo webhook url test connect |


### x gt repo hook ls

List repo webhook


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo hook ls [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--page` &lt;num&gt; | target page |
| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; | per_page data number |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |
| `--csv` | output csv data |
| `--yml` | output yml data |


### x gt repo hook create

Create repo webhook


- **Examples**:

Setting default push webhooks for &lt;owner/repo&gt; repo

```sh
x gt repo hook create --repo <owner/repo> --url <remote url>
```

Only Setting issue webhooks for &lt;owner/repo&gt; repo

```sh
x gt repo hook create --repo <owner/repo> --url <remote url> --no_push_events --issues_events
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo hook create [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--url` &lt;url&gt; | remote HTTP URL |
| `--encryption_type` &lt;password,signkey&gt; | encryption type |
| `--password` &lt;password&gt; | Requesting a URL with password to prevent maliciously request |
| `--no_push_events` | Turn off push code event(default is push code event) |
| `--tag_push_events` | Turn on push tag event |
| `--issues_events` | Turn on create&#124;close issue event |
| `--note_events` | Turn on comment code&#124;issue note event |
| `--merge_requests_events` | Turn on merge request&#124;merged event |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gt repo hook info

Show repo webhook detailed information


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo hook info [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | webhooks ID (obtain by `x gt repo hook ls`) |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gt repo hook edit

Edit repo webhook configure


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo hook edit|ed [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | webhooks ID (obtain by `x gt repo hook ls`) |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--url` &lt;url&gt; | remote HTTP URL |
| `--encryption_type` &lt;password,signkey&gt; | encryption type |
| `--password` &lt;password&gt; | Requesting a URL with password to prevent maliciously request |
| `--no_push_events` | Turn off push code event(default is push code event) |
| `--tag_push_events` | Turn on push tag event |
| `--issues_events` | Turn on create&#124;close issue event |
| `--note_events` | Turn on comment code&#124;issue note event |
| `--merge_requests_events` | Turn on merge request&#124;merged event |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |

Remove repo webhook

```sh

```

repo pages management

| ------- | ------- |

### x gt repo page info

Output repo pages information


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo page info [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |

| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |

# x gt repo pr

repo pull request management

## Examples

List &lt;owner/repo&gt; state is open PR

```sh
x gt repo pr ls --repo <owner/repo>
```

pass review, pass test, Squash Merge &lt;pr_number&gt; PR on &lt;owner/repo&gt;

```sh
x gt repo pr assign review --repo <owner/repo> <pr_number>
x gt repo pr tester test --repo <owner/repo> <pr_number>
x gt repo pr merge --repo <owner/repo> --merge_method squash <pr_number>

```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x gt repo pr set](#x-gt-repo-pr-set) | Setup repo review and tester repo configure |
| [x gt repo pr ls](#x-gt-repo-pr-ls) | List pull requests |
| [x gt repo pr create](#x-gt-repo-pr-create) | Create pull request |
| [x gt repo pr edit](#x-gt-repo-pr-edit) | Edit pull request |
| [x gt repo pr info](#x-gt-repo-pr-info) | Show pull request info |
| [x gt repo pr log](#x-gt-repo-pr-log) | List pull request log |
| [x gt repo pr commit](#x-gt-repo-pr-commit) | List pull request commit message |
| [x gt repo pr web](#x-gt-repo-pr-web) | Open pull request in browser |
| [x gt repo pr merge](#x-gt-repo-pr-merge) | Merge pull request |
| [x gt repo pr assign](#x-gt-repo-pr-assign) | repo pull request assigner management |
| [x gt repo pr tester](#x-gt-repo-pr-tester) | repo pull request tester management |


### x gt repo pr set

Setup repo review and tester repo configure


- **Examples**:

Setting x-foo and x-bar as assignees and testers for &lt;owner/repo&gt; repo

```sh
x gt repo pr set --repo <owner/repo> --assignees "x-foo,x-bar" --testers "x-foo,x-bar"
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo pr set [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--assignees` &lt;userlist(separator ,)&gt; | assignees username list |
| `--testers` &lt;userlist(separator ,)&gt; | testers usrename list |
| `--assignees_number` &lt;num&gt; | number of reviewers |
| `--testers_number` &lt;num&gt; | number of tester |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gt repo pr ls

List pull requests


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo pr ls [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--state` &lt;open,merged,closed,all&gt; | pull request state |
| `--head` &lt;branch&gt; | source branch |
| `--base` &lt;branch&gt; | target branch |
| `--since` &lt;ISO 8601&gt; | since update date |
| `--sort` &lt;created,updated...&gt; | sort way |
| `--direction` &lt;desc,asc&gt; | sort direction |
| `--milestone_number` &lt;id&gt; | milestone id |
| `--labels` &lt;labels(separator ,)&gt; | filter by labels |
| `--page` &lt;num&gt; | target page |
| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; | per_page data number |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gt repo pr create

Create pull request


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo pr create [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--title` &lt;title&gt; | pull request title |
| `--head` &lt;branch&gt; | source branch |
| `--base` &lt;branch&gt; | target branch |
| `--body` &lt;content&gt; | pull request content |
| `--milestone_number` &lt;id&gt; | milestone id |
| `--labels` &lt;labels(separator ,)&gt; | labels |
| `--issue` &lt;issue_id&gt; | related issue id |
| `--assignees` &lt;userlist(separator ,)&gt; | assignees username list |
| `--testers` &lt;userlist(separator ,)&gt; | testers usrename list |
| `--assignees_number` &lt;num&gt; | number of reviewers |
| `--testers_number` &lt;num&gt; | number of tester |
| `--close_related_issue` | close related issue after merge |
| `--prune_source_branch` | delete source branch after merge |
| `--draft` | set pr as draft |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |

| `--body` &lt;content&gt; | pull request content |

# x gt repo push

repo push rule management

## Examples

Setting and turn on push rule that only allow email suffix is '@x-cmd.com'

```sh
x gt repo push set --repo <owner/repo> --restrict_author_email_suffix --author_email_suffix "@x-cmd.com"
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x gt repo push set](#x-gt-repo-push-set) | Setting repo push rule configure |
| [x gt repo push info](#x-gt-repo-push-info) | Get repo push rule info |


### x gt repo push set

Setting repo push rule configure


- **Examples**:

Setting and turn on push rule that only allow email suffix is '@x-cmd.com'

```sh
x gt repo push set --repo <owner/repo> --restrict_author_email_suffix --author_email_suffix "@x-cmd.com"
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo push set [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--author_email_suffix` &lt;email_suffix&gt; | Setting push email suffix |
| `--commit_message_regex` &lt;regex&gt; | Setting commit message regex |
| `--max_file_size` &lt;size&gt; | Limit single file size(MB, &lt;=100MB) |
| `--restrict_push_own_commit` | Only push your own commits by owner email |
| `--restrict_author_email_suffix` | Turn on only support email suffix push |
| `--restrict_commit_message` | Turn on commit message regex check |
| `--restrict_file_size` | Turn on single file size check |
| `--except_manager` | Turn on repo admin ignore all check |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gt repo push info

Get repo push rule info


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo push info [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |

# x gt repo release

repo release management

## Examples

List all released versions of x-cmd/x-cmd repository

```sh
x gt repo release ls -r x-cmd/x-cmd
```

Create release name as v1.1.0 release desc as '# v1.1.0' to main branch on x-cmd/x-cmd

```sh
x gt repo release create --repo x-cmd/x-cmd --tag v1.1.0 --target_commitish test --body "# v1.1.0"
```

Upload a file as an attachment to a release of x-cmd/x-cmd repo

```sh
x gt repo release attachment upload --repo x-cmd/x-cmd --release_id <release_id> <file_path>
```

List all attachments of a release of x-cmd/x-cmd repo

```sh
x gt repo release attachment ls --repo x-cmd/x-cmd --release_id <release_id>
```

## Sub Commands

| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x gt repo release ls](#x-gt-repo-release-ls) | List repo release |
| [x gt repo release create](#x-gt-repo-release-create) | Create repo release |
| [x gt repo release info](#x-gt-repo-release-info) | Show detailed information of repo |
| [x gt repo release edit](#x-gt-repo-release-edit) | Update release information |
| [x gt repo release rm](#x-gt-repo-release-rm) | Remove repo release |
| [x gt repo release latest](#x-gt-repo-release-latest) | Show latest release |
| [x gt repo release attachment](#x-gt-repo-release-attachment) | repo release attachment management |


### x gt repo release ls

List repo release


- **Examples**:

List all released versions of x-cmd/x-cmd repository

```sh
x gt repo release ls -r x-cmd/x-cmd
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo release ls [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--direction` &lt;asc,desc&gt; | list direction |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |
| `--csv` | output csv data |
| `--yml` | output yml data |


### x gt repo release create

Create repo release


- **Examples**:

Create release name as v1.1.0 release desc as '# v1.1.0' to main branch on x-cmd/x-cmd

```sh
x gt repo release create -r x-cmd/x-cmd --tag v1.1.0 --target_commitish test --body "# v1.1.0"
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo release create [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--tag` &lt;tag_name&gt; | Please provide tag name |
| `--body` &lt;body_msg&gt; | Release Description(support markdown) |
| `--target_commitish` &lt;branch&#124;commit_SHA&gt; | branch name or commit SHA |
| `--name` &lt;release_name&gt; | Release name(default:tag name) |
| `--prerelease` | Mark pre-release version |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gt repo release info

Show detailed information of repo


- **Examples**:

Show the information for the release with ID &lt;release_id&gt; in the x-cmd/x-cmd repository

```sh
x gt repo release info -r x-cmd/x-cmd <release_id>
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo release info [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | Release ID (obtain by `x gt repo release ls`) |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gt repo release edit

Update release information


- **Examples**:

Edit the release with ID &lt;release_id&gt; as the pre-release version

```sh

```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo release edit|ed [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | Release ID (obtain by `x gt repo release ls`) |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--tag` &lt;tag_name&gt; | Please provide tag name |
| `--body` &lt;body_msg&gt; | Release Description(support markdown) |
| `--name` &lt;release_name&gt; | Release name |
| `--prerelease` | Mark pre-release version |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |

### x gt repo release attachment

repo release attachment management


- **Examples**:

Upload &lt;file_path&gt; as an attachment to release &lt;release_id&gt; of x-cmd/x-cmd repo

```sh
x gt repo release attachment upload --repo x-cmd/x-cmd --release_id <release_id> <file_path>
```

List all attachments of release &lt;release_id&gt; of x-cmd/x-cmd repo

```sh
x gt repo release attachment ls --repo x-cmd/x-cmd --release_id <release_id>
```

Remove attachment &lt;attachment_id&gt; from release &lt;release_id&gt; of x-cmd/x-cmd repo

```sh
x gt repo release attachment rm --repo x-cmd/x-cmd --release_id <release_id> -y <attachment_id>
```

- **Sub Commands**:


| Name | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| [x gt repo release attachment ls](#x-gt-repo-release-attachment-ls) | List release attachments |
| [x gt repo release attachment info](#x-gt-repo-release-attachment-info) | Get release attachment information |
| [x gt repo release attachment upload](#x-gt-repo-release-attachment-upload) | Upload file as release attachment |
| [x gt repo release attachment download](#x-gt-repo-release-attachment-download) | Download release attachment |
| [x gt repo release attachment rm](#x-gt-repo-release-attachment-rm) | Remove release attachment |


### x gt repo release attachment ls

List release attachments


- **Examples**:

List all attachments of release &lt;release_id&gt; of x-cmd/x-cmd repo

```sh
x gt repo release attachment ls --repo x-cmd/x-cmd --release_id <release_id>
```

Output the attachments list of release &lt;release_id&gt; as raw JSON

```sh
x gt repo release attachment ls --repo x-cmd/x-cmd --release_id <release_id> --json
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo release attachment|asset ls [FLAGS]
```

- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--release_id` &lt;num&gt; | Release ID (obtain by `x gt repo release ls`) |
| `--direction` &lt;asc,desc&gt; | list direction (default: asc) |
| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; | per_page data number |
| `--page` &lt;num&gt; | target page |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |
| `--csv` | output csv data |
| `--yml` | output yml data |


### x gt repo release attachment info

Get release attachment information


- **Examples**:

Show the information of attachment &lt;attachment_id&gt; on release &lt;release_id&gt; of x-cmd/x-cmd repo

```sh
x gt repo release attachment info --repo x-cmd/x-cmd --release_id <release_id> <attachment_id>
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo release attachment|asset info [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | Release Attachment ID (obtain by `x gt repo release attachment ls`) |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--release_id` &lt;num&gt; | Release ID (obtain by `x gt repo release ls`) |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gt repo release attachment upload

Upload file as release attachment



::: tip
Read the file from stdin by passing `-` as &lt;file_path&gt;. The attachment name defaults to the filename of the file path argument.
:::


- **Examples**:

Upload &lt;file_path&gt; as an attachment to release &lt;release_id&gt; of x-cmd/x-cmd repo

```sh
x gt repo release attachment upload --repo x-cmd/x-cmd --release_id <release_id> <file_path>
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo release attachment|asset upload [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | target upload attachment file path. Use `-` to read from stdin |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--release_id` &lt;num&gt; | Release ID (obtain by `x gt repo release ls`) |
| `--json`, `-j` | output raw JSON data |


### x gt repo release attachment download

Download release attachment


- **Examples**:

Download attachment &lt;attachment_id&gt; from release &lt;release_id&gt; of x-cmd/x-cmd repo to the current directory

```sh
x gt repo release attachment download --repo x-cmd/x-cmd --release_id <release_id> <attachment_id>
```

Download attachment &lt;attachment_id&gt; from release &lt;release_id&gt; of x-cmd/x-cmd repo into the ./dist directory

```sh
x gt repo release attachment download --repo x-cmd/x-cmd --release_id <release_id> --dir ./dist <attachment_id>
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo release attachment|asset download [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | Release Attachment ID (obtain by `x gt repo release attachment ls`) |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--release_id` &lt;num&gt; | Release ID (obtain by `x gt repo release ls`) |
| `--dir`, `-d` &lt;path&gt; | directory to save the downloaded file. Default: current directory |


### x gt repo release attachment rm

Remove release attachment


- **Examples**:

Remove attachment &lt;attachment_id&gt; from release &lt;release_id&gt; of x-cmd/x-cmd repo

```sh
x gt repo release attachment rm --repo x-cmd/x-cmd --release_id <release_id> -y <attachment_id>
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo release attachment|asset rm [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | Release Attachment ID (obtain by `x gt repo release attachment ls`) |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--repo`, `-r` &lt;owner/repo&gt; | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
| `--release_id` &lt;num&gt; | Release ID (obtain by `x gt repo release ls`) |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Ignore remove prompt interception |

### x gt repo ls

Interactive UI show repo by owner



`x gt repo ls` is multi-command merge sugar to conveniently use
* `x gt user repo ls`
* `x gt org repo ls`
* `x gt enterprise repo ls`



If you need more control options, Please use them


- **Examples**:

Interactive UI show current user repositories

```sh
x gt repo ls
```

Interactive UI show &lt;org_path&gt; repositories

```sh
x gt repo ls <org_path>
```

- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo ls [FLAGS] <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | &lt;ownerPath&gt; (default ownerPath: current user) |


- **Flags**:


| Name, Shorthand | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `--page` &lt;num&gt; | target page |
| `--per_page` &lt;num&gt; | per_page data number |


### x gt repo browse

Open repo in the web browser



::: tip Setting environment variables `BROWSER` can be specified to use a browser to open
`BROWSER = "open -a '/Applications/Google Chrome.app'"`
:::


- **Usage**:

```sh
x gt repo browse|b <#1>
```

- **Arguments**:


| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | &lt;owner_path&gt;/&lt;repo_path&gt; |
