# x zuz (1) - Multi-Format Compression and Extraction Tool

## Packaging Files or Directories into Archives

In daily use, we often need to package files or directories into archives. However, different compression formats require different tools, and the command formats of these tools are often inconsistent.

Therefore, `x-cmd` designed the `x zuz` module. It is a multi-format, cross-platform compression and extraction tool designed to let users no longer need to remember various commands for different compression formats—just use one simple command to easily complete all tasks.

`x z` is a shorthand for the `x zuz compress` command, used to package specified files or directories and generate archives in the specified format.

::: tip
Use the `x z` command for compression
:::

- For example, compress the `setup.log` file into `zip` format:

    ```sh
    x z log.zip setup.log
    ```

- For example, package the `setup.log` file and `bin/` directory together into `tar.gz` format:

    ```sh
    x z example.tar.gz setup.log bin/
    ```

<!-- [image] x z command packaging zip and tar.gz archives output -->
![x z](/image/mod/zuz.1_1.webp)

Whether it's a single file or multiple files and directories, the `x z` command automatically completes the corresponding compression task for you—no need to worry about which compression tool or command options to use. Just specify the target compression format and source files or directories.

## Viewing Supported Archive Formats

The `x zuz` module supports multiple compression formats, covering common compression and extraction needs. You can view currently supported compression and extraction formats with the following command:

```sh
x zuz show
```

<!-- [image] x zuz show command output -->
![x zuz show](/image/mod/zuz.1_2.webp)

:::: ul
::: li **Supported compression formats**

- `tar`, `tar.gz`, `tar.Z`, `tar.xz`, `tar.zst`
- `gz`, `bz2`, `xz`, `tgz`, `zst`, `zip`, `rar`, `7z`, `lha`, `lzh`

:::
::: li **Supported extraction formats**

- `tar`, `tar.gz`, `tar.Z`, `tar.xz`, `tar.zst`, `tbz`
- `gz`, `bz2`, `xz`, `tgz`, `zst`, `zip`, `rar`, `7z`, `lha`, `lzh`, `Z`

:::
::::

## Listing Archive Contents Without Extraction

To conveniently check archive contents, ensure file integrity, or quickly locate a specific file, the `x zuz` module supports listing files inside archives without extracting the entire package.

For example, list files in `log.zip` and `example.tar.gz` archives:

```sh
x zuz ls log.zip
x zuz ls example.tar.gz
```

<!-- [image] x zuz ls command output -->
![x zuz ls](/image/mod/zuz.1_3.webp)

---
[More] To learn more about the zuz module, visit x-cmd.com/mod/zuz

# x zuz (2) - Easily Decompress Various Archives

## Decompressing Archives to the Current Directory

`x uz` is shorthand for the `x zuz decompress` command, used to decompress archives to the current directory or a specified directory. This command allows users to easily decompress files without worrying about the specific format or decompression tool.

For example, to decompress a `zip` archive and extract its contents to the current directory:

```sh
x uz gh_2.67.0_windows_amd64.zip
```

<!-- [image] Showing the output of the x uz command decompressing to the current directory -->
![x uz 1](/image/mod/zuz.2_1.webp)

Regardless of the archive format, `x uz` will automatically select the appropriate decompression method based on the file extension.

## Decompressing Archives to a Specified Directory

`x uz` supports decompressing archives to a specified directory; simply provide the target directory path.

For example, to decompress a `zip` archive and extract its contents to the `./gh` directory:

```sh
x uz gh_2.67.0_windows_amd64.zip ./gh
```

<!-- [image] Showing the output of the x uz command decompressing to a specified directory -->
![x uz 2](/image/mod/zuz.2_2.webp)

If the `./gh` directory does not exist, `x uz` will automatically create it, ensuring that the files are correctly extracted to the specified location.

## Decompressing Archives and Deleting the Archive Afterwards

In some cases, users may want to automatically delete the archive after decompression to save disk space. The `x uzr` command (shorthand for `x zuz uzr`) can help achieve this.

For example, to decompress a `zip` archive and automatically delete it after decompression:

```sh
x uzr gh_2.67.0_windows_amd64.zip
```

<!-- [image] Showing the output of the x uzr command -->
![x uzr](/image/mod/zuz.2_3.webp)

This is particularly useful for handling large numbers of temporary archives or automated tasks, especially when dealing with large files or frequent decompression, as it can effectively save storage space.

---
[More] For more information about the zuz module, please visit the x-cmd website - x-cmd.com/mod/zuz

# x zuz z

Compress file

## Examples

Compress the specified file or folder into a specified format archive.

```sh
x z <file name>.<Compression format> <file or folder>
```

## Usage

```sh
x zuz z|compress <#1> <#n>
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| ------- | ------- |
| `#1` | The compressed file name and file format |
| `#n` | The destination files or folders that needs to be compressed |
